text: Friends, thank you from the bottom of my heart for your touching welcome with your warm presence.
rewrite: Friends, I am deeply grateful for your heartfelt welcome and the warmth of your presence.

text: Friends, with a strong PASOK on 21 May we are opening a new page for young people and new generations.
rewrite: Friends, a robust PASOK on May 21st marks the start of a fresh chapter for youth and new generations.

text: Thousands of accounts drinking water in your name and its executives, like someone here in Thessaly, trying to discredit a woman who had the courage to report abuse.
rewrite: Thousands of accounts are slandering you and your leaders, similar to someone in Thessaly attempting to undermine a woman brave enough to expose mistreatment.

text: Mr Mitsotakis, who promised an effective executive state but turned out to be a stooge of powerful economic interests, a champion of temporary employees and a champion of direct assignments.
rewrite: Mr Mitsotakis pledged an efficient administrative state but proved to be a puppet for influential economic groups, an advocate for temporary workers, and a proponent of direct appointments.

text: A country with strong institutions, with the rule of law, with the defence of human rights.
rewrite: "A nation with robust institutions, governed by the rule of law, and committed to upholding human rights."

text: Corresponding universal protection of agricultural property, in order to preserve the productive power of our farmers. Reform of bankruptcy law with an emphasis on the reorganisation and rescue of companies. Establishment of the right of option for borrowers to purchase their loan before it is transferred to funds.
rewrite: Universal safeguards for agricultural assets, aimed at maintaining the productive capacity of our farmers. Bankruptcy law reforms focused on corporate restructuring and rescue. Granting borrowers the option to buy back their loans prior to transfer to funds.

text: A Greece that will be a pillar of stability and peace throughout the Southeastern Mediterranean.
rewrite: "A Greece that stands as a bastion of stability and peace across the Southeastern Mediterranean."

text: So, in closing, I invite you to these last weeks, these last days left until the great battle of May 21. I expect nothing from the channels and from powerful economic interests.
rewrite: Thus, as we conclude, I urge you to embrace these final weeks, these remaining days leading up to the pivotal battle on May 21. I place no trust in media channels or influential economic interests.

text: Friends, our priority is also to tackle private debt, to protect the main house and to prevent the deflation of the Greek economy.
rewrite: Friends, our main focus is also to address private debt, safeguard the primary residence, and avert deflation in the Greek economy.

text: Therefore, immediate measures are needed to protect and support productive Greece, to reduce production costs, especially for agricultural supplies, animal feed and fuel, with zero excise duty on agricultural oil, as long as the energy crisis lasts.
rewrite: Thus, urgent actions are required to safeguard and assist productive Greece, to lower production expenses, particularly for agricultural inputs, animal feed, and fuel, by eliminating excise duty on agricultural oil for the duration of the energy crisis.

text: We do not forget the "Pinochet" for the democratically elected Prime Minister of the country.
rewrite: "We do not overlook the 'Pinochet' in relation to the nation's democratically elected Prime Minister."

text: For this, fight again. May 21 we are winners together. All together.
rewrite: Fight once more for this cause. On May 21, we will triumph as one. United, all of us.

text: Also the green transition. The green transition, for Mr Mitsotakis, is a business for the few.
rewrite: "Additionally, the green transition. For Mr. Mitsotakis, the green transition is an endeavor for the select few."

text: Only this party, in terms of values and democracy, has historically opposed the phenomenon of neo-Nazism in our country.
rewrite: This party alone has historically stood against neo-Nazism in our nation, both in its values and democratic principles.

text: We propose the creation of 50,000 full-time jobs for young unemployed people in the private sector with a 4-year subsidy of employer contributions.
rewrite: "We suggest establishing 50,000 full-time positions for unemployed youth in the private sector, supported by a four-year subsidy for employer contributions."

text: Isn't Mr Tsakalotos talking about local currencies in a European Union country not terrorising the centrist citizens?
rewrite: "Is Mr Tsakalotos not discussing local currencies within an EU nation that do not alarm centrist citizens?"

text: A strong Greece in Europe and the world. A Greece that is strong and no one can usurp its sovereign rights.
rewrite: A powerful Greece within Europe and globally. A nation of strength where no one can infringe upon its sovereign rights.

text: Friends. PASOK is here united and strong. All generations raise the sun of PASOK, its flag, the flag of hope.
rewrite: Comrades. PASOK stands united and strong. Every generation lifts high the sun of PASOK, its banner, the banner of hope.

text: We will go with the woman, the working woman who has no place to leave her child in the morning. As there are not enough nursery places, how are we going to deal with the demographic issue? If we do not support a network of nurseries and pre-school education throughout Greece to bring down the cost of raising your children, it is a priority for the democratic party to address the huge demographic issue.
rewrite: We will stand with the working mother who has nowhere to leave her child each morning. Given the shortage of nursery spots, how can we tackle the demographic challenge? Without backing a nationwide network of nurseries and early education to reduce child-rearing expenses, addressing the severe demographic issue remains a key priority for the democratic party.

text: The whole process for the new CAP programmes must be completed within one year without bureaucracy, with specific dates for application, assessment and payment. Stop inconveniencing our farmers, abolish the runner-up beneficiary policy through proper resource planning and not in wasted subsidies.
rewrite: The entire procedure for the new CAP programs should be finalized within a year, free from bureaucratic delays, with clear deadlines for application, evaluation, and disbursement. Cease causing difficulties for our farmers; eliminate the runner-up beneficiary policy via effective resource allocation, not through inefficient subsidies.

text: You know, this place has always had a patriotic, democratic feeling. That's why Golden Dawn never grew in Crete.
rewrite: "You know, this region has always held a patriotic, democratic spirit. That's why Golden Dawn never gained a foothold in Crete."

text: What do we say? What Spain did. Tax the super profits as long as they don't change their policy to financially support the middle class and the new generation, their entrepreneurship.
rewrite: "What should we propose? Follow Spain's approach. Impose a levy on excess profits unless they adjust their policies to provide financial backing for the middle class and younger generations, fostering their entrepreneurial ventures."

text: It also closes the eye. In Golden Dawn, by not voting to put a legislative obstacle in the way of allowing neo-Nazism and not only neo-Nazism to the murderers of Pavlos Fyssas to participate in the next Parliament. Which of these things is progressive?
rewrite: It also shuts its eyes. Within Golden Dawn, by failing to vote for a legislative barrier that would prevent neo-Nazism—and not just neo-Nazism—from enabling the killers of Pavlos Fyssas to enter the next Parliament. Which of these actions is progressive?

text: A Greece that will be a pioneer in the world of the real green transition.
rewrite: "A Greece that will lead the way in the global shift toward a truly green transition."

text: Friends. Finally, we also have a duty to invest in the natural resources of water. You farmers know very well that the next few years will be difficult and it is very likely that, just as we have been talking about energy this year, we will be talking about water in a few years' time.
rewrite: Friends. We must also commit to investing in water as a natural resource. You farmers understand that the coming years will be challenging, and it is probable that, much like we've focused on energy this year, we will be discussing water in the near future.

text: This is why we call on the Greek people. To make a choice of responsibility. A decision for change. A decision of change that is a clear choice between the state of opacity that exists only to serve the blue children and a state of meritocracy, transparency and respect for institutions.
rewrite: This is why we appeal to the Greek people. To choose responsibly. To decide for change. A decision for change that represents a clear choice between the opaque state, which exists solely to serve the privileged few, and a state built on merit, transparency, and respect for our institutions.

text: But what do we do? We embrace the real concerns of every Greek woman and every Greek man with the social democratic programme of concrete political choices and solutions for better days.
rewrite: "But is our response? We address the genuine worries of each Greek woman and man through a social democratic agenda of specific political decisions and remedies for brighter times."

text: We do not forget the mockery of the people with the false referendum of 2015.
rewrite: "We have not forgotten the people's scorn for the fraudulent 2015 referendum."

text: So we have a duty to create a healthy economy that will open up jobs with dignity.
rewrite: Thus, we bear the responsibility to build a robust economy that fosters dignified employment opportunities.

text: What do we propose? Up to 50.000€, 5% on dividends. And above 50,000, the tax is graduated to the highest level, 15%.
rewrite: What is our proposal? For amounts up to 50,000€, a 5% tax on dividends. Beyond 50,000€, the rate increases progressively, reaching a maximum of 15%.

text: So I'm scared. That the Left in our Greece. has gone from the left of caviar to the left of carnage. This is not the real left. The left is the one that respects human rights, the rule of law, and all these systems of parastate and digital gangs have nothing to do with it. This left is PASOK and the democratic party.
rewrite: So I'm afraid. That the Left in Greece has shifted from a caviar left to a left of violence. This isn't the genuine left. The true left upholds human rights, the rule of law, and all these networks of shadow states and digital mobs have no place in it. This left is PASOK and the democratic party.

text: I can't imagine my closest partner. Nash is giving you the TV licence tender. So I can hand out the channels to certain oligarchs who support me.
rewrite: "I can hardly picture my nearest ally. Nash is awarding you the TV licence contract. This allows me to allocate the channels to specific oligarchs who back me."

text: So we have other priorities. On 21 May, give us the strength, because for us the priority is both progress and stability from the first Sunday solutions, positions, a programme and a new political ethos, which they so desperately need. Particularly young people, so that they can believe in politics again.
rewrite: Thus, we have different priorities. On May 21st, grant us the strength, as our focus is on both advancement and steadiness from the initial Sunday resolutions, stances, a plan, and a fresh political spirit, which they urgently require. Especially the youth, so they can once again have faith in politics.

text: So here, from Evros, I want to look at the big issues. Why is the population decreasing? The biggest issue in Greece is demographic. Why is our population decreasing? Because we do not have a strong welfare state, the cost of living is galloping, private spending is third in Europe.
rewrite: From Evros, I aim to address the major concerns. Why is our population declining? The primary challenge in Greece is demographic. Why are we losing people? Due to a weak welfare system, soaring living costs, and private expenditure ranking third highest in Europe.

text: Friends and friends. On the other side is SYRIZA. It only knows. A practice. Divisiveness and populism along with the magic solutions that just missed to destroy the country. Today Mr. Tsipras is tightly embraced by the representative of the Karamanlis government, Mr. Antonaros. A terribly left-wing and progressive choice.
rewrite: Friends and comrades. Across from us stands SYRIZA. It understands only one approach. A method of division and populism, paired with simplistic solutions that nearly ruined the nation. Today, Mr. Tsipras is closely aligned with Mr. Antonaros, a figure from the Karamanlis administration. A profoundly left-wing and progressive selection.

text: Friends. Today the message here from Trikala. It is loud and clear. As long as the democratic party is beaten with paracratic methods, it will grow stronger and stronger in every corner of Greece. First of all, I would like to wish you a happy birthday, because we have many celebrants.
rewrite: Friends. Today the message from Trikala is resounding and unmistakable. As long as the democratic party is attacked through undemocratic means, it will only grow stronger across every region of Greece. First, I want to extend birthday wishes to you, as we have many to celebrate.

text: And as for the neo-geniuses of the New Democracy, who had the audacity to say that German reparations are a thing of the past: NO gentlemen. The Greek people have a memory and honour those who sacrificed for our country.
rewrite: "And concerning the new visionaries of the New Democracy, who dared to claim that German reparations belong to history: NO, sirs. The Greek nation remembers and honors those who gave their lives for our homeland."

text: Of course. Taxing the excess profits of all the powerful. And those 150 companies and the ELECTRICITY COMPANIES that received billions in subsidies at the expense of the Greek people and of course the profits of the banks.
rewrite: Certainly. Imposing taxes on the surplus earnings of all influential entities. This includes the 150 corporations and the POWER COMPANIES that gained billions in subsidies, funded by the Greek populace, along with the banks' profits.

text: We insist on lowering taxes on wage labour to reduce black work and to have good wages, especially for the young generation who are currently condemned to very low wages, unable to build a decent future.
rewrite: We advocate for reducing taxes on labor to curb undeclared work and ensure fair wages, particularly for the younger generation, who now face meager pay and cannot secure a stable future.

text: How can you? How can you Greeks trust the leader of the Patsy's who bought billions of loans, millions of your loans to speculate with your efforts, with your sacrifices?
rewrite: "How can you Greeks place your faith in the leader of the Patsy's, who acquired billions in loans, millions of your own, to gamble with your hard work and sacrifices?"

text: We don't want Greece to be a huge hotel. We want the travellers who come to Greece to taste the products of Made in Greece: agri-food, processing, good wine, good oil, our well-processed livestock products.
rewrite: "We don't wish for Greece to become merely a vast hotel. We desire that visitors to Greece experience the offerings of Made in Greece: agricultural goods, processed items, fine wine, quality oil, and our well-prepared livestock products."

text: And of course, the Greek mother. We have a duty to safeguard the economic and social position of the Greek mother, so I pledge that in the coming years no child will be left out of nurseries throughout Greece.
rewrite: "And naturally, the Greek mother. It is our responsibility to protect the economic and social standing of the Greek mother, so I vow that in the years ahead, no child across Greece will be excluded from nursery care."

text: Therefore, turn your back on depravity, turn your back on discord, turn your back on preservation wherever it comes from. On 21 May the sun of hope, the sun of hope, the sun of perspective, the sun of social justice, the sun of national dignity is rising again.
rewrite: Thus, reject corruption, reject division, reject self-preservation in all its forms. On May 21, the dawn of hope, the dawn of perspective, the dawn of social justice, the dawn of national honor returns.

text: This is the democratic, patriotic movement that guarantees both social justice and national dignity against the extremes of the political system. We do not play with the extremes. We are against those who undermine institutions, democracy and the public interest.
rewrite: "This democratic, patriotic movement upholds social justice and national dignity, standing firm against the extremes of the political system. We do not engage with extremism. We oppose those who threaten institutions, democracy, and the public good."

text: They say we have no seats. 15 days ago I said that all political leaders should commit themselves. That if we were part of the next government. All the institutions in the country and all the hospitals will have their administrations staffed by open international competitions and not by their party children as has been the case in recent years.
rewrite: "They claim we lack representation. Two weeks prior, I insisted that every political leader must pledge. That should we join the upcoming administration. Every national institution and hospital will fill their administrative roles through transparent global contests, not by appointing party affiliates as has occurred lately."

text: Friends and friends, jobs. Young people cannot live on the 400 and 500 euros of Mr Mitsotakis' growth and flexibility. As is the case with 700 000 Greeks in Greece.
rewrite: Friends and colleagues, employment. The youth cannot survive on the 400 to 500 euros offered by Mr. Mitsotakis' policies of growth and flexibility. This mirrors the situation of 700,000 Greeks across the country.

text: Also, banks. The banks, we've given billions for their capital adequacy. They too profited in the crisis, when the interest rate on deposits and mortgages was the highest in Europe.
rewrite: Additionally, the banks. We provided billions to bolster their capital adequacy. They also gained during the crisis, as deposit and mortgage interest rates were the highest in Europe.

text: So that's why, friends. I call on every Greek woman on May 21 together to make a decision to change the page for all Greeks and especially for the younger generation, so that your children and grandchildren can stay here with dignified jobs, so that we can deal with our demographics and give our country a perspective.
rewrite: Therefore, my friends, I urge every Greek woman on May 21 to join in making a choice that will turn a new page for all Greeks, particularly the youth, ensuring your children and grandchildren can remain here with respectable work, enabling us to address our demographic challenges and provide our nation with a hopeful future.

text: So we are the democratic party, because we respect justice, we respect people, we respect the citizen and we have a vision for Greece to become a normal European country and not our state, and not our state to be a tool of power for the tenant of Maximos.
rewrite: "We are the democratic party, as we uphold justice, value individuals, honor citizens, and envision Greece evolving into a standard European nation—not our state, nor our state serving as an instrument of power for the occupant of Maximos."

text: But we stood up then. Because today's era is reminiscent of the "dirty" '89 when you beat us both right and left together. As we stood then, we will stand now. The more you beat us, the stronger we get.
rewrite: "But we rose up back then. Because the present time echoes the 'dirty' '89, when you struck us from all sides. As we stood firm then, we will stand firm now. The harder you hit us, the tougher we become."

text: What do we say? 400,000€ tax-free across the board, not a single euro more, no multiplication. 400,000€ is a fair limit for the tax-free parental allowance. It was €200,000 in the past.
rewrite: "What should we propose? A flat €400,000 tax-free for everyone, no additional amounts, no scaling. €400,000 is a reasonable cap for the tax-free parental benefit. Previously, it stood at €200,000."

text: In the energy crisis the big oil producers are earning billions that they didn't earn in the previous years when there was no energy crisis, because our new taxes are the subsidies that he gave them from the taxes of the Greek people to reduce the tariffs, but he's going through one pocket and putting it in the other. Is that all we have seen?
rewrite: Amid the energy crisis, major oil companies are making billions they never saw in prior years without such a crisis, since our new taxes are essentially the subsidies he provided them using Greek citizens' tax money to lower rates—yet he's merely shifting funds from one pocket to another. Is this the full extent of what we've witnessed?

text: It is this patriotic movement that brought Cyprus into the European Union with the Cyprus problem unresolved. It was this patriotic movement that handled with national dignity all the issues with the Balkans, Turkey, the Southeastern Mediterranean.
rewrite: It is this patriotic movement that led Cyprus into the European Union while the Cyprus issue remained unresolved. This same patriotic movement addressed all matters concerning the Balkans, Turkey, and the Southeastern Mediterranean with national dignity.

text: So that's why it's good here from Patras. Trust in PASOK and let us make the change possible because we know that we made the brave changes you want - give us the strength again together to build a Greece of dignity and perspective.
rewrite: That's precisely what makes Patras an ideal starting point. Have faith in PASOK and allow us to enable the transformation, as we've already initiated the bold changes you seek. Grant us your collective strength once more to forge a Greece of honor and vision.

text: Let the citizens of Alexandroupolis remember. When were these major projects, the hospitals, the roads. I am not PASOK, did not make a mistake, but that has been built in the country and in regional development. It is the work of this democratic party that puts the national interest above all else. The public interest.
rewrite: Let the people of Alexandroupolis recall. When were these significant projects, the hospitals, the roads, constructed? I am not PASOK, and I have not erred, but what has been built across the nation and in regional advancement is the achievement of this democratic party, which places the national interest above all else. The common good.

text: How can you trust them? They exposed our country internationally and both of them. One with the wiretapping, the other with the referendums have made the country a negative topic in many media outlets around the world.
rewrite: How can you place faith in them? They've brought international scrutiny upon our nation and both individuals. One through surveillance activities, the other via referendum actions, have turned the country into a subject of unfavorable coverage in numerous global media.

text: Friends. We must understand that on May 21, voting for PASOK, only PASOK comes out. And what our political opponents are saying - Mr Mitsotakis saying that you vote PASOK and you get SYRIZA and Mr Tsipras saying that you vote PASOK and you get New Democracy - shows their terror and their anxiety for the rebirth of the democratic party, for the great mass participation of democratic citizens here in Ioannina as well.
rewrite: Friends, we must realize that on May 21, a vote for PASOK is a vote solely for PASOK. What our political rivals claim—Mr. Mitsotakis saying a vote for PASOK brings SYRIZA, and Mr. Tsipras saying a vote for PASOK brings New Democracy—reveals their fear and unease about the revival of the democratic party and the broad participation of democratic citizens here in Ioannina.

text: Friends, I want to thank you very much for your presence. It is a great honor. Today here in Alexandroupolis we continue our struggle for vindication on May 21, a vindication that is not partisan, it is a vindication against the arrogance of power against the client state against the lack of respect for institutions and democracy against political forces that unfortunately invest in populism and toxicity.
rewrite: Friends, I extend my deepest gratitude for your presence here. It is a tremendous honor. Today in Alexandroupolis, we carry forward our fight for justice on May 21—a justice that transcends party lines. It is a stand against the arrogance of power, against a client state, against the disrespect for our institutions and democracy, and against political forces that, regrettably, thrive on populism and toxicity.

text: Friends, recently Mr Mitsotakis said that he cannot talk to the PASOK of my time. He said that I was not a danger to democracy. You know this very well, because you gave me a strong mandate of autonomy in December 21.
rewrite: Friends, Mr. Mitsotakis recently stated that he cannot engage with the PASOK from my era. He remarked that I posed no threat to democracy. You are well aware of this, as you granted me a robust mandate for autonomy on December 21.

text: So we don't want the state to be a booty, we don't want the state to be a booty to the tenant of the Maximos building. This party wants the state to guarantee the public interest with transparency, with meritocracy, with respect for the citizen.
rewrite: "We do not wish for the state to become a prize, nor for it to be a prize for the occupant of the Maximos building. This party aims for the state to safeguard the public interest through transparency, meritocracy, and respect for the citizen."

text: Our goal is an open, non-discriminatory society and this is a historical legacy of PASOK. A society that will not live with the nightmare of racism and xenophobia.
rewrite: "Our aim is to foster an open, inclusive society, a historical legacy of PASOK. A society free from the specters of racism and xenophobia."

text: We didn't have the eavesdropping state, we haven't had such a state for decades and a prime minister appears to cover up for his nephew and the NSA or the competent prosecutor and businessmen who were dealing with these illegal software. Didn't they bring them into parliament, they became a shield to protect this parasite and he says he is a liberal? That is not liberalism. That's agitation for power. It's arrogance. It's all that they have to fight for.
rewrite: "We have not been a surveillance state for decades, yet a prime minister seems to shield his nephew, the NSA, the responsible prosecutor, and businessmen involved with these unlawful programs. Were they not brought before parliament, only to serve as a shield for this parasite? And he claims to be a liberal? That is not liberalism. It is a drive for power. It is arrogance. It is everything they stand to defend."

text: If we had had a meaningful discussion on the refugee migration issue. Substantial but without games, our farmers all over Greece would not be crying today because they have no farm workers and their fruit is rotting on the trees. We would respect as a state, European laws and the framework that exists and respect for refugees, and on the other hand we would have a serious immigration policy to deal with the huge issues of the Greek economy, as is the case in livestock farming, tourism and the agricultural sector.
rewrite: Had we engaged in a genuine dialogue on refugee migration—substantive and free of political maneuvering—farmers across Greece would not now be lamenting the shortage of labor while their fruit decays on the branches. As a state, we would uphold European laws and the existing framework, showing due regard for refugees, while simultaneously implementing a robust immigration policy to address the profound challenges facing the Greek economy, particularly in livestock, tourism, and agriculture.

text: Corresponding property, corresponding protection for agricultural property, protection for borrowers in Swiss francs, by limiting the interest rate increase to 1/3 for the borrower and 2/3 for the banking institution. Substantial negotiation with banks and taking measures to eliminate and prevent increases in interest rates on loans for weak households and reducing the banks' profit margin for consistent borrowers, so that consistent borrowers also have incentives to continue to comply with their arrangements.
rewrite: Matching property, matching safeguards for agricultural assets, safeguards for Swiss franc borrowers, by capping interest rate hikes at one-third for the borrower and two-thirds for the banking institution. Extensive negotiation with banks and implementing steps to stop and avert interest rate rises on loans for vulnerable households, while trimming banks' profit margins for reliable borrowers, so that reliable borrowers also have motivation to keep honoring their agreements.

text: Is the economy doing well? And there the questions are relentless. The trade deficit increased under the New Democracy. Public debt has broken the 400 billion euro barrier and only 14% of investment is productive and not real estate. Investment that is gutting the Greek economy investment that has made rents skyrocket and land purchase costs expensive for Greeks in this day and age.
rewrite: Is the economy performing well? The questions continue without pause. Under New Democracy, the trade deficit has grown. Public debt has surpassed 400 billion euros, with only 14% of investment being productive rather than in real estate. This investment is hollowing out the Greek economy, driving rents to soar and making land purchase costs prohibitively high for Greeks today.

text: We have the one who talks about progressive governance. You cannot have progressive governance by turning a blind eye to Golden Dawn. It cannot. On the one hand, Mr Mitsotakis is allowing 3 years to campaign. Golden Dawn from prison. And on the other hand, the so-called left, a few months before, when we have to show the way to protect our democratic constitution, to play Pontius Pilate to fish in the murky waters of the far right.
rewrite: We have those who advocate for progressive governance. Yet you cannot achieve progressive governance by ignoring Golden Dawn. It is impossible. While Mr. Mitsotakis permits three years for campaigning, Golden Dawn operates from prison. Meanwhile, the so-called left, just months earlier, when we must demonstrate how to defend our democratic constitution, chooses to wash its hands like Pontius Pilate, fishing in the troubled waters of the far right.

text: this party? This democratic movement, PASOK. It has always handled national issues with realism and patriotism, without grand talk. That is why I call on the Greeks to trust us on national issues as well. This is the party that put Cyprus in the European Union with the Cyprus problem unresolved. This is the party that created the Helsinki Strategy, which Karamanlis discredited.
rewrite: This democratic movement, PASOK, has consistently approached national matters with realism and patriotism, avoiding lofty rhetoric. That is precisely why I urge Greeks to place their trust in us on national issues as well. This is the party that secured Cyprus' entry into the European Union despite the unresolved Cyprus problem. This is the party that established the Helsinki Strategy, which Karamanlis later undermined.

text: During the days of the current prime minister, social inequalities and the accuracy of basic foodstuffs have widened. Prices are still galloping through this twelve-month inflationary surge. New jobs the more than 400 €. This is the gentleman's growth. Mitsotakis, the growth of 300 € but making many young people. Your children and your grandchildren are unable to establish themselves in our country and are constantly looking for opportunities abroad.
rewrite: Under the current prime minister's tenure, social disparities and the cost of essential foods have increased. Prices continue to race ahead amid this year-long inflationary wave. New positions pay just over 400 €. This is the gentleman's growth. Mitsotakis, the growth of 300 € yet leaving many young people behind. Your children and grandchildren cannot build a life in our nation and perpetually seek prospects overseas.

text: Friends, we are facing Kyriakos Mitsotakis who is hiding what is coming as a result of his political choices. And on the other side, Mr Tsipras, who promises things that once again he knows cannot be done. Back then he called them illusions. Now he knows he won't be in government and can say whatever he wants.
rewrite: Friends, we confront Kyriakos Mitsotakis, concealing the consequences of his political decisions. Meanwhile, Mr. Tsipras pledges actions he understands are unattainable. Previously, he termed them illusions. Now, aware he won't be governing, he feels free to promise anything.

text: For us, it is a policy that makes Greece a country at the forefront of sustainable development and gives priority to the weakest, to the middle class, to the real producers, farmers, manufacturers, to make choices with photovoltaics, renewable sources, with a fair democratized energy transition that will not lead to new energy poverty.
rewrite: "For Greece, this policy positions the nation as a leader in sustainable development, prioritizing the most vulnerable, the middle class, and genuine producers—farmers and manufacturers. It enables choices centered on photovoltaics and renewable sources, ensuring a fair and democratized energy transition that avoids creating new forms of energy poverty."

text: Friends, why do I call them unrepentant? Because we have organizations, hospitals that for many decades, except for a short period of our own government in 2010 with open gov, as soon as the elections are over, failed politicians, old MPs, old cronies of Maximos, take over the positions of governors, organizations and hospitals.
rewrite: Friends, why do I label them as unrepentant? Because our institutions, including hospitals, have for decades—aside from a brief period under our own administration in 2010 with open governance—been quickly seized after elections by failed politicians, former MPs, and old associates of Maximos, who assume control as governors and heads of organizations and hospitals.

text: When his former finance minister tells him about local currencies, doesn't that scare people? And when Mr Katrougalos reveals that the hit on the middle class and freelancers is coming again? Who are they helping? The people or New Democracy with these unspeakable regressions?
rewrite: "When his former finance minister mentions local currencies, doesn't that alarm the public? And when Mr. Katrougalos discloses that the middle class and freelancers are facing another blow? Who benefits from this? The citizens or New Democracy, through these indefensible setbacks?"

text: The pension is starving, there are no good jobs. Mitsotakis' growth is a growth of 400 € for young people, a young person with 400 € cannot build a life of dignity. So what do we say to your children and grandchildren who have boarded planes and gone to European countries and other third countries? We say that we have a programme that will bring sustainable development, regional development. We are the party of regional development.
rewrite: The pension is insufficient, and quality jobs are scarce. Mitsotakis' growth means just 400 € for young people—a sum too meager to build a dignified life. So what do we tell your children and grandchildren who have boarded planes for Europe and other third countries? We say we have a plan to achieve sustainable development and regional growth. We are the party of regional development.

text: Friends, Thessaloniki. Thessaloniki today sends a message of hope to every part of the country for the next 6 days. The struggle will make us the strong leading force in our country. Friends, your presence today is truly moving and shows that the more they fight us, the stronger we grow.
rewrite: Friends of Thessaloniki, today this city sends a hopeful message across the nation for the coming six days. Our struggle will forge us into the powerful, guiding force of our country. Your presence here today is deeply moving, proving that the more they oppose us, the stronger we become.

text: And PASOK. How will it use the vote of the Greek people? They ask us again. We do not prejudge the will of the Greek people. We do not set up coalitions on the sidelines and behind the scenes we do not say, like Mr Mitsotakis, that the first Sunday does not count and we will hold more elections until he becomes prime minister. We are not talking about a government of either winners or losers.
rewrite: "And PASOK. How will it utilize the Greek people's vote? They question us once more. We do not preempt the will of the Greek people. We do not form coalitions in the background or behind closed doors, nor do we claim, as Mr. Mitsotakis does, that the initial Sunday is insignificant and that further elections will be held until he assumes the premiership. We are not discussing a government comprised of either victors or the defeated."

text:
Our trees are rotting this year, the hotels have thousands of shortages, and so does the catering industry.
So let us stop with the cheap false dilemmas, we want border security, but we also want an organised immigration plan to deal with the huge problems of the agricultural sector, manufacturing and tourism. That is what I am ready to discuss, not cheap communication games that divide the Greek people.
rewrite:
This year our trees are decaying, hotels face thousands of vacancies, and the same goes for the catering sector.  
So let's end these simplistic false choices: we need border security, yet we also require a structured immigration strategy to address the severe issues in agriculture, manufacturing, and tourism. That is what I am prepared to negotiate, not shallow messaging tactics that split the Greek populace.

text: This is the party of social justice and national dignity. That is why I invite every Greek here in Ioannina. To trust this party, the democratic party of respect for human rights, the rule of law and the party of hope and perspective for the underprivileged, the party of the middle class.
rewrite: This is the party of social justice and national pride. That is why I call on every Greek in Ioannina to place their trust in this party—the democratic party that upholds human rights and the rule of law, the party of hope and vision for the disadvantaged, and the party of the middle class.

text: I can't imagine. I can't imagine. A close associate of mine. My closest associate. And he's a graduate of the Democritus University of Thrace. To be the protagonist in a wiretapping ring. And then to cover him up because he knows they knew?
rewrite: "I cannot fathom it. I simply cannot. A trusted colleague of mine. My most trusted colleague. And he is an alumnus of the Democritus University of Thrace. To be the central figure in a wiretapping scheme. And then to shield him because they were aware he knew?"

text: Support for farmers, farmers, farmers, farmers' cooperatives with priority to renewable energy parks, so that each one of you knows that through renewable energy sources you will have fixed energy costs for the next 15 years, as is the case in all European countries, and not the green transition to be a business of 5 oligarchs in Greece. We want the green transition with energy justice without energy poverty, with priority for producers. And to the poorest Greeks we want a highly interconnected network, that is what we are saying.
rewrite: Support for farmers and agricultural cooperatives, prioritizing renewable energy projects, ensures that each of you can secure stable energy costs for the next 15 years, as seen across Europe. The green transition must not become a venture for a handful of oligarchs in Greece. We advocate for a just green transition, free from energy poverty, with producers at the forefront. For the most vulnerable Greeks, we call for a robust and interconnected energy network—this is our commitment.

text:
Let's go to the polls. Let's go to the polls. And we are asking for a strong mandate to make past the divisiveness, arrogance, authoritarianism and the client state.
This patriotic movement has a duty to stand in the way of the destruction of the Greek economy, it has a duty to create the conditions for fair development, social justice and national dignity.
rewrite:
Let's head to the polls. Let's head to the polls. We seek a decisive mandate to move beyond division, hubris, authoritarian rule, and a client state.
This patriotic movement is duty-bound to halt the ruin of Greece's economy, and to forge the path for equitable growth, social justice, and national honor.

text:
To do. A new beginning. For the Greek people to feel that our party is fighting for justice, for change, for fair and sustainable development, you know? Even at the European level and these 2 governments have exposed us; irreparably in 2015, don't you remember what happened in the referendum of mockery?
The Greek people voted no and suddenly. Mr. Tsipras makes the no a yes.
rewrite:
To be done. A fresh start. For the Greek people to sense that our party is battling for justice, for transformation, for equitable and lasting progress, understand? Even at the European level, these two administrations have revealed our vulnerabilities; irreversibly in 2015—do you not recall the events of the farcical referendum?
The Greek people voted no, and abruptly. Mr. Tsipras turns that no into a yes.

text: And indeed. To have the nerve to want to make fun of him. We have no need to mock Andreas Papandreou, because this party, this people, this movement is the child of Andreas Papandreou. It is not the child of populism.
rewrite: "And indeed. To dare to even think of ridiculing him. There is no reason for us to mock Andreas Papandreou, for this party, this nation, this movement is the offspring of Andreas Papandreou. It is not the offspring of populism."

text: And then Mr Mitsotakis. And what did we see of Mr. Mitsotakis? to answer the question why PASOK? I saw Mr Mitsotakis. Increasing the public debt by 50 billion. We saw Mr Mitsotakis increasing inequalities, we have an economic crisis, a pandemic crisis, and instead of the rich losing, the poorer people are losing.
rewrite: "And then there's Mr. Mitsotakis. What did we witness from Mr. Mitsotakis? In response to why PASOK? I observed Mr. Mitsotakis. He expanded the public debt by 50 billion. We saw Mr. Mitsotakis widening inequalities; amid an economic crisis and a pandemic crisis, instead of the wealthy suffering, it's the poorer people who are losing out."

text: A month ago that the European institutions and they say, we want to see the government, it's never before that a Greek government does not accept European institutions, saying there's no need to meet you on human rights issues. So here we are talking about two people who I do not reject it, because it is a question of ego, I do it because I believe that the protagonists of problems and disparagement cannot be the protagonists of solutions, but they must be marginalized and there must be a democratic progressive solution.
rewrite: A month ago, European institutions stated they wished to meet with the government. It is unprecedented for a Greek administration to refuse such a request, declaring there is no need to discuss human rights. Thus, we refer to two individuals whom I do not dismiss out of ego, but because I hold that those who create and belittle problems cannot lead solutions. They should be sidelined, allowing for a democratic and progressive resolution.

text: He feeds rabbits and stones, he feeds things that will never happen. As he says, he's going to raise 25% of the private sector wage. How are you going to do it, Mr Mitsotakis, by royal decree? We know of no other government in Europe that says before the elections how much private sector wages will be increased.
rewrite: "He tends to rabbits and stones, he tends to what will never come to pass. As he claims, he intends to increase private sector wages by 25%. How do you plan to achieve this, Mr. Mitsotakis, by royal command? We are unaware of any other European government that announces specific private sector wage hikes before an election."

text: The Recovery Fund to finance the energy grid across Greece, so that municipalities can make communities energy efficient. Farmers, ranchers, energy price stability. I am very much afraid that costs will rise and what happened last year will happen. The tariff will be reduced from our taxes and from our taxes they will make billions in subsidies. Those who are being coddled by the media, by Mr Mitsotakis, we have a duty to stand in the way of this injustice that is being done at the expense of the production of Greece, of the country.
rewrite: The Recovery Fund aims to finance Greece's energy grid, enabling municipalities to enhance community energy efficiency. This includes support for farmers, ranchers, and stabilizing energy prices. There is significant concern that costs may escalate, repeating last year's scenario. Tariffs will be lowered using tax revenues, which will then fund billions in subsidies. Those favored by the media and Mr. Mitsotakis must be opposed; we have an obligation to resist this injustice, which undermines Greece's production and national interests.

text: But all these years we've been bored. We're tired of hearing from the channels, from the New Democracy's executives about the state of the unqualified. Who were the excellence? All those involved in the tragedy of Tempe were appointed party children of the Grand Maximus and ONNED.
rewrite: Yet all these years we have felt a profound boredom. We are weary of listening to the channels, to the executives of New Democracy, speak about the condition of the unqualified. Who were the excellent ones? Every person implicated in the Tempe tragedy was a party child appointed by the Grand Maximus and ONNED.

text: It doesn't fit, Mr Tsipras, Andreas Papandreou and the stories of the sea without borders. Andreas Papandreou and "Aegean Prespes" do not fit. Leave the great leader of the democratic party alone, in the arms of history. All you have offered him is the road to prison.
rewrite: "It does not suit you, Mr. Tsipras, to speak of Andreas Papandreou and tales of a borderless sea. Andreas Papandreou and 'Aegean Prespes' do not align. Let the great leader of the democratic party rest, embraced by history. All you have given him is a path to imprisonment."

text: We are so much autonomous from the oligarchy. The new political ethos of the party will respect every Greek woman and every Greek who has just been a point of corruption, we sent a lady home, while Mitsotakis covers his nephew and Mr Tsipras covers his best friend, by having him on the ballot papers, on the SYRIZA ballot papers.
rewrite: "We are largely independent from the oligarchy. The party's fresh political spirit will honor every Greek woman and every Greek who has merely been a target of corruption; we dismissed a woman, whereas Mitsotakis shields his nephew and Mr. Tsipras protects his closest friend by placing him on the ballot, on the SYRIZA ballot papers."

text: The real left is here in the democratic party. And finally, justice everywhere - yes, the Greek people are thirsty for justice - we all feel that we need a better quality of justice in the country - justice everywhere - but if Mr.Tsipras believed this, if Mr.Pappas, who was convicted 13-0 by the Special Court for the illegal TV licenses he wanted to give to his oligarch friends, had believed it, he would not have been on the SYRIZA ballot papers.
rewrite: The authentic left resides within the democratic party. Ultimately, justice is needed everywhere—indeed, the Greek people yearn for justice—we all sense the necessity for a higher standard of justice nationwide. However, if Mr. Tsipras truly held this belief, and if Mr. Pappas, who was unanimously convicted 13-0 by the Special Court for attempting to grant illegal TV licenses to his oligarch associates, had believed it, he would not have appeared on the SYRIZA ballot.

text: Our priority is energy communities, our priority is investment in the grid and storage, our priority is for the poorest Greeks to have photovoltaics on their roofs so that they are not driven into energy poverty and new inequalities after 2030.
rewrite: "Our focus is on energy communities, our focus is on investing in the grid and storage, our focus is on ensuring the poorest Greeks have solar panels on their roofs to avoid energy poverty and new disparities after 2030."

text: We want a state that respects the citizen. A state that will have a robust democracy, a strong welfare state that will reduce inequalities and give prospects to Greek children through strong public public education, strong public health care. These are the great needs that our country has today. For these needs I call upon you to fight for them every day.
rewrite: "We seek a state that honors its people. A nation built on resilient democracy and a powerful welfare system to lessen disparities, offering Greek youth a future through robust public education and comprehensive public healthcare. These are the pressing needs our country faces now. For these causes, I urge you to strive for them daily."

text: With a strong PASOK, I pledge to every Greek to create a social housing pool of 150,000 houses throughout Greece, newly built or with Recovery Fund funds or rebuilt with apologies, with tax incentives and relief for their owners. I am talking about closed houses with a view to making them available at cheap rent so that young couples and the poorest Greeks can have decent access. This is how we achieve competition to drive down rents. Because today one of the biggest cost of living systems every day is the cost of rent.
rewrite: With a robust PASOK, I promise every Greek citizen to establish a social housing stock of 150,000 homes across Greece, either newly constructed, funded by the Recovery Fund, or renovated with apologies, supported by tax incentives and relief for property owners. I refer to vacant homes intended for affordable rental, enabling young couples and the most disadvantaged Greeks to secure decent housing. This approach fosters competition to reduce rental prices. Because currently, one of the most significant daily living expenses is the cost of rent.

text: Friends. Portugal has a 10% difference in tax between a family with no children and a family with 2 children. We have a debt at this level, a tax incentive to have many families with 2 children so that Hellenism can survive in the future, otherwise we will be eight and a half million of an ageing population.
rewrite: Friends. In Portugal, there is a 10% tax gap between a childless family and one with two children. We owe it to ourselves to create tax incentives that encourage families to have two children, ensuring the survival of Hellenism for the future. Without this, we risk becoming a population of eight and a half million, increasingly aged.

text: And they're not interested in the growth of the Greek economy, but to speculate a little bit more. So we have another plan for that we want all negotiations to be done with transparency criteria over the table, as it would be with the banking system and of course what kind of state we envision not. However, the state that subsidises the oligarchs and they make more profits through the energy crisis than in previous years from the taxes of the Greek people.
rewrite: "They are not concerned with the Greek economy's growth, but rather with further speculation. Therefore, we have an alternative plan: we insist that all negotiations be conducted with clear, transparent criteria on the table, as would be expected in the banking sector, and certainly not the kind of state we imagine. Instead, it is a state that supports the oligarchs, allowing them to profit more from the energy crisis than in past years, funded by the taxes of the Greek people."

text: Tsipras said yesterday that Varoufakis with the Demetra programme is a sponsor of Mitsotakis, and if Varoufakis did not exist, Tsipras added, he would have had to invent him in order to terrorise the centrist citizens. But is he the only one who terrorises the centrist citizens, Mr Tsipras?
rewrite: Tsipras stated yesterday that Varoufakis, through the Demetra programme, acts as a sponsor for Mitsotakis, and if Varoufakis were not present, Tsipras remarked, he would have needed to create him to frighten centrist citizens. Yet, is he the sole individual who frightens centrist citizens, Mr Tsipras?

text: This public health that George Gennimatas built with Paraskevas Avgerinos and Mr Mitsotakis is dismantling with his legislation. This education that the child of the farmer and the farmer in the 1980s here from Aitoloakarnania was studying to become a doctor, an engineer, a lawyer, producing wealth and providing his family with dignity and prospects. This education as a lever for social justice and upward social mobility. We envision it with a strong public character.
rewrite: This public health system, established by George Gennimatas alongside Paraskevas Avgerinos, is being dismantled through Mr. Mitsotakis's legislation. This education, which in the 1980s enabled the farmer's child from Aitoloakarnania to study and become a doctor, engineer, or lawyer—generating wealth and offering dignity and prospects to their family. This education serves as a lever for social justice and upward mobility. We envision it with a robust public character.

text: 2/3 of state revenues are indirect taxes that hit the poorest Greeks, the middle class, the most vulnerable. And of course, it does not explain how it will reduce the obscenity of foodstuffs. What it will do about the speculative oligarchs who quadrupled their profits in 2022.
rewrite: Two-thirds of state income comes from indirect taxes, which disproportionately burden Greece's poorest citizens, the middle class, and the most vulnerable. Moreover, it fails to clarify how it will address the exorbitant cost of basic foods. Nor does it specify what actions will be taken against the speculative oligarchs whose profits quadrupled in 2022.

text: I want you to think about who is against us. Against us are those who have even come to instrumentalize the neo-Nazism of Golden Dawn.  The so-called left-wingers are not voting to prevent our democracy from preventing the murderers of Fyssa from taking part in the elections. And Mr Mitsotakis is counting the neo-Nazi party in the polls to see what he will do.
rewrite: "Consider who opposes us. Our adversaries include those who have even exploited Golden Dawn's neo-Nazism. The self-styled leftists refuse to vote to stop our democracy from barring Fyssa's killers from the elections. Meanwhile, Mr. Mitsotakis factors the neo-Nazi party into his polling calculations to determine his next move."

text: It is no accident, friends. After Lehman Brothers in 2007, PASOK executives were saying, "Take measures against Karamanlis, he didn't get them and we ended up with the memoranda. So we come today in 2023 to not cry 30 we say take measures all together, let us learn from the mistakes of all and not some remain unrepentant at the expense of you and your children.
rewrite: It is no coincidence, friends. Following Lehman Brothers in 2007, PASOK officials were urging, "Act against Karamanlis; he failed to heed warnings, and we ended up with the memoranda. So here we are in 2023, not to lament but to insist: we must all take action together, learning from everyone's errors, not letting some remain unrepentant at the cost of you and your children."

text: Free farmland concession and tax reduction for young farmers. We need to support the primary sector throughout Greece and link agri-food with tourism, so that we can increase exports to create good jobs. Not only. On issues that are closely related to the tourism sector, but more broadly to the Greek economy.
rewrite: Free land grants and tax cuts for young farmers. We must bolster the primary sector across Greece and connect agriculture with tourism to boost exports and generate quality employment. Moreover, on matters directly tied to tourism, and more broadly, to the Greek economy as a whole.

text: We don't forget that you handed over billions of "red loans" to the crows of the funds and they are blackmailing the weakest Greeks. Do not underestimate, Mr Tsipras, the intelligence of the Greek people. It remembers very well who was leftist first. It was Andreas Papandreou. And not you and Kammenos.
rewrite: We have not forgotten that you entrusted billions in "red loans" to the fund's vultures, who are now extorting the most vulnerable Greeks. Do not underestimate, Mr. Tsipras, the intelligence of the Greek people. They remember clearly who was the original leftist. It was Andreas Papandreou. Not you and Kammenos.

text:
We will go with the person who took a mortgage for their main house and now their mortgage has doubled with the small and medium-sized businessman whose bank door remains closed, at the same time that Europe from the Recovery Fund gave 11 billion to support these people who cannot get liquidity in the banking system.
The new republic gave the first 1.1 billion at 1.2 interest to 67 strong businesses. Without taking a drachma small business. So that is why we are calling for redirection of Recovery Fund loans.
rewrite:
We stand with the homeowner whose mortgage has doubled and the small business owner facing closed bank doors, while Europe's Recovery Fund provided 11 billion to aid those lacking banking liquidity.  
The new republic allocated the initial 1.1 billion at 1.2% interest to 67 robust enterprises, leaving small businesses without a drachma. This is precisely why we urge a reallocation of Recovery Fund loans.

text: Friends and friends rail reconnection of the region with the rest of Greece. you can't talk about transport costs and the cheapest. I won't say safe with the tragedy of Tempe, but it is the safest as long as the state works properly. So that he wouldn't have other priorities, the buffoonery, the speculation. The train, the most environmentally sustainable means of transport, should not exist throughout Greece, especially in areas with strong development potential.
rewrite: Friends and allies advocate for reconnecting the region with the rest of Greece. One cannot discuss transport costs and the most affordable options. I won't call it safe after the Tempe tragedy, but it is the safest as long as the state functions correctly. This ensures there are no other priorities, like buffoonery or speculation. The train, the most environmentally sustainable mode of transport, should be available across all of Greece, particularly in areas with high development potential.

text: PASOK's ballot papers have democrats, progressives, socialists, people who fight every day for justice, for the prospects of our people, they have neither the extreme right-wing burnouts of ANEL nor the closest associate of Mr Karamanlis. For this lessons of historicity and social roots of this historic party, we do not accept these partners of the devaluation of the right word.
rewrite: The ballot papers of PASOK include democrats, progressives, and socialists—individuals who daily strive for justice and the future of our nation. They contain neither the far-right remnants of ANEL nor the closest ally of Mr. Karamanlis. Given the historical lessons and social foundations of this historic party, we cannot accept these partners in the devaluation of the right word.

text: Friends, we have a duty to protect small and medium-sized enterprises. We have a duty to protect the people who in a fair way, in an honest way, have tried to stand on their own two feet. That is why we are universally proposing 120 instalments for tax and EFKA for everyone and not for a few, as the Mitsotakis government did, which is being swept away by the economic reality, by the desperation of thousands of Greek small and medium-sized businesses.
rewrite: Friends, we have an obligation to safeguard small and medium-sized enterprises. We have an obligation to protect those who, fairly and honestly, have sought to be self-reliant. That is why we are proposing 120 installments for tax and EFKA payments for all, not just a select few—unlike the Mitsotakis government, which is being overwhelmed by economic realities and the despair of thousands of Greek small and medium-sized businesses.

text: Friends. A crucial issue is demography. The tax rates between a family with no children and a family with 2 children are 2 points different in Portugal, they are 10 points different. So we are supporting with serious tax incentives all families with children in the country, because the democratic party believes that the greatest national issue of our time is demographic shrinkage.
rewrite: Friends. Demographics is a vital matter. In Portugal, the tax difference between a childless family and one with two children is 2 percentage points; it is 10 points elsewhere. Therefore, we are providing substantial tax incentives to all families with children nationwide, as the Democratic Party holds that the foremost national challenge of our era is population decline.

text: But they have the nerve to take the name of Andreas Papandreou in their mouths. Andreas Papandreou, Mr Tsipras, would never have called in '81 for the excrement of the junta to vote for PASOK. He would not have considered them to be deceived. Andreas Papandreou would never have talked about Prespes in the Aegean. Andreas Papandreou would never have said that there are no borders at sea.
rewrite: Yet they dare invoke the name of Andreas Papandreou. Mr. Tsipras, Andreas Papandreou would never have appealed in '81 for the remnants of the junta to support PASOK. He would not have regarded them as misled. Andreas Papandreou would never have spoken of Prespes in the Aegean. Andreas Papandreou would never have claimed that maritime borders do not exist.

text: And we have to deal with it with substantial policies. Also, development. What development? Is it sustainable growth to hear about millions of tourists every year without a general benefit to the Greek economy? Obviously we consider it our tourism, but what tourism? Tourism that consumes Greek wine that tastes Greek processed products, Greek oil and other products, so that the benefit is not only in specific regions.
rewrite: We must address this with robust policies. Additionally, development—but what kind? Is it sustainable growth to welcome millions of tourists annually without widespread gains for Greece's economy? Certainly, we view it as our tourism sector, yet what form should it take? Tourism that enjoys Greek wine, consumes authentic Greek processed goods, Greek olive oil, and other local products, ensuring benefits extend beyond just certain areas.

text: You know my goal? This party is to become the home of every democrat and progressive Greek to stop being hostage to a false dilemma between Tsipras and Mitsotakis, so I call on every democrat, every progressive from Ioannina to come to our side and stand by us in this difficult struggle. But you can be sure that it will be victorious because it is a struggle for dignity and perspective.
rewrite: "What is my aim? This gathering aims to become the home for every democrat and progressive Greek, to end the captivity of a false choice between Tsipras and Mitsotakis. Therefore, I urge every democrat, every progressive from Ioannina to join our side and support us in this challenging fight. Yet rest assured, it will be triumphant because it is a battle for dignity and a future."

text: We are not taking a measure between them, we are on the opposite side of these authoritarian choices, these authoritarian practices that undermine the future of Greece, that expose the Greek people. Because we are the party of principles, of values. That is why we are against it, because we have never played with democracy. We have never played with the rule of law, we have never played with institutions, we have never instrumentalised justice.
rewrite: "We are not choosing between them; we stand firmly opposed to these authoritarian decisions and actions that jeopardize Greece's future and endanger its citizens. As a party rooted in principles and values, we reject such approaches because we have always respected democracy. We have never compromised on the rule of law, undermined institutions, or manipulated the justice system."

text: Friends, Mr Tsipras is the real golden sponsor of Mr Mitsotakis. The other day, Mr Tsipras said that his sponsor is Varoufakis, who is terrorising the centrist citizens with his 'Demetra' plans. And I ask you, is he the one who is talking about the Aegean Prespes? Is he who says that the sea has no borders not terrorising the centre?
rewrite: Friends, Mr. Tsipras is truly the primary benefactor of Mr. Mitsotakis. Recently, Mr. Tsipras claimed that his own sponsor is Varoufakis, who frightens moderate citizens with his 'Demetra' proposals. Yet I ask, is he not the one discussing the Aegean and Prespes? Does his statement that the sea knows no boundaries not also alarm the center?

text: Friends, they are trying to blackmail citizens with fake dilemmas, hoping to distort our electoral base. They want to plunder PASOK, but the plunder is over. PASOK is here to send home the government of Mr Mitsotakis, without going back to the painful experience of 2015-19 with Tsipras and Kammenos.
rewrite: Comrades, they aim to coerce the people with false choices, seeking to undermine our voting foundation. They intend to pillage PASOK, yet that looting has ended. PASOK stands ready to dismiss Mr. Mitsotakis' administration, without returning to the distressing period of 2015-19 under Tsipras and Kammenos.

text: For this message, a message of disapproval for New Democracy and a message of victory for the Democratic Party.
rewrite: "This message conveys disapproval toward New Democracy and celebrates a triumph for the Democratic Party."

text: It does not talk about the national debt. 50 billion extra public debt that Mr Mitsotakis has loaded onto future generations of Greeks. And there is something else. For the first time since 2010, the trade deficit is one of the largest in Europe. It's the biggest Greece has had in 12 years. This is the real state of the Greek economy.
rewrite: It fails to address the national debt—an additional 50 billion euros in public debt that Mr. Mitsotakis has placed on the shoulders of future Greek generations. Moreover, there is another issue. For the first time since 2010, the trade deficit ranks among the largest in Europe. It is the most significant deficit Greece has seen in 12 years. This reflects the true condition of the Greek economy.

text: But is that all? They tell us they are afraid. He says that we will settle with New Democracy. Our ballot papers, Mr Tsipras, are full of centre-left, progressive democrats. You made up with New Democracy before the elections of 21 May, with Kammeni, with Mr Antonaros and with all those who have identified themselves with the decline of the country and the extreme right.
rewrite: "But is that the whole story? They claim to be fearful. He insists we will reconcile with New Democracy. Our ballots, Mr. Tsipras, are filled with center-left, progressive democrats. You aligned with New Democracy ahead of the May 21 elections, alongside Kammeni, Mr. Antonaros, and all those who have become synonymous with the nation's decline and the far right."

text: Friends. Many important projects I can say for your area, as I will meet next with the local government on the issue of the bridge of Servia, which remains closed, another issue that must be addressed to stop the bisection of the municipality in two. All these problems show that when a region like yours, which is going through what it is going through demographically and economically, is not a priority for the country, then unfortunately the public interest is at risk along with all of you.
rewrite: Friends. I can mention several significant projects for your region, as I will soon meet with local officials regarding the Servia bridge, which remains closed—another matter that must be resolved to prevent the division of the municipality. These issues demonstrate that when an area like yours, facing demographic and economic challenges, is not a national priority, then unfortunately the public good is endangered, along with all of you.

text: And of course, without populism, without grandstanding, respecting public finances. Knowing the real situation of the debt, we propose for pensioners a 1.1 billion cost for those who really need it, and I say the amount so that Mr Mitsotakis's buffoonery that our programme is not cost-effective is over.
rewrite: "And naturally, without resorting to populism or grandstanding, while honoring public finances. With full awareness of the actual debt situation, we are putting forward a 1.1 billion measure for pensioners who are truly in need, and I state this figure to put an end to Mr. Mitsotakis's absurd claim that our program lacks cost-effectiveness."

text: And who wins? The powerful. 150 listed companies have quadrupled their profits in 2022, banks have made billions, having the biggest difference between the interest rate on deposits and the interest rate on mortgages and of course the injustices continue with Mr Mitsotakis' law. The powerful financial players transferred without parental benefit tax up to 4.8 million euros to their children in movable property, real estate and shares.
rewrite: "And emerges victorious? The influential. 150 listed corporations saw their profits quadruple in 2022, with banks earning billions, benefiting from the largest gap between deposit and mortgage interest rates, while inequities persist under Mr. Mitsotakis' legislation. Affluent financiers transferred assets—including securities, real estate, and stocks—worth up to 4.8 million euros to their offspring, exempt from inheritance tax."

text: Cooperatives, small and medium-sized enterprises. We need to legislate in the Greek Parliament. Negotiations should take place as is the case with the banks and not the fund being interested in speculating and making 20%, 30% and then going off to destroy another society and another country. Give priority to the arrangements on the table and not to blackmail and the sudden elimination of the borrower at the table, as has been imposed for eight and a half years by Syriza and New Democracy.
rewrite: Cooperatives and small to medium-sized businesses require legislative action in the Greek Parliament. Negotiations must proceed similarly to those with banks, rather than allowing funds to pursue speculative gains of 20% or 30%, only to then dismantle another society and nation. Priority should be given to the existing proposals on the table, not to coercion or the abrupt exclusion of borrowers, as enforced for eight and a half years by Syriza and New Democracy.

text: Friends. A huge issue is purchasing power and private debt. Do you remember too well the mockery of others? We say simple things like two thousand, ten thousand at the most crucial moment of negotiations with the troika. text: We supported the euro against populism. text: So, dear friends. On 21 May we vote PASOK and PASOK comes out. We are opening a new page for our country, for the young people, for all generations, and that is why we call on the Greek people to make a choice of responsibility, a choice of change and to choose between a state of opacity that exists only as a spoil for the blue children and a state of transparency and respect for institutions and human rights. rewrite: So, dear friends. On May 21st, we vote for PASOK, and PASOK will emerge. We are turning a new page for our nation, for the youth, for every generation. text: Friends, our vision for Greece is grafted from the deep historical and social roots of PASOK. The vision of justice, of reducing inequalities, of a strong welfare state, of education and health care that act as an engine of upward mobility, as in the 1980s, when the child of the farmer and the stockbreeder became a doctor, an engineer and built his life and his family with dignity. rewrite: Comrades, our vision for Greece is rooted in PASOK's profound historical and social foundations. It is a vision of fairness, of narrowing disparities, of a robust welfare system, and of education and healthcare serving as catalysts for social advancement—much like in the 1980s, when the farmer's or herder's child could become a doctor or engineer, building a dignified life and family. This is the promise we must renew for every child in Greece.

text: Just before I close, I would like to say a few words about our national issues and about the refugee migration issue. Refugees are one thing, migration is another. text: The Recovery Fund was made for the pandemic. The pandemic undermined the national health care system. We have a duty to support it, to reduce inequalities, to drive down the cost of living. For that, strong primary health care across the country. For that, 15,000 permanent staff recruitment, for that, pay for doctors and all NHS staff at the European Union average. rewrite: The Recovery Fund was established to address the pandemic's impact. The crisis strained our national health care system. We must bolster it, lessen disparities, and lower living costs. text: Friends, the Prime Minister is completely unable to understand the daily needs of citizens, of people who are struggling to make ends meet until the end of the month. That is why we propose a social reservoir of 150,000 houses in all the major urban centres, especially in Athens and Thessaloniki. So that your children can come and study with dignity. So that young couples can have a family with children. Our first priority is to address the demographic issue.
rewrite: "We, collectively, place the younger generation at the forefront. We assert that if the new generation cannot stand independently, the nation will never stand firm. Hence, as young people worry about living worse than their parents, we are obligated to provide them the means to begin their lives with dignity. This is why we propose a social housing reserve of 150,000 homes across major urban centers, particularly in Athens and Thessaloniki. So your children can pursue their studies with dignity. So young couples can build families with children. Our foremost priority is tackling the demographic challenge."

text: Friends, on 21 May we are forming a new progressive social alliance, a new majority current of progress, hope and responsibility. On 21 May we put an end to the arrogance of Mr Mitsotakis, while turning our backs on the populism of Mr Tsipras, which we have paid dearly for. Next Sunday evening, our political opponents will be surprised on the evening of next Sunday. They will be surprised. Already today they are probably surprised. The celebration of democracy started early, it starts today here in Athens and it will culminate on Sunday evening with the historic resurgence of the democratic movement, of PASOK. PASOK is here united and strong.
rewrite: Friends, on May 21 we are building a fresh, progressive social coalition—a new mainstream of progress, hope, and accountability. On May 21 we halt the arrogance of Mr. Mitsotakis, while rejecting the populism of Mr. Tsipras, for which we have paid a heavy price. This coming Sunday night, our political rivals will be taken by surprise. They will be astonished. In fact, they are likely already surprised. The celebration of democracy has begun early; it starts here in Athens today and will reach its peak on Sunday evening with the historic revival of the democratic movement, of PASOK. PASOK stands here united and strong.

text: The mother, the family, the young mother - who in the difficulties of the present time - knows all too well that by having a family, she prevents the continuation of her economic function, her position, her daily life. We are committed: No child will be left out of daycare, no child will be left out of creative activity centres. Increase the allowance for women freelancers. And of course, a reduction in taxes on families with children. Today, a family without children and a family with children - with children - has 3 tax rate points less. In Portugal the difference is 10%, in Ireland 14% and in Belgium 15%. That is why I am committed to strong tax incentives for young couples with children, to give a real boost to tackling the demographic issue.
rewrite: The mother, the family, the young mother—facing today's hardships—understands all too well that starting a family disrupts her economic role, her status, her daily routine. We pledge: No child excluded from daycare, none left out of creative activity centers. Raise the allowance for women freelancers. And certainly, lower taxes for families with children. Currently, a childless family and a family with children—with children—pays 3 tax rate points less. In Portugal the gap is 10%, in Ireland 14%, and in Belgium 15%. That is why I pledge robust tax incentives for young couples with children, to genuinely advance efforts on the demographic challenge.

text: I can't imagine being convicted 13-0 by the Special Court. And saying justice everywhere and then instead of sending him home I have him on my ballot. I can't imagine. The cover-up. That he took a Greece of the few, which despised the many, where there was no justice, where there was no respect for the individual, where there was discrimination based on religion and political identity, and made it the Greece of all Greeks. This is the great dowry of PASOK. This is the great dowry of the democratic party.

text: In conclusion. I think a resilient economy is very critical. What does this economy mean? It is a preventable one. And not coming in after you've created the problem, doing prevention. What is the big problem of our farmers? Energy, when we could have dealt with it a few years ago with renewables. So, like this summer. We were talking about energy costs, we'll be talking in a few years. This is a given for the cost of using water resources.So to prevent Well this phenomenon, we have prioritized the support of projects related to water resources throughout Greece, so here.
