rewrite: In summary, I believe a resilient economy is crucial. What does this entail? It means focusing on prevention rather than reacting after issues arise. Consider the major challenge for our farmers: energy. We could have addressed this years ago with renewable sources. Just as we discussed energy costs this summer, we will be doing so again in the future. Similarly, the expense of water resource use is inevitable. To mitigate this issue, we have emphasized supporting water-related projects across Greece. For instance, the Filiatrano dam, finished in 2017—six years ago—still lacks tenders for networks covering 35,000 acres. This should be a key priority for the incoming government.

text: Third cost of living point regarding rent, rents have gone through the roof. Funds have come in, they've taken very large properties, estates, they'll do short term rentals, leases, students, they don't go to the big cities because they can't find rent cheap with decent. housing. We say with the Recovery Fund, tax incentives and reconstruction incentives to open closed houses, to create new urban plans, also to bring down the cost of both the market and rent through a pool of 150,000 social housing units in the model of Austria, Spain, Portugal, Italy, Germany. Since they are all doing this because they see how much the cost of living is rising by the skin of their teeth. Why should we not do it too when, because of tourism and because of all these problems with the investments that are being made, which are mostly real estate, we will end up being strangers in our country and a vast hotel This is an injustice.
rewrite: Third cost of living issue concerns rent, which has skyrocketed. Investment funds have entered, acquiring large properties and estates for short-term rentals, leases, or student housing, avoiding major cities where affordable, decent housing is scarce. We propose using the Recovery Fund, along with tax and reconstruction incentives, to reopen shuttered homes and develop new urban plans. This would also reduce market and rental costs by establishing a pool of 150,000 social housing units, following models from Austria, Spain, Portugal, Italy, and Germany. These nations are acting because they acutely feel the rising cost of living. Given tourism and the dominance of real estate investments, we risk becoming strangers in our own country, merely a vast hotel—an injustice we must avoid by taking similar action.

text: Friends. The energy issues are very important, but the institutional issues concerning farmers are also important. In addition to the introduction of the unconditional and tax-free status, subsidies, compensation and aid for farmers, we believe that we need to update the ELGA insurance regulation by extending coverage for disasters to livestock caused by climate change. The Ministry of Rural Development cannot pretend that it does not understand the damage caused by climate change every year. Our farmers and even when the figures say that this year. rewrite: Friends. Energy matters are crucial, yet the institutional concerns affecting farmers are equally vital. text: Friends. May 21 we are fighting a very big fight. A fight that we call on every citizen to make a decision for change. Many of you believe that it is weak, impossible to make again a strong welfare state like the one of the 80s and 90s with a strong NHS with a strong public education. Even more people believe that it is impossible to stop the bureaucracy and the client state. Thousands of young people believe that fair development is impossible and that it is always a game of growth for the few. For the powerful. So give me, on 21 May, the power to make the impossible possible together with all of you, together with all the progressive, democratic people of the country. rewrite: Friends. On May 21, we face a crucial battle. A battle that calls on every citizen to choose change. rewrite: In the realm of public education, which is our foremost concern, we must prepare the youth. Lower tutoring expenses through supplementary teaching. text: So that's why we are proposing a national strategic development plan with a change in the priorities of the Recovery Fund to support domestic production with the creation of new jobs, regional development with the interconnection of tourism, as we said, with all sectors of the Greek economy. rewrite: This is why we propose a national strategic development plan, shifting Recovery Fund priorities to bolster domestic production and generate new jobs, along with regional development by linking tourism to all sectors of Greece's economy. rewrite: Therefore, it is now incumbent upon us, the Democratic Party, to dismantle these antiquated power structures and forge a wide-ranging social coalition for a robust, future-oriented Greece. rewrite: Parental benefits. This is where Mr. Mitsotakis spoke and acted from, from the TIF. Because whatever he declares about the affluent, he implements. text: The prime minister is a liberal. Who has all the orphans of Mr. Karatzaferis in his crucial ministries of government. rewrite: The prime minister claims to be a liberal. Yet, he has placed all the political orphans of Mr. Karatzaferis in his key government ministries. rewrite: Friends, I must emphasize this point. Coming from Agrinio, from Aitoloakarnania, I address the critical issue facing our farmers. rewrite: So who embodies this new political spirit? Should we revisit the Tempe tragedy? What occurred in Tempe? rewrite: Trust signifies justice, yet justice for everyone, not merely for a select few, for those who believe that regardless of their actions, they will never face consequences. rewrite: People remember what the Right stands for. text:

rewrite: My friends, the small and medium-sized enterprises. The government highlights the strong GDP growth post-pandemic, but this stems from consumption and tourism. text: Friends, I cannot, here from Ilia, not refer to the agricultural issues of the whole country. We have said from Trikala that we must support agricultural production. For us, a sustainable development model is not to turn the whole of Greece into a vast hotel, but simply to strengthen tourism by interweaving the agricultural sector, agri-food, livestock farming and processing with all the hordes of tourists who come to Greece every year, otherwise only the entrepreneurs and the islands will benefit at the expense of the production of the rest of the country. A large part of these people to taste Greek products in Greece and then in the next few months to ask for them on the shelves of supermarkets in all the countries of the European Union and thus your products, the processed products to be internationally competitive, boosting exports and creating many good jobs throughout the Greek periphery so that the children of farmers stay here to produce wealth, to make families and finally to deal with the huge demographic issue of the country. rewrite: Friends, I cannot, here in Ilia, avoid addressing the nation's agricultural concerns. We stated in Trikala that we must bolster agricultural output. For us, a sustainable model does not mean transforming all of Greece into one large hotel, but rather enhancing tourism by integrating agriculture, agri-food, livestock, and processing with the many tourists visiting Greece annually. For a significant number of these visitors to sample Greek goods here, and then in the coming months seek them on supermarket shelves across the EU. This will allow farmers' children to remain, creating wealth, building families, and ultimately helping to address the nation's serious demographic challenge. This is a key priority for us. text: Friends. Cost of living. Education. That is a big issue and it's not just universities that many people are talking about it's also primary education that has collapsed in our country. So that's why we have to mainly give a foundation in primary education. I think that the best system we have to follow is a uniform system, which will give a national baccalaureate. So that the national exams are abolished. Every child should choose at their school and take exams there so that it is an informed choice, study and not a choice based on their family's financial ability. The older ones know. The great power of public education in the 80s. That gave the public university the opportunity for the child of the farmer's child of the cattle farmer in Komotini to study to be a doctor, an engineer, a lawyer, to stay at home and raise a family. Today, the cost of living, the cost of studies, the cost of tutorials makes children choose on their computerised form not on the basis of their real ambition sometimes, but on the basis of the financial capacity of the family. The PASOK, this huge social injustice against the younger generation is not tolerated and will stand in the way by completely changing the way of school selection. And of course, remedial teaching in our schools. To reduce inequalities and to reduce tutoring. And strengthening special education structures to truly create an inclusive school.
rewrite: Friends. The cost of living. Education. This is a major issue, and it’s not only universities—primary education in our country has also collapsed. That’s why we must focus on building a strong foundation in primary education. I believe the best approach is a uniform system leading to a national baccalaureate, eliminating national exams. Every child should select and take exams at their own school, ensuring an informed, study-based choice, not one dictated by their family’s financial situation. Older generations remember. The strength of public education in the 80s allowed a farmer’s child in Komotini to become a doctor, engineer, or lawyer, while staying close to home and family. Today, living costs, tuition, and private tutoring often force young people to pick paths based on family finances rather than true ambition. PASOK will not tolerate this profound social injustice toward the younger generation and will intervene by overhauling school selection. We will also introduce remedial teaching in schools to lessen inequalities and reduce reliance on tutoring, while strengthening special education to build genuinely inclusive schools.

text: Friends, as I said before, for us demography is the great national issue. But it is not solved by benefits that do not even arrive in the first week of the month. We are providing comprehensive solutions of a strong welfare state. For young couples, the priority is to bring down the cost of living. What are the inelastic costs? First, rent. Rents have been galloping in recent years. So we propose to do what is happening in Portugal, Spain, Italy, Italy, Germany and Austria. That is, to have a pool of social housing, either newly built from the Recovery Fund, or with tax and reconstruction criteria with zero ENVAT to be included in the pool and rented for 15 years at a very low rent to your children and grandchildren to have families. This is a programme that does not create citizen-customers, like Mr Mitsotakis's programme, where very few people can take advantage of low-interest loans, but it is a programme that is used by 150,000 families and at the same time, through competition, it brings down rents overall in all the urban centres of the country.
rewrite: Friends, as I have previously stated, demography is our paramount national challenge. Yet it cannot be addressed through benefits that vanish before the month even begins. We are advancing holistic solutions befitting a robust welfare state. For young couples, the foremost aim is to reduce living costs. What are the fixed, unavoidable expenses? First, housing. Rents have been soaring in recent years. Therefore, we propose to follow the example set in Portugal, Spain, Italy, Germany, and Austria. That is, to establish a social housing stock—either newly constructed with Recovery Fund resources, or integrated through tax and renovation incentives with zero VAT—to be part of this pool and leased for 15 years at minimal rates, enabling your children and grandchildren to start families. This initiative does not produce citizen-consumers, unlike Mr. Mitsotakis's scheme, which offers low-interest loans accessible to only a handful. Instead, it is a program that serves 150,000 families and, through market competition, lowers rents across all urban centers in the country.

text: Also central to our commitment to young people is our social housing programme. Rents are soaring in all urban centres. Mr Mitsotakis has made a programme, we have just started talking about social housing, which does not give low-rent houses, it gives low-interest loans to buy a house based on the price per square metre. rewrite: Also central to our dedication to youth is our social housing initiative. Rents are skyrocketing in every city. Mr. Mitsotakis has proposed a plan—we have only begun discussing social housing—that does not provide low-rent homes but offers low-interest loans for purchasing property based on square meter prices. Once you can support yourself independently, you move out and another takes your place, so this will assist not just 150,000 young couples but hundreds of thousands of Greeks suffering under the cost of living. text: I will tell you some policies today. These are mainly for the younger generation, but not only for the younger generation. Which are in our programme. But before I go. To the political issues. rewrite: Today, I will outline several policies. These primarily target the younger generation, though not exclusively. They are part of our program. text: I must admit that I find it difficult to understand what is going on with the Prime Minister, his arrogance had been noticed and had long ceased to surprise me.His lack of empathy was also something I had spotted and I was not at all surprised by his inability to identify with public sentiment and one or stand up for the problems facing the Greek people.What has always impressed me is the ease with which he distorts reality and underestimates our intelligence. The figures used by all the governments of the western world. But what leaves me stunned is his behaviour in the wiretapping scandal. From Rhodes he addressed his friends of PASOK to all of you, saying that we have moved elsewhere and I am taking you elsewhere.Who is saying this? rewrite: I must confess, I struggle to comprehend the Prime Minister's conduct. His arrogance has been evident for some time and no longer shocks me. His absence of empathy was also apparent, and I was hardly surprised by his failure to connect with public feeling or to address the issues confronting the Greek populace. What consistently astounds me is the facility with which he twists the truth and belittles our discernment. Each day, Kyriakos Mitsotakis increasingly resembles Mr. Tsipras. I did not anticipate him rivaling him in falsehoods, even casting doubt on the official OECD statistics—figures utilized by every government in the Western world. Yet what truly leaves me speechless is his conduct regarding the wiretapping affair. From Rhodes, he spoke to his PASOK associates, to all of you, claiming we have progressed and he is leading you forward. Who is declaring this? The man who began 2019 championing a modern administrative state and concluded by presiding over a shadow administrative entity? The master of no-bid contracts? The exemplar of corruption? The leader of temporary staff funded by your taxes?

text: Also, why when farmers take to the streets because the New Democracy government condemned them to poverty. The communists were again in front, demanding measures for their survival in the villages.
rewrite: Moreover, when farmers protest in the streets due to the New Democracy government driving them into poverty, the communists once more lead the charge, calling for actions to ensure their survival in rural areas.

text: To be fair. This was the case in previous years as well.Because you can't say. In PASOK you are selling off the OSE. For 200-400 million euros, but then give it away at a minimum price? And endowing the Italians with 250 million euros from the barren lines.And making an independent authority where you put people seconded from unrelated departments, with the result that there is no control over the trains. I want to stimulate the memory, not just to remember the tragedy, but to understand why our state is not changing, because we don't take the lessons of history, we skip everything easily, while we can imitate the best practices of other European countries and create a normal state that guarantees the public interest, where Greek children will finally feel secure and have a perspective. rewrite: To be fair, this was also true in past years. You cannot claim that in PASOK you are selling OSE for 200-400 million euros, only to practically give it away at a minimal price? And then grant the Italians 250 million euros from the unprofitable lines. You establish an independent authority staffed by people transferred from unrelated departments, leading to a lack of oversight over the trains. You sign a telecommunications contract without a single euro of Greek funding, relying entirely on European money. And you approve seven extensions under both SYRIZA and New Democracy. I mention this because we have suddenly forgotten the tragedy of Tempe. How quickly we forget. I aim to jog our memory, not just to recall the tragedy, but to grasp why our state remains unchanged—because we fail to learn from history, we gloss over everything too easily, even though we could adopt the best practices of other European nations and build a functional state that safeguards the public interest, where Greek children can finally feel secure and have prospects. This is our grand vision: a state that will ensure that guarantee. A society of equality and justice, offering opportunities for the young. How else will they remain in Greece? To start families, to stand on their own feet. Unless this state operates on principles different from the current ones.

text: Therefore, apart from the energy costs, we have to deal in a redemptive way with the precariousness of the rural world. rewrite: Thus, beyond energy expenses, we must address the vulnerability of rural areas in a restorative manner. This is precisely why we propose zero excise duty on agricultural inputs, animal feed, fuel, and agricultural oil for the entire crisis period. Naturally, while aiming to prioritize ELGA's issues, we advocate updating the ELGA Insurance Regulation to extend coverage for livestock and crop losses due to climate change. This summer is set to be among the most severe on record. text: On this waterfront in July 2021, at the events of the KNE, thousands of young people, together with the people of the island, we sent the message that the friendship of the peoples will win, that in Greece and Turkey the enemy is the same, NATO -Governments and capitalism. rewrite: In July 2021, on this waterfront, during the KNE events, thousands of youth and the island’s residents together declared that the friendship between peoples will prevail—that in Greece and Turkey, the common enemy is the same: the NATO-backed governments and capitalism. That socialism, a future free from crises, wars, and refugees, is worth fighting for. text: Friends, compañeras and comrades, the Southwest calls on the people to vote for it in order to continue for another four years its unpopular work. rewrite: Friends, compañeras and comrades, the Southwest urges the public to grant it another four years to persist in its widely disliked efforts. text: The left that is at the heart and soul of the democratic party is the rule of law, respect for human rights and the separation of powers. PASOK is here, comrades. Are the ones who shouted Hangmen in the Constitution and compared the elected Prime Minister of the country, George Papandreou, with Pinochet, the dictator of Chile, progressive forces? Or was it? rewrite: The democratic party's core principles are the rule of law, human rights, and the separation of powers. PASOK is present, comrades. Friends, PASOK is here to welcome the progressive Left, the progressive centre, and the hopes of all democratic citizens, moving beyond discord and the toxic disputes that are hindering our nation's future. But what defines progressive forces, reflecting on recent events? Are those who cried "Hangmen" in the Constitution and likened the elected Prime Minister, George Papandreou, to Chile's dictator Pinochet truly progressive? Or was it? Or are they progressive forces who, in the '15 election, urged people not to repay loans, promising stubbornness? They also declared no house should be held by a banker, yet introduced electronic auctions, reduced first home protections, and sold billions in red loans in '15 to exploit the most vulnerable. The vultures of the funds. This is the Left, and Mr. Tsipras' progress here is the Left that safeguards the first home. This is the Left that obstructs the de-fellatinisation of the Greek economy.

text: Friends, compañeras and compañeros. We are proud of the attitude of our comrades over the years on the island. rewrite: Friends, compañeras and compañeros. We take pride in the stance our comrades have shown over the years on the island. text: It is on the basis of this law and the objectives that derive from it that all the parties that have governed to date and want to serve this system again from governmental positions formulate their programmes. rewrite: It is according to this law and the aims that stem from it that every party which has governed so far and seeks to serve this system once more from government roles crafts its platform. This explains why all their programs feature bold slogans like: "green growth," market liberalization, fiscal balance, banking system stability, and more. text: The magnificent mobilisations and strikes of March, with the basic demand that the responsibilities for the crime of Tempi should not be covered up, the thousands of young mouths shouting "PASOK - SYRIZA - New Democracy, this crime has a history", record a dynamic that must not be broken. rewrite: The powerful mobilizations and strikes in March, centered on the demand that accountability for the Tempi crime not be concealed, along with the thousands of young voices declaring "PASOK - SYRIZA - New Democracy, this crime has a history," mark a momentum that must not be lost. Instead, it must intensify, expand, and evolve into an organized movement of resistance. The drive for this can only come from a significantly strengthened KKE in the May 21 elections.

text: It proves that the democratic party, the historic movement founded by Andreas Papandreou, has once again become a leading player in the political scene of the country. A short while ago, Mr Mitsotakis. Giving an interview to a television channel, he said that I have a personal problem with him. rewrite: This demonstrates that the democratic party, the historic movement established by Andreas Papandreou, has regained its role as a key force in the nation's political landscape. Recently, Mr. Mitsotakis, in a television interview, claimed I hold a personal grievance against him. The matter, Mr. Mitsotakis, is not about any personal issue with you. The reality for you is that, ahead of May 21, millions of Greeks have a personal grievance with your policies. For Mr. Mitsotakis and his communications team, every campaign day resembles April Fools' Day. In all my interviews and those of our entire staff, we have unequivocally stated there is no possibility of a coalition with Mr. Varoufakis' party and those who gambled the country on the drachma. rewrite: Beware! Do not be deceived! Not one of them claims they will halt this! They all assume it as a given, since, according to Mr. Tsipras, auctions occur in every privileged nation!

rewrite: Then, roughly a month back, the KKE joined thousands of French workers in Paris's Bastille Square to sing "The Internationale." text: So let us now look to the future. Why PASOK? Beyond our history and the struggles of yesterday in the proud struggles. And I am really touched to see here the generations of 114 and the founding of 1974, the generations that in the difficult years stayed with the party and kept it alive so that we can take it in our hands and make it great again. To the next. In the next election, friends. In the next election. We have commitments. The specific commitments. Commitments that make people's lives better. That turn the page. So that's why I'm talking about programmatic convergences. It is not a novelty, in most countries in Europe there are coalition governments. But it is not an exchange of ministries. rewrite: Let us now turn our gaze forward. Why PASOK? Beyond our past and the proud battles of yesterday. I am deeply moved to see here the generations from 114 and the founding in 1974, those who stood by the party through hard times and sustained it, so we could take it up and restore its greatness. Onward. In the coming election, friends. In the coming election. We have pledges. Clear pledges. Pledges that improve lives. That mark a new beginning. This is why I speak of programmatic alignments. It is not new; across Europe, coalition governments are common. But it is not a mere exchange of ministries. It is no longer backroom power-sharing, but agreements on policy. Indeed, Tsipras. Now he favors that idea. Why does he see no path alone? And he says the very German social democrats he scorned months ago for partnering with the CDU are now admirable. So we discuss programmatic agreements and convergence at the forefront. The top priority is the cost of living. That is why we must construct a new welfare state. The heaviest costs today are healthcare and education. Rent, daily essential expenses.

text: So we come to solve the issue of the NHS. How? But the Recovery Fund was not for many reasons, it was for health, the green transition, digital convergence. Those were the priorities of the Recovery Fund that was done because of the pandemic. Europe gave 32 billion to Greece because of the pandemic. Of the 32, 21 of them were subsidies. What did the other countries do? It's not just the Greek public health system that has a problem. The Portuguese gave 8%, the Italians 11%, we gave 2% for services and another 2% for the energy upgrade of buildings. This is Mr Mitsotakis's belief in the public social good of health care, and we will stand in the way of the privatisation of health care that will further impoverish the weakest Greeks. That is why I am committing from the Recovery Fund 8 to 10% of the resources to go to the NHS. Second commitment, strong primary health care throughout Greece, an extensive network in every city, in every village to have services close to the citizen for the citizen, when a country has such issues of an ageing population and of course staffing of the NHS. Financial incentives for all health professionals to keep our doctors in Greece and not to travel to Germany, Belgium and France. And of course, let us end the mockery of heavy and unhealthy work. I pledge after the elections as a government to include all our health workers in the heavy and unhealthy so that they have real solutions and not the applause of the mockery.
rewrite: We now address the NHS issue. How? The Recovery Fund, established due to the pandemic, was allocated for health, green transition, and digital convergence—these were its priorities. Europe provided Greece with 32 billion; of this, 21 billion were subsidies. What did other nations do? The problem isn't unique to Greek public health. Portugal allocated 8%, Italy 11%, while we dedicated 2% to services and another 2% to building energy upgrades. This reflects Mr. Mitsotakis's commitment to public healthcare as a social good, and we will oppose privatisation that would further impoverish vulnerable Greeks. Hence, I pledge to direct 8–10% of Recovery Fund resources to the NHS. Second, ensure robust primary healthcare across Greece—an extensive network in every city and village to bring services closer to citizens, addressing challenges like an ageing population and NHS staffing. Offer financial incentives to retain health professionals in Greece, preventing their departure to Germany, Belgium, and France. Finally, end the farce of arduous and unhealthy work conditions. I vow that after the elections, our government will classify all health workers under heavy and unhealthy work provisions, securing tangible solutions rather than empty applause.

text: And of course, the seismicity. The well-known seismicity was also coming here all over Greece, in '12, '13, '14, and it was saying you owe, don't pay. I'm coming to bring the seismicity. rewrite: "And naturally, the seismic activity. The widely recognized seismic activity was also arriving across Greece, in '12, '13, '14, and it declared you owe, do not repay. text: For us. The real qualitative development will be when we don't have a vision of Greece becoming a vast hotel, but when we have a vision of tourism working with agri-food, with manufacturing and that the profits that they have on the islands and in specific parts of Greece are shared by farmers and livestock farmers throughout Greece. This is a real model of European development that benefits all the Greek people. Also, the foreign investment business says for foreign investment. rewrite: For us, genuine qualitative progress will come not from envisioning Greece as one vast hotel, but from seeing tourism collaborate with agriculture, food production, and manufacturing, ensuring that profits generated on the islands and in specific regions are distributed among farmers and livestock producers across all of Greece. This represents a true European development model that serves all Greeks. Additionally, regarding foreign investment, truly productive foreign investment accounts for only 14% of the total, with the remainder tied to real estate and exports from existing Greek companies. Thus, the question for Mr. Mitsotakis is unavoidable: Who has gained from these policy decisions? Certainly not Greek households, whose disposable income has shrunk under price pressures. It is revealing that 30% of Greeks now face poverty and social exclusion, according to official Eurostat data, while inequalities have grown alarmingly. Consequently, small and medium-sized enterprises have not benefited from the favorable low-interest loans of the Recovery Fund, which are largely managed by banks and, as per figures from two months ago, have provided 1.1 billion at a 1.2% interest rate to just 67 enterprises, leaving thousands of SMEs excluded. This is why we argue that the Recovery Fund should be directed with incentives toward this vast segment of small and medium-sized businesses.

text: I wonder who is more humanistic? The one who has the record for incarceration or the one who has the record for building hot spots? rewrite: "Who truly embodies humanism? The one with the highest incarceration rates or the one who constructs the most detention centers? The architect of the Moria camp or the one who expanded it? Our response is: Neither. Each has fully enacted the European Union's regressive policies. All have served NATO, an entity that both wages war and generates refugees while disregarding borders. text: Friends, education is what the Greek people need. Dignity in public education too. The centre of gravity today is not the school, the high school and the lyceum, but the tutorials. rewrite: Friends, the Greek people require education. Public education must also uphold dignity. Today, the focus is not on schools, high schools, or lyceums, but on private tutoring. We must stop this, as it places a huge burden on Greek families. What is our proposal? We implement the National Baccalaureate, similar to other European nations, so that public schools become the priority for youth, not tutorials. There will be no family anxiety or student distress. rewrite: "Indeed, comrades, the South-West region tallied its profits and setbacks throughout the pandemic period. text: The "grey zones" have been enlarged to "Blue Homeland". Not only do we have violations, but also overflights over Greek islands, which have resumed after the earthquakes. Treaties defining borders are being challenged.  From here, from the island of Lesvos, from the northeastern Aegean, we want to denounce once again that this unacceptable claim is being made on the back of NATO, which does not recognise borders in the Aegean. It has the support of the USA and the EU, which "put their economic and political interests in Turkey in the balance". In other words, all those who are drinking water in their name and have the audacity to present them as guarantors of sovereign rights.
rewrite: The "grey zones" have expanded into the "Blue Homeland." We are witnessing not only violations but also renewed overflights above Greek islands, which resumed following the earthquakes. Agreements that establish borders are now being contested. From here, from Lesvos, from the northeastern Aegean, we must once more condemn this unacceptable claim, advanced under NATO's cover—an entity that does not acknowledge Aegean borders. It is backed by the USA and the EU, who "weigh their economic and political interests in Turkey on the scales." In short, all those who profit in their name yet dare to portray themselves as defenders of sovereign rights.

text: Friends, Compañeras and Compañeros, On the basis of recent experience, we put the honest question to the workers, the youth, all our people: Can the satisfaction of our modern needs be realized within a system based and operated on the law of voracious profit? It is this law that characterizes as a cost the wages, the insurance of those without whose work no good, no service is produced. It is the same law that considers life and health protection measures to be costs, that broke up 57 families recently in Tempe, that is responsible for the dozens of employer crimes in sectors and workplaces, that wipes out working-class families.
rewrite:
Comrades, Friends, and Fellow Workers,  
Given recent events, we pose a sincere question to laborers, young people, and all our citizens: Can the demands of contemporary life be met under a system founded and driven by the rule of insatiable profit? This very rule treats wages and benefits for those whose labor creates every product and service as mere expenses. It is the same rule that views safeguards for life and health as costs, that shattered 57 families in Tempe not long ago, that is to blame for countless employer violations across industries and worksites, and that devastates working-class households.

text: A battle between two worlds separated by an abyss. A battle between real progress and regression. It is through such heroic moments that the concept of progress has been imprinted in the collective memory and consciousness of our people, that is to say, the concept of an unswerving and unyielding struggle, even against the most difficult correlation of forces, but which always proves that the impossible can become possible and can win! This is the progress that our people know, the open-minded, progressive, left-wing people who live in Kaisariani, Kokkinia, Peristeri, in every popular neighbourhood of Attica and all of Greece.
rewrite: A conflict between two realms divided by a chasm. A clash between genuine advancement and retreat. It is in these valiant moments that the idea of progress has been etched into the collective memory and awareness of our nation—the notion of a steadfast and resolute fight, even against the most daunting odds, yet one that consistently demonstrates that the impossible can be made possible and can triumph! This is the progress our people recognize, the broad-minded, forward-thinking, left-leaning citizens residing in Kaisariani, Kokkinia, Peristeri, in every working-class district of Attica and across all of Greece.

text: And since spring is well and truly here and the notorious "hard winter" is over, let's see: Was it hard for everyone? This year, listed companies on the stock exchange will distribute their largest dividends to their major shareholders since 2009. And with very little taxation, since SYRIZA took it from 15% to 10% and ND from 10% to 5%. Banks, respectively, posted pre-tax profits of €4.5 billion, while a number of energy and oil monopolies are showing historic profitability performances with over €1 billion in one year. All this and more is their common agenda. So while they chase the investment grade, the people and youth have a vested interest: To raise to a higher rank their solidarity with the KKE, their struggle for their own needs and rights.
rewrite: Now that spring has fully arrived and the infamous "hard winter" has passed, let's consider: Was it truly difficult for all? This year, stock market-listed firms are set to pay out their biggest dividends to key shareholders since 2009, with minimal tax burdens—SYRIZA reduced rates from 15% to 10%, and ND from 10% to 5%. Meanwhile, banks reported pre-tax earnings of €4.5 billion, and several energy and oil monopolies are achieving record profits, exceeding €1 billion annually. These outcomes align with their shared objectives. Thus, as they pursue investment-grade status, the public and youth have a crucial stake: elevating their solidarity with the KKE and intensifying their fight for personal needs and rights.

text: Friends. Many generations have trusted PASOK over the years to make change possible and we want to make this change possible on 21 May with a state of dignity and perspective. I heard Mr Mitsotakis in the debate, in very simple terms, say that my monitoring. He does not say it had to be done because I was never a national danger. Of course, the New Democracy cadres what they were saying on TV, what I was writing on the Internet, what agents of China, Turkey, Armenia and various other such nonsense. But Mr Mitsotakis, with what he said. What is he implying? That surveillance is an act which creates a new situation for justice. The argument of legal surveillance, but politically incorrect, has now collapsed. We need the judiciary to do its job well and I expect it to call the prosecutor of the NIS, Mrs. Vasiliki Vlachou, who is in debt as a national danger to legalize my surveillance in between the democratic elections of PASOK. We will be the party that will guarantee the end of this institutional decline. The people do not forget what right-wing means, what maintenance means. And we have a duty to fight to prove that this party, with its rebirth, will show who the real opponent of the new democracy is. And certainly not the sponsors of the new democracy.
rewrite: Friends. For many generations, PASOK has been trusted to enable change, and we aim to realize this change on May 21 with a state of dignity and vision. In the debate, I heard Mr. Mitsotakis state very plainly that I was monitored. He does not admit it was necessary, as I was never a threat to the nation. Naturally, New Democracy members spoke on TV about what I posted online, labeling me an agent of China, Turkey, Armenia, and other such absurdities. Yet with his words, Mr. Mitsotakis implies something: that surveillance establishes a new precedent for justice. The defense of lawful but politically improper monitoring has now crumbled. The judiciary must perform its duty effectively, and I anticipate it will summon the NIS prosecutor, Mrs. Vasiliki Vlachou, who is obligated as a national security concern to justify my surveillance during PASOK’s democratic elections. We will be the party that ensures an end to this institutional decay. The public remembers what the right wing represents, what preservation entails. It is our responsibility to struggle and demonstrate that this party, through its renewal, will reveal the true adversary of New Democracy. And that is decidedly not the backers of New Democracy.

text: That is why, as our people say, the children of the caring ones cook before they are hungry. In this case, the children of the caretakers vote for the JCP! To terrorize the terrorists, so that we can fight our battles from better positions! To stop them, to win victories, to finally pave the way for the radical changes we all long for.
rewrite: That is why, as our people say, the children of the thoughtful prepare their meals before hunger strikes. Here, the children of the guardians cast their votes for the JCP! To strike fear into the terrorists, enabling us to wage our struggles from stronger ground! To halt them, to secure triumphs, to ultimately clear the path for the profound transformations we all deeply desire.

text: Friends. But history is not only to remember, it is also to compare, to compare who has contributed and who has harmed. We then. In the face of these great changes that our country needs, we say remember what happened in 2010. More recently of these great changes, because I hear some people say that the new democracy and Mitsotakis was, he says always on the right side of history. And so I say here from Chania, if in 2010. PASOK MPs had followed the vote of Tsipras and Mitsotakis. Greece today was in the euro or in the drachma and if Mr. Mitsotakis does not remember, let him ask his sister who voted against him so that the country does not go to the drachma can not play with the memory and intelligence of the Greek people. The Greek people are not lotus eaters, Mr Mitsotakis, and they remember both the zappias and the anti-memoranda. And of the mockery to get the chair of power. rewrite: Friends. Yet history is not merely for recollection; it is also for comparison, to weigh who has served and who has damaged. We, then. Confronting these profound shifts our nation requires, we declare: recall the events of 2010. More recently, amid these great transformations, because I hear some claim that the new democracy and Mitsotakis have always stood on history's right side. Thus, I state here from Chania: if in 2010, PASOK MPs had aligned with the votes of Tsipras and Mitsotakis, would Greece today be in the euro or the drachma? And if Mr. Mitsotakis forgets, let him consult his sister who opposed him to keep the country from the drachma—one cannot trifle with the memory and intellect of the Greek people. The Greek people are not lotus-eaters, Mr. Mitsotakis; they recall both the betrayals and the anti-memorandum struggles. And the mockery to seize the seat of authority. Only the democratic party held the correct stance of governance. Only the one who shouldered the patriotic duty and prevented the nation from becoming another Argentina, averting a staggering collapse.

text: Today, there is a solution to build a very safe and modern network in all transport so that we do not have to live tragedies like this crime in the tempi that brought thousands of people, thousands of young people to the streets and squares here in Lamia under the slogan "their profits or our lives".
rewrite: Today, there exists a means to establish a highly secure and contemporary network across all transportation systems, ensuring we avoid tragedies akin to this crime at Tempi, which mobilized thousands, including many youths, into the streets and squares of Lamia under the rallying cry "their profits or our lives."

text: Because also when the government of the New Democracy discovered as the only means of protection in fires, not the fire-fighting means, not the prevention measures, not the necessary recruitment of personnel, but 112, the people and the firefighters and the people fought together with the firefighters and the people to create firebreaks, to stop the devastation. The people were fighting to save themselves.
rewrite: Since the New Democracy government identified 112 as the sole protective measure against fires—rather than firefighting resources, preventive actions, or adequate staffing—the public, alongside firefighters, united to establish firebreaks and halt the destruction. text: So, in front of us, Mr Mitsotakis is hiding what is coming as a side effect of his own political choices and on the other hand, Mr Tsipras, unrepentant, like in '15, is saying things that he cannot implement by deceiving, attempting to deceive once again the citizens. Friends, what does Mr Mitsotakis say? Give him, he says, self-reliance to raise the minimum wage to EUR 950 and the average wage to EUR 1 500. But he has nothing to say about where Greece is today, where Greece is with his government. The minimum wage, according to the OECD figures, which he despises, which he does not consider reliable. I have never heard a prime minister of a western country who does not consider the OECD figures to be reliable. We cannot listen, Mr Mitsotakis, only to the parroting of New Democracy in the media. Indeed, let us listen to an international organisation. The minimum wage, the real minimum wage, has fallen by 40%. The indirect taxes you paid in 2022 were two-thirds of total state revenues. Greek households are third from the bottom of the European Union in purchasing power. But watch out. And while all this is happening for the middle class and the poorest Greeks, 150 listed companies quadrupled their profits in 2022 unchecked, taking advantage of the energy crisis. It also does not mention that the public debt has increased by 50 billion and the trade deficit - and this is the most important thing because this is why we entered the memoranda - is the largest trade deficit since 2010, since Greece entered the memoranda.
rewrite: So, before us, Mr. Mitsotakis conceals the consequences stemming from his own policy decisions, while Mr. Tsipras, unapologetic as in 2015, makes promises he cannot keep, trying once more to mislead the public. Friends, what is Mr. Mitsotakis claiming? He asks for trust to increase the minimum wage to €950 and the average wage to €1,500. Yet he avoids addressing Greece's current state under his leadership. The minimum wage, based on OECD data he dismisses as unreliable—I have never heard a Western leader question OECD credibility. We cannot, Mr. Mitsotakis, just echo New Democracy's media lines. Let's instead heed an international body: the real minimum wage has dropped by 40%. Indirect taxes in 2022 made up two-thirds of state revenue. Greek households rank third lowest in EU purchasing power. But note this: while the middle class and poorest suffer, 150 listed firms saw profits quadruple in 2022, unchecked amid the energy crisis. He also omits that public debt rose by €50 billion, and the trade deficit—the key reason for the memoranda—is the largest since 2010, when Greece entered them.

text: As for what Mr Tsipras says about the 5-10 MPs he may be missing and the rest is the most agonistic expression of politics, it is political commerce and if progressive people had a thousand reasons today to turn their backs on him, the way Syriza is politicking is another reason. We remind Mr Tsipras that in the past, when he was short of MPs to pass the third memorandum, he found them in the MPs of the ND and PASOK. That is where he can look for them today. And if he wants to see who is paving the way for the Mitsotakis government, he should look at himself in the mirror, since his party, SYRIZA, supported the central choices of the Mitsotakis government and his own forces are making a compromise with the forces of ND and PASOK in municipalities, trade unions and in the GSEE.
rewrite: Regarding Mr. Tsipras's remarks on the 5-10 MPs he may lack and the rest being the most contentious form of politics, this is political bargaining. If progressive individuals already had numerous reasons to reject him today, Syriza's political maneuvering adds another. We recall to Mr. Tsipras that previously, when he needed MPs to pass the third memorandum, he secured them from ND and PASOK. That is where he can seek them now. And if he wishes to identify who is facilitating the Mitsotakis government, he should examine his own reflection, as his party, SYRIZA, has backed key decisions of the Mitsotakis administration, and his own allies are aligning with ND and PASOK in local governments, unions, and the GSEE.

text: Friends, but the elephant in the room is Turkey, let's be honest. We want a stable neighbouring country, but we also need a unified European foreign policy, a policy based on respect for international law and not a policy that coddles Turkey, making it feel unchecked and unconstrained. But the Greek borders are not only Greek, they are also Euro-Turkish, and I think it is unfair that we Greeks should pay billions of euros to guard our borders and those of the rest of Europe. It is a huge disadvantage for the rule of law, sorry for the welfare state, when we give billions for armaments, something that the Danes, the Dutch, the Germans and other central Europeans do not do. What needs to be done? I have said it many times. Unified armaments. The European army, like Frontex, which guards the Greek borders, has become a European army, just as the Europeans have to put their hand in their pockets and for the fence on the Evros, they have to put their hand deep in their pockets to pay for the guarding of the Greek-Turkish border. And let them learn a lesson from the events in Ukraine. It is unfair for the Greek people to pay billions in armaments without co-productions, without the prospect of a common defence and foreign policy.
rewrite: Friends, but let's address the obvious issue: Turkey. We desire a stable neighbor, yet we also require a cohesive European foreign policy—one grounded in respect for international law, not one that indulges Turkey, allowing it to act without restraint. However, the Greek borders are not solely Greek; they are also Europe's borders with Turkey. I believe it is unjust that we Greeks must spend billions of euros to protect our borders and those of the rest of Europe. This is a significant detriment to the rule of law, and regrettably to the welfare state, when we allocate billions for military spending—something the Danes, the Dutch, the Germans, and other central Europeans do not do. What is the solution? I have stated it repeatedly: unified armaments. The European army, similar to Frontex which secures the Greek borders, should evolve into a true European force. Just as Europeans must contribute financially for the fence on the Evros, they must also dig deep into their pockets to fund the protection of the Greek-Turkish border. Moreover, let them take a lesson from the situation in Ukraine. It is unfair for the Greek people to bear the cost of billions in armaments without joint productions or the promise of a shared defense and foreign policy.

text: Tourism should become a right and a bridge of real friendship, acquaintance and cooperation between peoples. That is why we are on the road to confrontation with the real opponent, the one that all the other parties hide because they serve it, the inhuman system of exploitation.
rewrite: Tourism must be established as a right and a genuine bridge of friendship, understanding, and cooperation among peoples. This is precisely why we are confronting the true adversary—the one concealed by all other parties because they serve it—the inhumane system of exploitation.

rewrite: On the same cost-benefit balance, however, across the nation and here in Lesvos, the essential civil protection and recovery efforts for those impacted are also being weighed. This is why Vrissa remains deserted and hazardous, neglected by two governments, as earthquake survivors were forced to spend heavily from their own savings to reconstruct their houses, with many relocating elsewhere on the island. In this area, members and associates of the KKE, alongside farmers and young people, were combating the blazes with the scarce firefighters, who themselves highlighted shortages both prior to and after the fire.

rewrite:
Friends. To conclude. I wish to express my deepest gratitude for your attendance here today. I want you to understand that the struggle I am undertaking aims to show your children and the younger generations that we are not all alike. Regarding these commitments, are they set in stone? If not, is it merely some partisan pride? It is because I believe we must bring our people together and not let the right and Syriza split them over the smallest issue. If a nuclear accident were to occur in Ukraine—knock on wood—would Tsipras and Mitsotakis be at odds? PASOK's role is finished. Back in 2011, it began in Evros with the fence; Tsipras and Mitsotakis argued, and because they argued, SYRIZA dismantled it. No, because one of them, the New Democracy officials, claimed we were doing it to guide the public, the memoranda, while others said the European taxpayer was mistaken to fund it. So what does Syriza desire? That the Greek people should bear the cost of securing Europe's borders with billions in arms, which the Greek Parliament did not approve for our border protection, and that Europeans should not pay, even though these are European borders.  
Why am I mentioning this? We do not engage in populism. We do not toy with emotions or issues.

text: Now, you see, they are selling an election fairy tale to the Greek people that from 2015 to 2019 it was the Troika alone that ruled and not Syriza... But then, how can they be proud of what they were legislating? But their audacity knows no bounds...that is, almost 150 years after the uprising of the Chicago workers, who gave their blood to secure the 8-hour work week, to work as many hours as they worked in 1870 and with a mongoose in hand and this is considered "modern"!
rewrite: Now, they are peddling an election myth to the Greek public, claiming that from 2015 to 2019, it was solely the Troika in charge, not Syriza... Yet, how can they take pride in the laws they enacted? Their boldness is truly limitless...nearly 150 years after the Chicago workers' uprising, where blood was shed to win the 8-hour workday, they advocate working as many hours as in 1870, with a mongoose in hand, and call this "modern"!

text: After the elections, the banks, the crows of the funds, the various Patsis and all the others to whom ND, SYRIZA and PASOK have handed over the red loans of the people for a plate of lentils will continue to auction off houses and to squeeze people's families.
rewrite: Following the elections, the banks, the vultures of finance, the various profiteers, and all those to whom ND, SYRIZA, and PASOK have surrendered the people's non-performing loans for a pittance will persist in foreclosing homes and pressuring families.

rewrite: We will also remember the effort to prosecute elected representatives and other activists, including members of the KKE, our candidate who heads the workers' center, and the secretary of the Federation of Agricultural Associations, for allegedly "urging the people to halt." It is disgraceful that no party aside from the KKE has spoken out to protect those who acted on behalf of the people of Lesbos from being targeted. It has been shown that the people rescue the people in tough and extraordinary times, when the state reveals its antagonistic stance in this manner as well.

text: We also have a duty to talk about young people and social housing, and here in Patras thousands of young people, thousands of young couples cannot find cheap housing. Rents with dignity and housing with dignity. That is why we have announced a programme of 150,000 social housing units, either newly built to the Recovery Fund or with tax incentives and incentives for reconstruction. We are opening up old homes with zero VAT. Sorry zero VAT are put into the social pool and rented out for the next 15 years at low cost to 150,000 couples. What is the difference between our programme and the one announced by the new Republic? Mr Mitsotakis. He gives new home ownership with low-cost loans. What do we say; say to a house with dignity, with low cost and when you get on your feet we will give it to another Greek, because that is how we escalate the cost of living for hundreds of thousands and for more than a generation. rewrite: We must also address the issue of youth and social housing. Here in Patras, thousands of young individuals and couples struggle to find affordable homes. They need dignified rents and dignified housing. That is why we have launched a program for 150,000 social housing units, either newly constructed through the Recovery Fund or through tax incentives and support for renovations. We are revitalizing older properties with zero VAT—apologies, zero VAT—to add them to the social housing pool, renting them at low cost to 150,000 couples for the next 15 years. How does our plan differ from the one announced by the New Democracy party under Mr. Mitsotakis? He offers new home ownership through low-cost loans. What is our approach? We provide dignified housing at low cost, and once you are back on your feet, we pass it on to another Greek citizen. This is how we tackle the cost of living for hundreds of thousands, benefiting more than a single generation. This is proactive governance—not treating citizens as mere customers, as Mr. Mitsotakis’s New Democracy intends. Their plan is impractical because home purchase costs are so high that very few can meet the requirements of his proposed program.

text: Friends, From here, from the blood-soaked shooting range of Kaisariani, where 79 years ago, on May Day 1944, 200 communists fled with their heads held high, their eyes proudly fixed on the barrels of their Nazi executioners, we commemorate this year's Labour Day. And we pledge that we will continue on their path, that we will never betray their sacrifice, so that better days will finally dawn for our country and our people that they too craved. The river of blood that watered the wall of Caesarian that day, the human corpse that roasted "just one manly stature" after each Nazi rifle shot, was another heroic act of resistance by the exploited against their exploiters.
rewrite: Comrades, From this very ground, the blood-drenched firing range of Kaisariani, where 79 years ago on May Day 1944, 200 communists marched forth with heads high, their gaze proud upon the muzzles of their Nazi executioners, we mark this year's Labour Day. We vow to persist on their course, to never dishonor their sacrifice, so that the better days they too yearned for may finally rise for our nation and our people. The river of blood that soaked the wall of Caesarian that day, the human form that fell "a single manly stature" with each Nazi rifle shot, stands as yet another heroic act of resistance by the oppressed against their oppressors.

And of course, the workers are not going to see any relief either, with some "simple digital applications" and "payment systems", like those proposed by Varoufakis, which, according to many reports, the European Central Bank is already planning, wanting to shield the banking system from risks and to hit the big US companies that dominate digital transactions today. rewrite: "But it also indicates that the governments of other nations, which are facing protests across Europe, share responsibility, as do the EU and the exploitative system itself. Naturally, workers won't find relief through mere 'digital applications' and 'payment systems,' such as those suggested by Varoufakis. text: The Thessalian people can reject the arguments for supposedly "strengthening the local economy" due to the presence of foreign military forces! We are talking first of all about money that is stained with the blood of thousands of people who have been killed over the years in Syria, Libya, Iraq, Afghanistan, Yugoslavia, Ukraine and in so many other wars. rewrite: The Thessalian populace can dismiss claims that foreign military presence "bolsters the local economy"! These funds are tainted by the blood of countless lives lost in Syria, Libya, Iraq, Afghanistan, Yugoslavia, Ukraine, and numerous other conflicts. This so-called "progress" signifies decay, corruption, and decline, transforming areas into replicas of 1960s Trumps. Just as they considered the Tempis, they must weigh involvement in U.S. and NATO schemes—and reject them. Indeed, human lives do matter to us!

text: Despite the homeric squabbles over who and how to govern, there is a common approach from the Southwest, Syriza and PASOK on the basic issues that determine what the governor will do. That's why they can get along fine in the GSEE administration, which took a vacation in Kavouri when the workers went on strike on March 8 to share out the chairs in the presidium. rewrite: Despite the epic disputes over who should govern and how, there is a shared stance from the Southwest, Syriza, and PASOK on the fundamental matters that shape the governor's actions. This is why they cooperate smoothly in the GSEE administration, which took a break in Kavouri while workers struck on March 8 to allocate the presidium seats. Or their collaboration in municipalities with a communist mayor to prevent re-election, as seen in Patras. Yet even in towns with a combative history, where a communist mayor might be re-elected, as is happening here in Kaisariani, the factions of New Democracy, Syriza, and PASOK have merged into one.

text: Our aim is to ensure strong sustainable growth that will enable the economy to stand on its feet regionally with competitiveness. Inward-looking by exploiting modern digital capabilities in all sectors of production and always respecting the environment. The benefits of this policy cannot be only for the few and the powerful; they must be spread to the whole of Greek society. That is why we are talking about a progressive tax system that ensures the necessary resources to reduce inequalities and fight poverty, development linked to the real needs of the people that guarantees a better life for the working man, so that he can live in a house he can afford access to housing. With dignity and low cost to get after several years of life a decent pension and feel secure in a health system that supports him in the hard times and not as we live today. A total decline. With policies that support the Greek family to be able to make ends meet, with social structures and a quality public education system for all the children of the Greek people. Our goal is to offer young people fair and equal opportunities to live, to develop in their own country, to get an education, to work with decent wages, to start a family.
rewrite: Our goal is to achieve robust, sustainable growth that allows the economy to become regionally competitive and self-reliant. This outward-oriented approach leverages modern digital tools across all production sectors while consistently protecting the environment. The gains from this strategy must not be limited to a privileged or powerful minority; they must reach every part of Greek society. That is why we advocate for a progressive tax framework to secure the funds needed to lessen inequality and combat poverty, fostering development aligned with people’s actual needs. This ensures a better quality of life for workers, enabling them to afford suitable housing, live with dignity, and after years of labor, receive an adequate pension. It also means feeling protected by a health system that provides support in difficult times—unlike the widespread decline we face today. We pursue policies that help Greek families manage their finances, backed by strong social services and a high-quality public education system for all children. rewrite: Friends, it is not just about institutions; conduct also shapes the economy. Mr. Mitsotakis claims to have lowered tax rates. Examining the data, certain rates have indeed been cut. rewrite:
Friends. Therefore, this is where commitments are essential. I pledge that if the people grant us their trust, we will forge a new covenant of honor with the farmers and peasants of our nation, for as our old advertisement before the '93 elections stated, blood is not water. Do the rural citizens of this country clearly recall which party provided them with substance, strength, and dignity? Thus, immediate action to support our producers: reducing production costs, particularly for agricultural inputs and fuel; zero excise duty on agricultural oil throughout the crisis; backing energy communities among farmers and renewable energy production; universal protection of farmland from seizures; establishing non-confiscatable, tax-free subsidies and compensation; and direct aid to farmers. Updating the ELGA insurance rules to extend livestock disaster coverage due to climate change—an issue the ministry overlooks. Completing the entire process for new CAP programs within a year, with fixed deadlines for application submissions and payments, ending bureaucratic delays. Eliminate the runner-up beneficiary system through efficient resource planning, not wasteful spending, ensuring decent housing and language programs for foreign farm workers to encourage them to stay, preventing the severe harvest and production crises seen over the past year and a half.

Friends. Yet beyond this, a long-term vision for the primary sector is crucial. Prioritizing increased funding from the Recovery Fund for green and digital transformation of production, including organic farming. Enhancing the competitiveness and global reach of our vital national products.

rewrite: Friends, we have a duty to the younger generation to pledge that living expenses will decrease. Your children and grandchildren are moving to Athens and Thessaloniki for their studies. rewrite: Regarding Vangelis Venizelos. In the Novartis scandal, he orchestrated his own political downfall. We all recall the events in the Greek parliament. rewrite: Communists steadfastly champion friendship among peoples, opposing nationalist animosity and advocating for mutually beneficial cooperation between nations for the welfare of their populations. These developments, under the guise of 'peace,' risk unleashing new conflicts in the Aegean while simultaneously diverting vital resources away from the Greek and Turkish peoples—resources that should serve their common good rather than boosting capitalist profits. Thus, the true solution and hope rest in the joint struggle we can undertake together.
