Tomorrow we flood the streets and squares all over the country, commemorate the day of the global working class by going on strike. Demonstrating that our future is not barbarism and exploitation, that to their blackmail and the realism of subjugation, we respond by bringing our own contemporary needs to the fore. Yes, we are putting our own needs and the needs of our children first. Therefore, therefore, strong JKE, strength for the people. Because we know better than anyone that: "It is madness to abandon our dreams. To change the world is neither madness nor utopia. It is Justice!" That is why only the people save the people on the road of subversion, with a much stronger JCP!"
rewrite: Tonight, let us all delight in the splendid concert our beloved artists have arranged to give us renewed vigor. Tomorrow, we will fill the streets and squares across the nation, honoring the global working class by striking. We will show that our future rejects barbarism and exploitation, that against their blackmail and the realism of oppression, we assert our own modern demands. Indeed, we prioritize our needs and those of our children. Thus, thus, a powerful JKE, power to the people. For we understand better than anyone: "It is folly to forsake our dreams. Changing the world is neither folly nor utopia. It is Justice!" That is why only the people can save the people on the path of upheaval, with an even stronger JCP!

text: Because it is absurd today, at a time of enormous scientific progress, to mourn 57 or more deaths because telecommunications and transport security measures are considered a cost.
rewrite: Given the immense scientific advancements of our era, it is irrational to lament 57 or more fatalities when telecommunications and transport safety protocols are viewed merely as expenses.

text: But we also see PASOK, ready and willing to complement any government. After all, it has not lost responsibility for its participation in so many memorandum governments that have plundered our lives.
rewrite: "Yet we also observe PASOK, prepared and eager to support any administration. It has not, after all, escaped accountability for its involvement in numerous memorandum governments that have ravaged our livelihoods."

text: But, friends, let us look to the future, let us look ahead, why PASOK? What is the reason? Beyond the deep historical and social roots, the footprint, the great projects, infrastructure, hospitals, the NHS, public universities, independent authorities, proud foreign policy, patriotic stance on national issues. When have we ever had New Democracy and Syriza as our companions? What did they support of all this? The ASEP? Transparency? The protection of the first home? Which of PASOK's great reforms are they trying to appropriate? They supported with their vote in the Greek parliament. They have always been enemies of change and both of them were conscious enemies of the great changes made by PASOK to make Greece a normal European country and to make its people stand up proudly in international competition. So let's go to the future. What are we doing today? What is our programme? Why are we talking about European social democracy? Why are we proposing a strong welfare state and a truly competitive productive base? Because our people simply will not stand for it. Our people cannot afford any more inequalities. Our young people cannot go abroad by the tens of thousands because they have no prospects and no future here. The country is collapsing demographically. What do we do? We continue to listen to the Internet parasite. Killing themselves for nothing. If there is a nuclear accident in Ukraine, Tsipras and Mitsotakis will be fighting in Greece.
rewrite: Yet, comrades, let us turn our gaze forward, let us envision what lies ahead—why PASOK? What is the cause? Beyond its profound historical and social foundations, its lasting impact, the grand initiatives, infrastructure, hospitals, the National Health System, public universities, independent bodies, a dignified foreign policy, a patriotic approach to national matters. When have New Democracy and Syriza ever stood alongside us? What among these have they backed? The Supreme Council for Civil Personnel Selection? Openness? Safeguarding the primary residence? Which of PASOK’s major reforms do they seek to claim? They endorsed them through their votes in the Hellenic Parliament. They have perpetually opposed transformation, both knowingly adversaries of the significant shifts PASOK enacted to align Greece with Europe and to empower its citizens to compete with pride globally. Thus, let us advance toward the future. What is our current mission? What does our agenda entail? Why do we emphasize European social democracy? Why do we advocate for a robust welfare state and a genuinely competitive economic foundation? Because our populace simply will not tolerate otherwise. Our people can no longer endure further disparities. Our youth cannot depart by the thousands due to a lack of opportunities and a future here. The nation faces demographic decline. How do we respond? We persist in heeding the online detractors. Sacrificing for naught. Should a nuclear incident occur in Ukraine, Tsipras and Mitsotakis would be clashing within Greece.

text: And I want to say that in these difficult days when this election campaign started. Some people are again trying to raise false dilemmas. But what is the real dilemma of the election? It is egoism. Of Mr Tsipras and Mr Mitsotakis. Who cannot appreciate that what they have done over the last eight and a half years has led Greece to continue the merry-go-round of lost opportunities. The toxicity, the division. So what is the real dilemma? Is the real dilemma or do we as a nation as a people build a state that guarantees the public interest and security? Or do we continue the game in which the rulers of the day will have the state as a booty in their hands with the sole aim of buffoonery and strengthening their power? We, then, get in the way. To those who have bankrupted Greece. To the attitudes that are driving the young generation abroad. The practices that make citizens disillusioned. But now the people cannot say that they did not know as they did in 2014. Now we know very well what Mr Tsipras and Mr Kammenos were, and what Mr Mitsotakis was? They have been tested. So today, does Mr Mitsotakis think he can hide his executive failure? The grave insult to the institutions, the widening of social inequalities, the reduction in the purchasing power of citizens and job insecurity does not call for a positive vote for the work he is doing. He goes all over Greece and spreads the scarecrow of Mr Tsipras' governance and says. Vote for me because they will come.
rewrite: "And I must emphasize, during these challenging times as the election campaign begins, some are once more pushing false choices. Yet what truly defines this election? It is self-interest. That of Mr. Tsipras and Mr. Mitsotakis. Neither can acknowledge how their actions over the past eight and a half years have kept Greece trapped in a cycle of missed chances. The bitterness, the polarization. So what is the real choice? Is it not whether we, as a nation and a people, construct a state that ensures the common good and safety? Or do we persist with the game where those in power treat the state as spoils, aimed only at mockery and consolidating their own authority? We stand in opposition. Against those who have brought Greece to ruin. Against the mindsets pushing our youth to leave. The actions that leave citizens disheartened. But today, the public cannot claim ignorance as in 2014. Now we fully understand what Mr. Tsipras and Mr. Kammenos represented, and what Mr. Mitsotakis stands for? They have been judged by their records. So now, does Mr. Mitsotakis believe he can conceal his administrative shortcomings? The severe disrespect for our institutions, growing social divides, the loss of citizens' buying power, and unstable employment do not merit approval for his tenure. He travels across Greece, raising the specter of Mr. Tsipras' rule and declares: Vote for me, or they will return."

text: This unpopular direction, determined by the EU's policy of "liberalisation" and the strategy of capital, is today agreed upon by ND, SYRIZA, PASOK, MERA25, all the parties of the system. That is why we say: There is no room for any more illusions! No one should be trapped again by the offer of phony salvation solutions, by a supposedly "more progressive government" the next day. Neither a better privatisation, nor a supposedly stricter public control, nor a 're-nationalisation without compensation' will save us! As long as transport is a commodity and the railway companies operate within the capitalist economy, the situation cannot be radically, fundamentally changed.
rewrite: This widely opposed course, driven by the EU’s “liberalisation” policy and the interests of capital, is now endorsed by ND, SYRIZA, PASOK, MERA25—all the establishment parties. That is why we insist: No more illusions! Let no one be deceived again by false promises of rescue, by the mirage of a “more progressive government” tomorrow. Neither improved privatisation, nor allegedly tighter public oversight, nor a ‘re-nationalisation without compensation’ will deliver us! So long as transport remains a commodity and rail firms operate under capitalism, no radical, fundamental change is possible.

text: I expected, of course, that there would be many of us in our old harbour, but I did not imagine that even that would seem small compared to today's impressive gathering.
rewrite: "I had anticipated, naturally, that our old harbor would be filled with many of us, yet I never imagined it would appear modest next to today's remarkable assembly."

text: Because it is absurd that today, young couples cannot have their own home, with rents now being prohibitive here in Piraeus as well.
rewrite: Given the absurdity that young couples today are unable to secure a home of their own, with rents having become prohibitively high even here in Piraeus.

text: Thank you, my patriots, Chaniots, neo-democrats of Crete. I repay you for the great love you show me today.
rewrite: "Thank you, my fellow patriots, Chaniots, and the new democrats of Crete. I return the profound affection you have shown me this day."

text:
Today the conditions have been scientifically formed for the existence of a system of Primary Health Care and hospitals fully staffed with all specialties and all modern means.
There is a solution so that tourism, recreation and relaxation are a guaranteed right of the working class and the grassroots, not an expensive commodity. To enjoy the beauties of the whole country with modern infrastructure, which they are now unable to do in large numbers, mainly for economic reasons.
rewrite:
Today, the scientific conditions exist for a comprehensive Primary Health Care system and hospitals fully equipped with all specialties and modern resources.  
There is a way to ensure tourism, recreation, and relaxation become a guaranteed right for the working class and ordinary people, not a costly luxury. This would allow them to enjoy the country's natural beauty through modern infrastructure, something many currently cannot do, primarily due to economic constraints.

text: Greece and friends. We have a duty to talk about our economy, but what economy? With the fake statistics? That everything is going well that wages have gone up 20% and salaries have gone up 20% but what it says 7.4% real wages have gone down. 5 billion more in taxes paid by the Greek people. Yes, but Mr Mitsotakis says that he has reduced all rates. How is that possible? Because he is simply reducing the rates a little for the many. And a lot for the powerful, because the revaluations and accuracy have made the state's revenues 66% indirect taxes that mainly hit the weak and the middle class. What do we say about all this? What do we say about growth that 700,000 jobs are up to 500€ for the new generation What do they do? The one place because of flexibility 2 places can be so upright or society? Can so the young generation can have a family? They wonder why Greek children continue to leave abroad? But that's why. Because we have an unfair development, a development that makes the rich richer and the poor poorer. On the other hand, Mr Tsipras is handing out money as he did in 2015. But he probably doesn't know a principle. It's good to get milk from the cow, but where and when to learn to feed for the cow? Because in the end the cow dies.
rewrite: Greece and its allies. We must discuss our economy, but which economy? The one with fabricated data? That claims everything is fine, that wages have risen 20% and salaries are up 20%, yet reports show real wages have actually fallen by 7.4%. An additional 5 billion in taxes paid by Greeks. True, but Mr. Mitsotakis claims he has lowered all tax rates. How can that be? Because he slightly reduces rates for the majority, while cutting them significantly for the powerful, as revaluations and precision have led to 66% of state revenue coming from indirect taxes, which primarily burden the vulnerable and middle class. What is our response to all this? What do we say about growth when 700,000 jobs pay up to €500 for the younger generation? What can they do? With such precarious work, can they afford two jobs just to survive? Can the youth even start families? Why do Greek children keep emigrating? This is precisely why. Because we have unjust growth, a development that enriches the wealthy and impoverishes the poor. Meanwhile, Mr. Tsipras is distributing money as he did in 2015. But he seems unaware of a basic principle: it’s fine to milk the cow, but when and where do we learn to feed it? Otherwise, eventually, the cow will perish.

text:
Trust means to feel that justice is indeed for all, that there is no impunity for the powerful. Dignity what does dignity mean in our time? Because many people don't discuss politics anymore, they don't trust what politicians say because they feel hurt, they feel their dignity is wounded.
So for us, dignity is that the weak Greek should not be afraid that he might lose his first home, that there should be no shame lists that the pensioner is afraid of. The next surgery and the unpleasant delays of constant postponements. The surgery due to lack of permanent staff in the NHS for young people dignity is to have access to a house at a cheap rent, decent housing to raise their family and children. This is the dignity that we, as PASOK, have a duty to give to the Greek people, because we are the party of Social Justice, the party that gave hope and prospects to vulnerable Greeks. Dignity means for the Greek children to do their computerised registration, not by looking at their grandparents' pockets, but by looking at their future and their dreams. That is dignity. That's confidence. This is the new beginning that all of us together on May 21 will make the bold changes for a strong Greece of social justice and national dignity. We have a duty to build sustainable growth in the Greek economy that creates quality jobs, away from an unfair tax system, to reduce inequalities and of course to create outward-looking investments with competition, with strong exports, not to hand over hundreds of thousands of businesses, farmers, ranchers, cooperatives. Their property to the crows of the funds and to deflate the Greek economy. There too we have a duty as a patriotic movement to prevent this dangerous de-fellatinization.
rewrite:
Trust is the belief that justice truly serves everyone, with no immunity for those in power. What does dignity signify today? Many have turned away from politics, distrusting politicians' words because they feel wounded, their dignity bruised.

For us, dignity means that no vulnerable Greek should fear losing their primary home, that there should be no shameful lists terrifying pensioners. It means no more distressing delays from constant postponements of surgeries due to shortages of permanent staff in the NHS. For the young, dignity is access to affordable rental housing, decent homes to raise families. This is the dignity we, as PASOK, must provide to the Greek people, as the party of Social Justice, the one that offered hope and opportunity to the vulnerable. Dignity for Greek children means computerized registration based on their future and dreams, not their grandparents' finances. That is dignity. That is confidence. This new beginning, on May 21, will bring bold changes for a strong Greece rooted in social justice and national dignity.

We must foster sustainable growth in the Greek economy, generating quality jobs, moving beyond an unfair tax system to reduce inequalities, and promoting outward-looking investments through competition and robust exports. We cannot allow hundreds of thousands of businesses, farmers, ranchers, and cooperatives to see their assets seized by fund vultures, draining the Greek economy. As a patriotic movement, we also have a duty to prevent this perilous de-fellatinization.

text: Because it is absurd today, in a country with so much sun, so much mineral wealth, water, air, that our people cannot enjoy cheap electricity by using all the energy sources in a planned way.
rewrite: "Given the abundance of sunlight, mineral resources, water, and air in our nation, it is absurd that our citizens cannot access affordable electricity through the coordinated use of all available energy sources."

text: It will involve us even more actively in the NATO games, in the imperialist war that is going on.
rewrite: "It will draw us more deeply into NATO's maneuvers, into the ongoing imperialist conflict."

text: That is why the forces supported by PAME have been in the majority in the last years in the Piraeus Labour Centre, which sets the tone for the overall popular demands in the city, such as against the miserable situation in both the primary health care and the three hospitals of Piraeus.
rewrite: This explains why PAME-backed forces have held the majority in the Piraeus Labour Centre in recent years, shaping the broader popular demands in the city, including those addressing the dire conditions in both primary health care and Piraeus’s three hospitals.

text: Friends, compañeras and compañeros. I am very, very happy to be here once again. Here in my place in Lamia, the capital of Fthiotida. From here from Sterea from Roumeli we carry to every corner of Greece the call to support the KKE in the elections. So that our people will be stronger the next day. Yes, we can do it, we can be proud on election night. That can only happen in one way, with the decisive support of the KKE.
rewrite: Comrades, friends and allies. It is a great joy to return once more. Here in my home of Lamia, the heart of Fthiotida. From this place in Sterea, in Roumeli, we send across Greece the appeal to back the KKE at the polls. So that our people emerge stronger the day after. Yes, it is possible; we can hold our heads high on election night. This will be achieved in only one way: through the resolute support of the KKE.

text: Friends and friends. Private debt. It is a bomb on the foundations of society. The debts of the Greek people. We don't have a magic wand. But our proposals are clear. We are restoring the protection of the main house for indebted households, by updating the PASOK law of 2010. A similar regulation for the universal protection of agricultural property. We cannot allow the rural land to be left unoccupied. Protection of borrowers with Swiss Franc is 80,000 families throughout Greece, by limiting the borrower's liability to 1/3 of the interest rate increase and 2/3 will be charged to the bank. Substantial negotiation with the banks to take measures to eliminate and prevent interest rate increases, loans, weak households and of course reduce the banks' profit margin for consistent borrowers. Our priority is to regulate even the loans bought by the funds, the red loans, so that a second chance is given. To the citizens and to have redemptive solutions and not to be hostage to financial systems that are not interested in regulation. Because what do they want what they got 10 and 15% in value to sell 20 and 25% and get out of Greece? So we in Parliament have to legislate so that negotiations with the funds are done in a framework, as with the banks in the forefront and not with blackmail leading. Thousands of people to deadlock and tragedies.
rewrite: Friends and allies. Personal debt. It is a bomb at the very base of society. The debts of the Greek people. We do not possess a magic wand. Yet our proposals are clear. We are reinstating the protection of the primary residence for indebted households, by modernizing the PASOK law from 2010. A similar framework for the universal safeguarding of agricultural property. We cannot permit farmland to lie fallow. Protection for borrowers with Swiss Franc loans—affecting 80,000 families across Greece—by capping the borrower's liability to one-third of the interest rate hike, with two-thirds borne by the bank. Meaningful negotiation with banks to adopt measures that eliminate and prevent interest rate surges, address loans for vulnerable households, and naturally, reduce the banks' profit margin for reliable borrowers. Our priority is to regulate even the loans acquired by funds, the non-performing loans, to grant a second chance. To provide citizens with redemptive solutions and not leave them hostage to financial systems indifferent to regulation. For what do they seek? Having bought at 10 or 15% of value, to sell at 20 or 25% and exit Greece? Therefore, we in Parliament must enact laws so that negotiations with funds occur within a structured framework, as with banks, at the forefront, not through coercive tactics leading thousands into deadlock and tragedy.

text: Yes, the further commercialisation and privatisation of the public health system is a great conquest for capital, which is being promoted by the New Democracy, but the forces of the KKE, together with other militants, through the mass organisations, are leading the struggle for the protection of the public health system, for recruitment and infrastructure, because in our conception health cannot be a commodity. This is why we are leading the struggle to open the hospital of Agia Varvara, the well-known Infectious Diseases Hospital, which was closed by the New Democracy and kept closed by the Syriza government, which now remembered how much the people of the region need it...
rewrite: Indeed, the increasing commercialization and privatization of public healthcare represents a significant victory for capital, advanced by New Democracy. However, the forces of the KKE, alongside other activists, are mobilizing through mass organizations to defend the public health system, advocating for staffing and infrastructure, as we believe health should never be treated as a commodity. This is precisely why we are spearheading the effort to reopen the Agia Varvara Hospital, the renowned Infectious Diseases Hospital, which was shut down by New Democracy and remained closed under the Syriza government—a government that has only now recalled the urgent need of the local community for this facility.

text: This means a new cycle of opportunities for the country. A cycle of opportunities, the prologue of which Crete is already experiencing.
rewrite: This marks a fresh cycle of prospects for the nation. A cycle of opportunities, whose beginning Crete is already witnessing.

text: So, when they talk about conquests, they talk about all that they give, that they offer with their laws to the industrialists, to the shipowners, to the bankers, to all the exploiters in order to make their profits... And when they talk about demands, they talk again about their own demands that they are planning to implement. We, when we talk about conquests, about the rights and needs of the workers, about all that today offers relief to the people's families, we talk about. This is the content of our demands, and if one thing is proven every day, it is that profits and privileges for capital are not compatible with the needs and rights of the workers and the people.
rewrite: Thus, when they speak of gains, they refer to all they provide, the benefits they extend through their laws to industrialists, shipowners, bankers, and every exploiter to secure their profits... And when they speak of demands, they again refer to their own planned impositions. We, when we speak of gains, of the rights and necessities of workers, of all that now brings relief to the people's families, we speak of these. This is the essence of our demands, and if anything is demonstrated daily, it is that the profits and privileges of capital cannot coexist with the needs and rights of workers and the people.

text: So that's it? Which is the big bet on May 21 Is all this life-changing description to be put into practice? And obviously it is in our hands and in the hands of the Greek people. But it is also in the hands of every member of our party. Every member of our party in the coming days has a duty towards the history of the party towards the Greek society towards the great struggles of the change of the 80s, 90s, 2000, of consistency, of hope, of social justice, of national dignity. In the coming days, each and every one of you should take the cause of the rebirth of the democratic party into your own hands, here today from Kalamata, from Messinia and the Peloponnese. Your warm welcome gives us hope. It fills us with strength. But above all, it makes us feel the weight of the debt of the new change. That is why we call on every Greek woman to make a decision for change on May 21, to change the country, to turn the page and live again years of perspective, years of justice, years without inequalities, years of stability. These are our values. These are our principles this is our struggle these are our struggles for this. All together May 21 for the great victory. I thank you from the bottom of my heart for your warm presence today and you can be sure that on 21 May PASOK will be reborn and dynamically return to the forefront of history for the benefit of all the Greek people, especially the weakest and the middle class. Good strength and good luck in our struggle.
rewrite: So, is that all? The major decision on May 21—will these transformative promises truly be enacted? Clearly, it rests with us and the Greek people, but also with every member of our party. In the coming days, each party member bears a duty to the party's history, to Greek society, and to the significant battles for change across the 80s, 90s, 2000s—upholding consistency, hope, social justice, and national dignity. Each of you must now personally champion the revival of the democratic party, starting here today in Kalamata, from Messinia and the Peloponnese. Your enthusiastic reception inspires hope and fortifies us. Yet, it also reminds us of the profound responsibility we carry for this new era of change. Therefore, we urge every Greek citizen to choose change on May 21, to transform the nation, turn a new leaf, and embrace a future filled with opportunity, fairness, reduced disparities, and stability. These are our core values, our guiding principles, and the essence of our fight—our collective efforts toward this goal. United, on May 21, we strive for a decisive victory. I sincerely thank you for your heartfelt presence today, and rest assured, on May 21, PASOK will be revitalized and powerfully re-enter the historical stage, serving all Greeks, particularly the most vulnerable and the middle class. Courage and good fortune in our shared endeavor.

text: Homeland, a big thank you for your warm welcome. Thank you from the bottom of my heart. Democratic Heraklion sends a message of joy, hope, victory and the rebirth of the democratic party. Here in Heraklion, the historic castle of PASOK. In the square where Andreas Papandreou loved and adored. Here again we begin by picking up the thread of history. Here in this square. In 1985 I first heard our founder Andreas Papandreou as a child. It was here in this square that I heard the late George Gennimata in 1993. Here in this square today, after many decades, I come. And I thank you from the bottom of my heart. Because you are once again proudly raising the flag of PASOK, the sun, the sun of optimism, the sun of hope, the sun of social justice and our national dignity. PASOK is here, united, strong. All generations of the Democratic Party are here in Democratic Heraklion, sending a message from all corners of the country. The Democratic Party, the people-born movement of May 21, is once again becoming the protagonist of developments. We have a national debt. We have a national debt. We have a national debt on May 21 to revive our movement, because it is a one-way street for Greece to become strong again and the Greek people to become proud.
rewrite: Homeland, a heartfelt thank you for this warm welcome. My deepest gratitude to you all. Democratic Heraklion sends a message of joy, hope, triumph, and the renewal of the democratic party. Here in Heraklion, the historic fortress of PASOK. In the square cherished and revered by Andreas Papandreou. Here, we once more take up the thread of history. Right in this square. As a child, I first heard our founder Andreas Papandreou here in 1985. In this same square, I listened to the late George Gennimata in 1993. Today, after many decades, I stand here in this square. And I thank you with all my heart. For you are proudly raising the flag of PASOK once again—the sun, the sun of optimism, the sun of hope, the sun of social justice and our national dignity. PASOK is here, united and strong. All generations of the Democratic Party are gathered in Democratic Heraklion, sending a message from every corner of the nation. The Democratic Party, the people's movement born on May 21, is reclaiming its role as a leading force in events. We have a national duty. We have a national duty. We have a national duty on May 21 to revitalize our movement, for it is the essential path for Greece to regain strength and for the Greek people to restore their pride.

text: Today the conditions have been scientifically formed for there to be a system of primary health care hospitals, fully staffed with all specialties and all modern means and not to have the hospital of Lamia operating with 60 fewer doctors than the organizational chart provides, apart from the other shortages in staff. Nor should we have the Health Centres under-operating with 2 and 3 general practitioners with shortages of nursing staff and with doctors transferred from the health centres to the hospital to cover the gaps.
rewrite: Today, the scientific groundwork exists to establish a comprehensive primary healthcare system, fully equipped with all specialties and modern resources. Yet, Lamia Hospital operates with 60 fewer doctors than its organizational plan requires, not to mention other staffing shortages. Similarly, Health Centres are understaffed, functioning with only two or three general practitioners, lacking nursing personnel, and having doctors transferred from these centres to the hospital to fill gaps.

text: SYRIZA hypocritically said that it was forced by the Brussels priesthood to follow this policy. But recently, SYRIZA MPs were standing up to applaud Tsipras in Parliament, when he declared himself proud of having secured the notorious cushion for the Greek economy, i.e. the bloody surplus of the 2015-2019 SYRIZA government. Now the OECD says in its recommendations for the next government that a new bloody surplus will be required to ensure Greece's investment grade and to make the country attractive for new investments by domestic and foreign groups.The EU is making similar demands for the disbursement of the Community funds. In other words, the unpopular policy will continue and intensify, no matter which government is formed.
rewrite: SYRIZA hypocritically claimed it was compelled by Brussels authorities to pursue this policy. Yet recently, SYRIZA MPs rose to applaud Tsipras in Parliament when he expressed pride in securing the notorious cushion for Greece's economy—the harsh surplus from the 2015-2019 SYRIZA government. Now, the OECD advises in its recommendations for the next government that another harsh surplus will be necessary to secure Greece's investment grade and attract new investments from domestic and foreign groups. The EU is similarly demanding this for the release of Community funds. Thus, the unpopular policy will persist and intensify, regardless of which government takes power.

text: Friends. If one wants to reveal how phony, how false the electoral confrontation of the parties of the system is, surely the issue of people's housing is one of the most characteristic. On the eve of the elections, all the accomplices in the crimes of auctions and household over-indebtedness are now posing as the late protectors of the first home; we, for our part, are clearly telling the wage-earners and the self-employed that it is time to pay up. They should think about how we got here, who is responsible, who has benefited and what is coming next. They should think about who told the truth and who is constantly trying to deceive them.
rewrite: Comrades. To expose the sham nature of the electoral contest among the system's parties, the matter of housing for the people stands as a prime example. As elections approach, all those complicit in the crimes of foreclosures and excessive household debt now posture as belated defenders of the family home; we, conversely, state plainly to workers and the self-employed that the moment to settle accounts has arrived. They must consider how we reached this point, who bears responsibility, who has profited, and what lies ahead. They must reflect on who has spoken truthfully and who persistently seeks to mislead them.

text: Friends, comrades, all these years, from 2012 until today, the KKE has been the only one that has kept the flag of progress and struggle high. That insisted that there is another way from the "yes to everything", from the will of the exploiters and the imperialist centres, the EU, the USA and NATO. Who made sure that the anti-people's measures are not passed "unanimously" and with complete unanimity. Which, here in the western districts of Athens, as the third largest political force, but also in the whole country, was on the side of the poor, continuing to fight for the people's movement to rise up. And in recent years, indeed, something seems to be changing.
rewrite: Comrades, throughout these years, from 2012 to the present, the KKE has stood alone in upholding the banner of progress and resistance. It has consistently asserted that an alternative path exists beyond the "yes to everything," beyond the dictates of the exploiters and the imperialist powers—the EU, the USA, and NATO. It has ensured that anti-people measures are not adopted "unanimously" and without opposition. Here in the western neighborhoods of Athens, as the third largest political force, and across the nation, it has stood with the impoverished, persistently striving for the resurgence of the people's movement. And indeed, in recent times, a shift appears to be underway.

text:
Such governance will break the shackles of international unequal relations and agreements. It will free the country from the EU and NATO, and will carry out bilateral agreements on an equal basis with other countries.
Today there is a solution to build a very safe and modern transport network. There is a solution to not being food-dependent - and not only - on this rich and blessed land. There is a solution for dealing with flooding, strong earthquakes, using scientific achievements, with integrated planning.

text: In the last twenty-four hours, Mr Mitsotakis has really shown who has a personal obsession. He is trying to convince the PASOK cadres, the friends of PASOK, the voters of PASOK, that I am leading you into a blind front against New Democracy. But the truth is one. That in the last few days there has been nesting within it the anxiety and fear that what is being born, the new one, will be the real opponent. It will be the democratic party of serious opposition, of the programme, of perspective, and not the cheap populism of Mr Tsipras. Because Mr Mitsotakis knows very well in his heart that if it were not for Tsipras, his government would already be a thing of the past in the minds of the Greek people. Friends, he is looking for a life jacket. He knows that the only lifeline is the Greek people's previous experience of 15-19 with Tsipras and Kammenos. I imagine he would want another PASOK and not this PASOK, the current PASOK. He wanted a subordinate PASOK, but all of you 200,000, 270,000 democratic citizens sent him a strong message on 12 December and I call on all the Greek people to send him a new message on 21 May.
rewrite: Over the past day, Mr. Mitsotakis has clearly revealed who harbors a personal fixation. He is attempting to persuade PASOK members, PASOK supporters, and PASOK voters that I am guiding you into a futile confrontation with New Democracy. Yet the reality is singular. In recent days, anxiety and fear have taken root within him that what is emerging, this new force, will become the genuine adversary. It will stand as the democratic party of substantive opposition, grounded in policy and vision, not the shallow populism of Mr. Tsipras. For Mr. Mitsotakis understands deeply that without Tsipras, his government would already be consigned to history in the consciousness of Greeks. Friends, he is searching for a lifeline. He recognizes that his sole hope lies in the Greek people’s prior encounter with Tsipras and Kammenos from 2015 to 2019. I suspect he desires a different PASOK, not the present one. He wished for a subservient PASOK, but all 200,000 to 270,000 of you democratic citizens delivered a powerful rebuke on December 12, and I urge every Greek to convey a fresh message on May 21.

text: People of Athens, welcome to this celebration of democracy, of hope, of hope, of perspective. A big thank you from the bottom of my heart for this warm welcome. A big thank you from the bottom of my heart for your trust. And another big thank you for the message of victory that we are sending tonight from all corners of the country. PASOK is here, united and strong, and we are sending a strong response to our political opponents. PASOK is here to give us a new perspective, a hope to turn the country around. Dignity for social justice. The democratic party, the movement of Andreas Papandreou, is here again, a protagonist in the political scene of our country. Friends, every day they fight us in the front and behind the scenes. Every day we are beaten by SYRIZA and New Democracy. But today Athens is sending a clear message: The more they hit us, the stronger we get. Mr Mitsotakis and Mr Tsipras, this is the party that is identified with the Greek people, this is the people-born movement. It is the movement of 1974 that sealed the post-independence, the best years of the Greek people. It embodied the dreams of many generations and made Greece a normal European country. Friends, PASOK is Here, United, Strong. Because the needs of our country call for new struggles. To daily struggles. The Greek people can no longer tolerate inequalities and unreliability. The Greek people can no longer tolerate the client state, the devaluation of the public interest.
rewrite: Citizens of Athens, welcome to this gathering for democracy, for hope, for a new vision. I extend my deepest gratitude for this heartfelt welcome. I thank you sincerely for your confidence. And I thank you once more for the triumphant message we broadcast tonight from every region of the nation. PASOK stands united and resolute, delivering a powerful answer to our political rivals. PASOK is present to offer a fresh outlook, a hope to redirect our country. Honor for social justice. The democratic party, the movement of Andreas Papandreou, has returned as a leading force on our nation's political stage. Comrades, each day they confront us openly and in secret. Each day we face attacks from SYRIZA and New Democracy. Yet today, Athens declares unmistakably: The harder they strike, the stronger we become. Mr. Mitsotakis and Mr. Tsipras, this is the party that embodies the Greek populace, this is the movement born of the people. It is the movement of 1974 that defined the post-junta era, the finest period for the Greek people. It realized the aspirations of countless generations and established Greece as a full member of Europe. Friends, PASOK is Here, United, Strong. For our nation's demands require renewed battles. For the struggles of every day. The Greek people will no longer endure inequity and instability. The Greek people will no longer tolerate a patronage system, the erosion of the common good.

text: It's coming back, this party is coming back. United, renewed, the great democratic party, where there is no change, where there is no reform without the signature of PASOK, in the best years of the Greek people. So I want to say something about change because some people think they can plagiarise the word. The word you can. You can't take the history because it is engraved in the memory of the Greek people. It is, Mr Tsipras, the images, the experiences of the underprivileged Greeks who have seen their lives improve. Those who experienced the post-civil war state and the PASOK of Andreas Papandreou recognized the national resistance. They are the ones who have engraved in their minds what the hospitals were before '81 and what the National Health System of George Gennimata and Paraskevas Avgerinos was from '80 onwards. They are the ones who crowded the buffet shops and after the late Anastasios Peponi's AESEP they saw what European meritocracy, normality means. They are the ones who saw the great infrastructure projects, the public universities, the CCP, Diavgeia, Kapodistrias in local government. But I ask you, Mr Tsipras and Mr Mitsotakis, when did you support even one of these great changes that marked the history of the country, the history of the democratic party? In all of them you were an obstacle. You have been the front line of conservation from both the right and the left.
rewrite: The party is returning, revived and united, the great democratic force where no change occurs, no reform is enacted without PASOK's endorsement, during the finest era for the Greek people. I must address the notion of change, as some believe they can co-opt the term. The word itself they might borrow, but they cannot seize the history, for it is etched into the collective memory of Greece. Mr. Tsipras, these are the images, the lived experiences of ordinary Greeks whose conditions improved. Those who knew the post-civil war era and Andreas Papandreou's PASOK acknowledged the national struggle. They remember vividly what hospitals were like before 1981 and the National Health System established by George Gennimata and Paraskevas Avgerinos from the 1980s onward. They recall crowding into buffet shops and, following the late Anastasios Peponi's AESEP, witnessing the meaning of European meritocracy and normalcy. They observed the major infrastructure projects, public universities, the CCP, Diavgeia, and Kapodistrias in local governance. Yet I pose this question to you, Mr. Tsipras and Mr. Mitsotakis: when have you ever backed even one of these transformative changes that defined the nation's and the democratic party's history? In every instance, you stood as impediments. You have consistently been at the forefront of preservation, whether from the right or the left.

text: Friends, much has been said in recent hours about Mr Katrougalos. Has Mr Vroutsis changed things much from Mr Katrougalos? He has improved things a little. We with 1.1 billion, which will be much less, because by abolishing the personal difference from 01/01/2024, after 4 years we will have zero costs. With 1.1 billion we are correcting all the injustices in the pension system created by the Katrougalos and Vroutsis laws. The EKAS that Mr Tsipras abolished we are making a new EKAS for 350,000 pensioners, the poorest pensioners in the country. We are abolishing the personal difference and we are also abolishing the unfair provisions for disability and widowhood pensions. And if they ask you how much is that? 1.1 billion, not Mr Mitsotakis' 6 and Mr Tsipras' 10. We are not kidding, we say a little, but that will be put into practice.
rewrite: Friends, there has been much discussion lately regarding Mr. Katrougalos. Has Mr. Vroutsis altered things significantly from Mr. Katrougalos? He has made some improvements. With 1.1 billion—which will actually be far less, since by eliminating the personal difference starting 01/01/2024, after four years our costs will drop to zero—we are addressing all the inequities in the pension system caused by the laws of Katrougalos and Vroutsis. The EKAS that Mr. Tsipras terminated, we are reinstating as a new EKAS for 350,000 pensioners, the most financially vulnerable in the nation. We are ending the personal difference and also removing the unjust terms for disability and widowhood pensions. And if they inquire about the cost? It’s 1.1 billion, not Mr. Mitsotakis’ 6 or Mr. Tsipras’ 10. We are serious; we propose a modest amount, but it will be implemented.

text: But who can really forget what we lived through the pandemic? When the ND government protected the private groups from treating patients with COVID-19, it heavily subsidized them to speculate on human suffering, either with tests or other morbidity, since public hospitals became "one disease" hospitals? Wasn't it then that PASOK agreed to everything and Syriza's "we'll settle this later" proposed a "minister of health of common consent"? In fact, this potential minister of the Mitsotakis government is now on the SYRIZA state ballot. These convergences in the criminal management of the pandemic, our people paid for them with thousands of deaths from covid and thousands more deaths from so-called other morbidity. We hear a lot about who is with the public health care system and who wants to privatize it.
rewrite: Yet who can truly erase the memory of our pandemic experiences? When the ND administration shielded private entities from handling COVID-19 cases, it lavished subsidies on them to profit from human distress, whether through testing or other illnesses, as public hospitals turned into single-disease facilities? Wasn’t it then that PASOK consented to all measures, while Syriza’s “we’ll address this later” stance suggested a “health minister by mutual agreement”? Indeed, this prospective minister under the Mitsotakis government now appears on SYRIZA’s state list. These alignments in the disastrous pandemic response cost our community dearly, with thousands lost to covid and many more to so-called other morbidities. We often hear debates over who supports public healthcare and who aims to privatize it.

text: Another element of our policy. It is social justice as far as private debt is concerned. The main objective of our programme is to give a second chance to the Greeks who have struggled fairly, objectively, but who have not endured, and we propose redemptive solutions. We do not want them to be held hostage by the funds, of course, and by the government of the day, which is unable to legislate. So that is why we are calling for the reinstatement of the protection of the first home under Law 3869 of 2010. Of course with updated criteria and objective criteria in relation to how much they have paid off their loan. The price of the house and other criteria that will protect the first home of every vulnerable Greek 120 instalments for the arrangements of debts to tax authorities and social security funds and of course a 30% haircut for those who are punctual. Rules of operation for funds: lower instalments, fixed interest rates and viable arrangements for borrowers and, of course, universal protection for agricultural land, especially when millions of euros of red loans from cooperatives have gone to funds, which do not want any arrangements. They want sudden death and quick profit. It is our duty to stand in the way of the de-fellatinisation of the Greek economy, which has been led by Mr Tsipras' alleged Stisakhtia and Mr Mitsotakis' ineptitude. A solution for borrowers with a Swiss franc clause. We are the only ones who have engaged very substantially with legislative initiatives for these 80 000 families. What are we saying? Fair distribution of exchange rate risk. One third will be borne by the borrower and two thirds by the banking institutions that made these loans.
rewrite: Another aspect of our policy involves social justice regarding private debt. Our program's primary goal is to offer a second chance to Greeks who have genuinely struggled but could not sustain their efforts, and we advocate for redemptive measures. We aim to prevent them from being held hostage by funds and a government that fails to enact necessary laws. Therefore, we demand the restoration of primary residence protection under Law 3869/2010, with revised, objective criteria based on loan repayments, property value, and other factors to safeguard every vulnerable Greek's home. This includes 120 installments for settling debts with tax and social security authorities, plus a 30% reduction for timely payers. For funds, we propose operational rules: reduced payments, fixed interest rates, and sustainable arrangements for borrowers, alongside universal protection for farmland, especially given that millions in non-performing loans from cooperatives have been acquired by funds seeking swift profits rather than settlements. It is our responsibility to counter the de-fellatinisation of the Greek economy, driven by Mr. Tsipras' so-called Stisakhtia and Mr. Mitsotakis' incompetence. We also address borrowers with Swiss franc clauses, as we are uniquely committed through legislative efforts for these 80,000 families. Our stance is clear: a fair sharing of exchange rate risk, with one-third borne by borrowers and two-thirds by the lending banks.

text: We are proud of the attitude of our comrades and other fighters, who isolated racism and cries of hatred when the boats of uprooted people were coming to the coast. Their attitude was decisive in the face of those who tried to turn the justified anger of the islanders against uprooted people, and not against the politics of war, uprooting, exploitation and refugeeism. We all know very well that the KKE did not fold, did not change its position on the refugee issue, not in words but in its pioneering action. This action took many forms. The mobilisations in this square to prevent our islands from becoming prisons for EU refugees are not forgotten. The mobilisations after the many years of shipwrecks are not forgotten, so that we do not get used to death. The moving mobilisation in the cold, mud and rain at the Vastria site, which cancelled the bans with the mass of city workers, youth and farmers from Kalloni, Mandamado, Mistena, Thermi and other villages, is not forgotten.
rewrite: We take pride in the stance of our comrades and fellow fighters, who countered racism and hateful rhetoric as boats carrying displaced people approached the shore. Their resolve was crucial against those attempting to redirect the rightful anger of islanders toward the displaced, rather than toward the policies of war, displacement, exploitation, and forced migration. It is well known that the KKE stood firm, unwavering in its stance on the refugee issue, demonstrated not just in words but through leading actions. These actions were multifaceted. The rallies in this square to stop our islands from becoming EU detention centers are remembered. The protests following years of shipwrecks are remembered, ensuring we never grow accustomed to loss. The poignant mobilization in the cold, mud, and rain at the Vastria site, which overturned restrictions with a mass of urban workers, youth, and farmers from Kalloni, Mandamado, Mistena, Thermi, and other villages, is also remembered.

rewrite: Friends and comrades, these are not mere words. They represent our core priorities, our initiatives, our principles, our stances, and our vision. Hence this banner—of ideals, positions, and values. I urge you to lift it together on May 21 in this fight. This is not a partisan battle. It is a contest that involves the candidates, the local committees. It is a patriotic, national, and social struggle. Precisely for this reason, we carry a great obligation. On the 21st, every democratically minded, progressive Greek citizen should sense that PASOK’s home is once more open to embrace the struggles of the Greek people, to protect the common good, to safeguard the nation’s interests. That is why I ask you to wage a battle for dignity—a strong, relentless, daily fight. I anticipate nothing from the domestic oligarchy, for what we advocate simply does not align with their interests. But I expect much from those whose lives are transformed by our message—and that means all of you. So take into your hands the struggle of the democratic party. We have only days left in every village, every city, every university, every workplace. Let us voice the language of progress, change, dignity, and hope—the language of the robust democratic party established by Andreas Papandreou, the party of hope and perspective. Hoist high the flag of social justice and national honor. Victory belongs to us. The triumph will be profound. On May 21, the country turns the page. Stay well, and good luck to us all. Thank you.

rewrite: Another crucial development issue: red loans. Our proposal is clear—what we implemented in 2010 for first homes, we as a government will do again in 2023, ensuring no first home is lost by vulnerable Greeks. We initiated this protection; Mr. Mitsotakis ended it. We are here without a memorandum to once more safeguard thousands from predatory lending. Today, these vultures prioritize destroying borrowers and the real economy; the democratic party must oppose this disastrous policy Mr. Tsipras led Greece into in 2015.

rewrite: Offering affordable, secure, and modern mass transit for everyone through an updated transport system, even in major urban areas, ensures no one is endangered, including in cities such as Thessaloniki, where the promise of reliable travel has turned into a bleak jest amid uncertainty over its operation. rewrite: Friends, your radiant expressions, your warm smiles, and your waving flags hold great significance for me. Your voices, particularly those of our young people, carry across the ocean from shore to shore in our country.

text: Friends, education. For us, education is the greatest lever of social justice and social mobility. Do you know all too well the older people? That public education made the child of the farmer in the Epirus of the cattle farmer study in the good years of the PASOK. Doctor, lawyer engineer, to produce wealth and build his family with dignity. We have a duty to strengthen all levels of public education again, so that all Greek children have free access to reduce inequalities and not Greek children taking computer tests by looking into the pocket of their grandfather's, grandmother's father and mother. But looking at their future and their ambitions for it, so for us the vision for public education is a priority. Schools today must be a key instrument for young people to respond to the digital world and sustainable development, offering equal opportunities to all young people, breaking down inequalities, setting them up to take on the challenges of the future both as citizens and as workers. For this there must be a strong public school and a strong public university. We know that the ideological policies of SYRIZA and, of course, the policies of New Democracy, which want to privatise education at all levels, have degraded and undermined education in our country. That is why it is time to take bold decisions. Always in cooperation with teachers, with an increase in public spending on education, so that we can gradually reach the average spending of the European Union countries, our proposals focus on strengthening quality by modernising content and implementing the 16 quality indicators of the European Union, with remedial teaching programmes to cover learning gaps and address inequalities by using modern digital capabilities, which unfortunately do not exist.
rewrite: Friends, education. For us, education remains the most powerful tool for achieving social justice and enabling social mobility. You are well aware of the older generation: public education allowed the farmer's child in Epirus, the herder's son, to study during PASOK's prosperous years—to become a doctor, lawyer, or engineer, to create wealth and build a dignified family life. We have an obligation to reinforce every level of public education once more, ensuring all Greek children have free access to reduce disparities, not forcing them to rely on their grandparents' or parents' pockets for computer exams. Instead, they should look toward their future and their aspirations. Thus, for us, the vision for public education is paramount. Schools today must serve as a vital instrument for youth to engage with the digital world and sustainable development, providing equal opportunities to all young people, breaking down inequalities, and preparing them to face future challenges as both citizens and professionals. This requires a robust public school system and a strong public university. We recognize that the ideological policies of SYRIZA and, certainly, the policies of New Democracy, which seek to privatize education at every level, have deteriorated and weakened education in our nation. That is why it is now time for courageous decisions. Always in collaboration with educators, through increased public investment in education, aiming to gradually reach the average spending levels of European Union countries, our proposals center on enhancing quality by updating curricula and implementing the EU's 16 quality indicators, with remedial teaching programs to close learning gaps and tackle inequalities by leveraging modern digital tools—which, regrettably, are currently lacking.

text: So what are we saying? First of all, rents. In all urban centres, rents are rising. We are saying as in all serious European countries a social housing reservoir, 150,000 houses for 150,000 new couples, for poor Greeks with low rents to be built either by the Recovery Fund or with tax incentives and incentives for reconstruction, to open up old houses. Already in Thessaloniki, 15,000 have been registered in the houses. So if we give reconstruction incentives, zero ENVIA and low rent for 15 years, thousands of our fellow citizens will find cheap housing, they will have families and of course this will help the regions, the residential areas, with competition to bring down rents in general and not say, we will give you new property, as Mr Mitsotakis says, and young people will go and see that because of the cost per square metre they cannot join these programmes. Second issue. Very important. And probably to wrap this up and see the disregard for simple logic. The New Republic says they knew the problem and they are striving to solve it. I want you to know that in the Recovery Fund the Portuguese put 26,000 new houses. Billions of euros from Europe, not a penny of their own money. 20,000 Spanish, 10,000 Italians. Thousands of Germans. Thousands of Austrians. And Mr Mitsotakis, in contempt of the younger generation, put up 100 houses, 70 in Athens and 30 in Thessaloniki. This is the social face of the conservative party that disdains and disrespects the problems of the younger generation, pretending not to see the demographic projectile.
rewrite: So what is our message? First, regarding rents. Across all cities, rental costs are increasing. We propose, as in other serious European nations, a social housing reserve—150,000 homes for 150,000 new couples, intended for low-income Greeks at affordable rents. These would be constructed either through the Recovery Fund or via tax breaks and renovation incentives to revitalize existing properties. In Thessaloniki alone, 15,000 units have already been registered. By offering renovation incentives, zero ENFIA fees, and low rents for 15 years, thousands of our citizens can access affordable housing, start families, and support local communities. This approach fosters competition to lower rents overall, unlike proposals that offer new property—as Mr. Mitsotakis suggests—which often remain out of reach for youth due to high per-square-meter costs. Second, a critical point. To conclude and highlight the neglect of basic logic: New Democracy claims awareness of the issue and efforts to address it. Yet consider the Recovery Fund: Portugal allocated 26,000 new homes, Spain 20,000, Italy 10,000, plus thousands from Germany and Austria—all funded by European billions, without domestic spending. Meanwhile, Mr. Mitsotakis, showing disregard for the younger generation, pledged merely 100 homes: 70 in Athens and 30 in Thessaloniki. This reveals the conservative party’s social indifference, dismissing the challenges faced by youth and ignoring the demographic crisis.

text: They bluntly admit that the introduction of these systems "implies costly investments without bringing, in general, direct benefits to those who are called upon to bear the costs" and the conclusion of the Committee of Experts appointed by the government says more or less the same.As long as the criterion is the profitability of the conglomerates, the life of the workers, of the people will continue to be played at "dice". The wording of this Conclusion is typical. He writes: "It should be pointed out that the railways are a heavy system, requiring high investment, while at the same time having very low returns on invested capital, which are insufficient to attract the interest of the private sector"!We get it: The tragedy in Tempe has a cause and culprits! rewrite: They openly acknowledge that implementing these systems "entails significant investments without typically providing direct advantages to those who must cover the expenses," and the government-appointed Committee of Experts reaches a largely similar conclusion. So long as the focus remains on the profitability of large corporations, the well-being of workers and ordinary citizens will remain a gamble. The phrasing of this conclusion is characteristic. It states: "It must be noted that railways represent a capital-intensive system, demanding substantial investment while yielding very low returns on capital, which fail to attract private sector interest." The message is clear: The Tempe disaster has identifiable causes and those responsible! It stems from EU and governmental policies that "liberalize" transport, treating rail services as mere commodities to boost the earnings of corporate interests.

rewrite: Comrades, friends and allies. This evening, from Larissa, from this powerful assembly, we convey a message of confidence, of expectation, a message of resolute reinforcement for the KKE. text: So that is why we are committed here in Chania. That we will make health centers primary care throughout Greece. We will get a permanent staff of 15,000 doctors. We will raise the salaries of our health workers to the average of the European Union and we will include them in the heavy and unhealthy sector so that they get what they deserve and not just the clapping of the mockery in the middle of the Covid pandemic. Friends, you are well aware of what is happening in the health centres of Kandanos Kissamos in the Multipurpose Medical Centre of Sfakia. What we are saying about health is a priority and it is a priority that we cannot have millions of travellers in Crete and our islands every year, but the support given to the NHS does not take into account this great diversification of the population in the summer months. So we want a new health map that takes into account the real data of the EU age population, but also the changes that have to do with tourism in the summer. So we will support with 10%, 8-10% from the NHS Recovery Fund and not the 2-4% that Mr Mitsotakis has from the lowest rates across Europe. For one reason alone he does not want health as a social good. He wants health as a gift to powerful economic interests to speculate on the backs of the pensioner and the middle class. rewrite: That is why we are dedicated here in Chania. We will establish health centers as the foundation of primary care across all of Greece. We will secure a permanent workforce of 15,000 doctors. We will increase the salaries of our healthcare professionals to match the European Union average, and we will classify them within the heavy and hazardous occupations sector, ensuring they receive the compensation they merit—not merely the hollow applause offered during the Covid pandemic. Friends, you know well the situation at the health centers in Kandanos Kissamos and the Multipurpose Medical Centre of Sfakia. What we emphasize about health is a top priority, and it is critical that we cannot host millions of visitors in Crete and our islands each year while the support provided to the NHS ignores this significant seasonal population surge in the summer. Therefore, we advocate for a new health strategy that reflects the actual demographic data of the EU-age population, as well as the shifts linked to summer tourism. We will allocate 8-10% from the NHS Recovery Fund for support, not the mere 2-4% that Mr. Mitsotakis allocates, which are among the lowest rates in Europe. For one simple reason: he does not view health as a public good. He treats health as a concession to powerful economic interests, profiting at the expense of pensioners and the middle class. So, for the twenty-first, we stand for a robust NHS—not an NHS controlled by oligarchs to the detriment of the Greek people.

rewrite: In other words, fulfilling our initial four-year term, as I pledged from the start, allows us to demonstrate that our words carry weight. Similarly, our efforts reflect our commitment to implementing the agreements we have made with the public.

rewrite: It is recognized, even by those who do not share all our views, that beneath every struggle, no matter what obstacle you confront, you will find a communist—a steadfast fighter. text: Friends, farmers, farmers, livestock farmers, processors, the cost of production is rising. It is now very difficult to produce in Greece. What should we do? The Recovery Fund became a network, it became an investment in renewable energy, but not for five oligarchs who will be neglecting the cable from Crete to mainland Greece or who will be neglecting the networks of mainland Greece, but it became a plan where thousands of producers can make energy communities and have low production costs in the next 15 years. rewrite: Friends, farmers, livestock breeders, processors, production costs are increasing. It has become extremely difficult to produce in Greece today. What must we do? We must reduce energy costs. How can we achieve this? How do others manage it? The Recovery Fund transformed into a network, an investment in renewables, not for a handful of oligarchs who would neglect the Crete-mainland cable or Greece's mainland networks, but into a plan enabling thousands of producers to form energy communities and secure low production costs for the next 15 years. I pledge we will achieve energy democracy and energy justice, prioritizing energy communities. Connection priority will be granted to the nation's producers and Municipal Energy Communities. This is PASOK's duty: to work once more and serve the Greek people sincerely. Friends. We once said for farmers that blood is thicker than water. rewrite: Yet we remain steadfast in focusing on these matters, and we—both literally and metaphorically—value human lives. rewrite:

text: Friends. You know very well that a big part of the cost of living for students in many parts of Greece is rent, why is it rent? That nowadays, because of the rampant use of short-term rentals, without criteria, without conditions, without framework in urban centres, as is the case in other major European capitals or cities. And without having social housing programmes, you have left the poorest Greeks at the mercy of the rapidly rising cost of living in relation to housing. So that's why, by imitating models of other countries with socialist governments, democratic governments. I say we need to build a social housing program, a pool of 150,000 homes that are either newly built through the Recovery Fund. I want you to understand the evidence and Mr Mitsotakis' disdain for this problem. In newly built homes from the Recovery Fund. The Portuguese did 20,000. The Spanish did 11,000. The new democracy included 70 houses in Athens and 30 in Thessaloniki. This is contempt for the real problems of the people. So we say. Either newer in the Recovery Fund, or with tax incentives or incentives to build. Open up the closed houses in all the major cities of the country, join the social housing, the tank at low rent, so that 150,000 families and students can have cheap and decent housing in the coming years. These schemes are happening all over Europe. I see no reason why they should not also happen in Greece so that there is decent housing that will lead to a drop in overall rents in the country. And not to new ownership, as Mr Mitsotakis suggests.
rewrite: Comrades. You are well aware that housing expenses constitute a major portion of living costs for students across much of Greece. Why housing? Because today, due to the unchecked proliferation of short-term rentals—without standards, without regulations, without any urban planning framework in city centers, as seen in other major European capitals and cities. And in the absence of social housing initiatives, you have abandoned the most vulnerable Greeks to the swiftly escalating costs of accommodation. Therefore, following examples from nations with socialist and democratic administrations, I argue we must establish a social housing scheme—a reserve of 150,000 residences, either newly constructed via the Recovery Fund. I urge you to grasp the facts and Mr. Mitsotakis's disregard for this issue. Regarding new homes from the Recovery Fund: Portugal built 20,000. Spain built 11,000. New Democracy included 70 in Athens and 30 in Thessaloniki. This shows contempt for the genuine struggles of the populace. Thus, we propose: either new construction through the Recovery Fund, or through tax breaks and construction incentives. Unlock the vacant properties in all major urban centers, integrate them into the social housing pool for affordable rent, enabling 150,000 families and students to access inexpensive, adequate housing in the coming years. Such programs are widespread throughout Europe. I see no justification for their absence in Greece, which would ensure proper housing and contribute to lowering nationwide rental prices. And not toward new ownership, as Mr. Mitsotakis proposes.

text: Friends and friends, I did not and do not intend in such a beautiful, large gathering to bore you with a full account of the government's work.
rewrite: Friends and colleagues, I have no wish to weary you with a detailed report on the government's activities at this splendid and sizable assembly.

text: What did Mr Mitsotakis do? Yesterday Golden Dawn was condemned. Yesterday the murderers of Fyssa and the immigrants went to prison. Years have passed, I think. So that is why we do not receive lessons in progress, consistency and credibility from the left-wing chanting right-wing.
rewrite: What actions did Mr. Mitsotakis take? Golden Dawn was convicted just yesterday. Yesterday, the killers of Fyssa and the migrants were imprisoned. Several years have passed, I believe. So what did he accomplish throughout this time? Are you aware of his actions? He was focused on the polls. Mr. Mitsotakis would remark, "Kasidiaris is below 3%. It's acceptable for him to decline since the threshold for self-reliance is dropping further." Recently, noticing Kasidiaris's rise, he exclaimed, "Oh, achieving self-reliance is becoming tougher; they might enter parliament." The legislation targeting Golden Dawn is the work of Mr. Mitsotakis's New Democracy. But what about the Left under Mr. Tsipras—what is its role? I urge you to consider whether any other left-wing party in Europe holds the same stance toward Nazis as Mr. Varoufakis's Mera 25 and Mr. Tsipras's Syriza. One of them even made statements today? Ideally, they wouldn't exist, but they do. We cannot prohibit them from contesting elections, and Mr. Tsipras failed to enact the necessary law to stop Golden Dawn's resurgence. rewrite: Friends. To conclude, I wish to emphasize that our party, as you are aware, has built a foundation of trust with the public on vital national matters.
