I insisted, as our party has historically, on the need for German reparations, as decided by the Greek Parliament on 17/04/10 9 within a specific framework that all parties have a duty to fight for justice for the heroes who fought Nazism and are heroes that are recorded in the collective memory of every Greek. I did not expect one of Mr Mitsotakis' closest associates to say that this is a thing of the past. In a few days' time, the past will belong to Mr Mitsotakis and his entourage, who even despise the struggles of the Greek people. The difficult years of occupation.
He had the audacity, Mr. Skertsos himself a week ago to say that the New Democracy is the party that has always been on the right side of history. He seems to forget that it is the party that bankrupted Greece. It is the party that for many years did not allow a real assessment of why we got into the memoranda? The stork did not succeed in the memoranda or bankrupt New Democracy, but their audacity is common and that proves the common audacity of Syriza and New Democracy. In iconoclasm.
The judgments of the European Court of Human Rights in the person of Mr. George a statement of apology was not issued by the right, nor by SYRIZA, who for years now have been spraying the Greek people with conspiracy theories, instead of saying something simple, that in 2009 PASOK took in its hands a bankrupt Greece with the stamp of the right-wing party. But how can Mr Tsipras, who also gives me lessons in progress, say that?
rewrite:
Today. Today. Under the guise of simplicity or arrogance, the Mitsotakis system's disregard has crossed every line. I say this because recently I visited the martyr city of Kalavryta. I emphasized, as our party has always done, the necessity of German reparations, as mandated by the Greek Parliament on 17/04/2019 within a framework where all parties must strive for justice for those who resisted Nazism—heroes etched in every Greek's memory. I did not anticipate that a close aide of Mr. Mitsotakis would dismiss this as a matter of the past. Soon, that past will define Mr. Mitsotakis and his circle, who even scorn the struggles of the Greek people during the harsh occupation years.

Mr. Skertsos himself had the audacity just a week ago to claim that New Democracy has always stood on history's right side. He appears to overlook that it is the party that led Greece to bankruptcy. For years, it prevented a genuine examination of how we fell under the memoranda. The stork did not bring the memoranda or ruin New Democracy, but their boldness is shared, revealing the common audacity of Syriza and New Democracy in their iconoclasm.

The rulings of the European Court of Human Rights concerning Mr. George saw no apology from the right, nor from SYRIZA, which has long inundated Greeks with conspiracy theories rather than stating plainly that in 2009, PASOK inherited a bankrupt Greece stamped by the right-wing party. Yet how can Mr. Tsipras, who lectures me on progress, assert this?

text: Be well, thank you. Good race, good strength.
rewrite: Stay well, thank you. A fine race, strong performance.

text: All these proposals, both ND and SYRIZA, either from the position of the government majority or from the position of the opposition, rejected them in the name of the "strength of the economy"! At the same time, of course, the tax exemptions for strategic investors and "distressed" shipowners, the reduction of taxes on dividends of major shareholders, give and take, both with ND and SYRIZA.That is why you must reject the false dilemmas that the parties of capital are addressing to you during the election campaign. The growth they preach, capitalist growth, is neither for everyone nor can it be fair. For you, the stability of big capital's profits is accompanied by intensification with no return, daily insecurity, debts and new and repeated deadlocks. This is the permanent situation for every small business, in a system where the big fish lives and reigns by eating the small fish.
rewrite: All these proposals, whether from ND or SYRIZA, whether from the governing majority or the opposition, were dismissed in the name of "economic strength"! Meanwhile, tax breaks for strategic investors and "struggling" shipowners, along with reduced taxes on dividends for major shareholders, are exchanged and upheld by both ND and SYRIZA. That is why you must reject the false choices presented by the parties of capital during the election campaign. The growth they advocate, capitalist growth, benefits not all and cannot be just. For you, the stability of big capital's profits comes with relentless intensification, daily uncertainty, mounting debts, and recurring impasses. This is the enduring reality for every small enterprise in a system where the large predator thrives by consuming the smaller ones.

text: I don't want to talk about the many projects, about the construction site that we have turned the country into, about the reforms that we have brought, about the fact that this Parliament, which is being dissolved today, look, has passed 423 laws.
rewrite: "I prefer not to discuss the numerous initiatives, the nationwide construction efforts we've undertaken, the reforms we've implemented, or that this Parliament, now being dissolved, has enacted 423 laws."

text: And my last commitment, non-negotiable: a strong Greece. The continuation of our defence planning. 68 arms projects that are being implemented and a consistent policy on migration, accompanied by parallel European initiatives.
rewrite: "And my final pledge, non-negotiable: a robust Greece. The continuation of our defense strategy. 68 military projects currently underway and a steadfast migration policy, supported by coordinated European actions."

text:
Friends,
compañeras and comrades
There are only a few days left until the opening of the ballot box on May 21 and there are days when a lot more can be done by the members and friends of the KKE, in order to take the Party as high as possible. With the ballot papers for each constituency in hand in the days that remain until the last minute, we are organizing an even wider opening to the people and the youth.
Home to home in the districts, post to post in the places of work and study, man to man everywhere, to carry the Party's call for an even stronger JCP, so that the people themselves will be strong on the next election day.
rewrite:
Comrades,
friends and allies
Only a few days remain until the polls open on May 21, and in this time, much more can be achieved by the members and supporters of the KKE to elevate the Party to its greatest possible strength. With the ballot slips for every district in hand, right up until the final moment, we are planning an even broader outreach to the people and the youth.
Door to door in the neighborhoods, station to station in workplaces and schools, person to person in every corner, to deliver the Party's appeal for a more powerful KKE, ensuring the people themselves stand strong on the coming election day.

text: Friends, there are only 6 days left. I am addressing all generations here from Thessaloniki and I am really happy because all generations are here today. It is the generation of 114, it is the generation of the founding of PASOK, it is the generation of the 1980s, it is the generation of the 1990s and it is the generation that will renew and make the democratic party a protagonist again. So I am addressing every democrat and every progressive who believes deeply in the rule of law, who believes deeply in respect, in human rights, who believes deeply in sustainable development, who believes deeply in social justice, come together to make our house strong again, because this house is the one that Eleftherios Venizelos founded and Andreas Papandreou re-founded in 1974. It is the house of democracy, it is the house of dignity, it is the house of hope, it is the house of perspective. Come together. Raise proudly the green flag of PASOK. Come together. May 21, may the sun of hope, the sun of social justice, the sun of individual dignity rise again. PASOK is here with each and every one of us as protagonists because we are a people's movement. All together we will fight the fight. All together, in every village, in every city, in every workplace. All together. We have only 6 days. Lift up the responsibility, lift up the need to re-embrace the struggles, the hopes. The patriotic movement of the democratic party is here to turn the page for our country, for a better future. Fight, fight, fight and on May 21 we will be victorious. May 21 the clocks of history turn back and show that the time of the people's movement has come, the time of the democratic party has come. Good strength and good fight.
rewrite: Friends, only six days remain. I speak to all generations gathered here in Thessaloniki, and I am truly glad to see every generation present today. It is the generation of '14, the generation that founded PASOK, the generation of the '80s, the generation of the '90s, and the generation that will renew and restore the democratic party as a leading force. So I call on every democrat and every progressive who deeply believes in the rule of law, in respect, in human rights, in sustainable development, in social justice—unite to strengthen our house once more, for this is the house Eleftherios Venizelos built and Andreas Papandreou rebuilt in 1974. It is the house of democracy, of dignity, of hope, of perspective. Come together. Raise high the green flag of PASOK. Come together. On May 21, may the sun of hope, the sun of social justice, the sun of personal dignity rise again. PASOK stands here with each of us as leaders, because we are a people's movement. Together we will wage this battle. Together, in every village, every city, every workplace. Together. We have just six days. Take up the duty, embrace again the struggles and the hopes. The patriotic movement of the democratic party is here to turn the page for our nation, for a brighter future. Fight, fight, fight, and on May 21 we will triumph. On May 21, let the clocks of history turn to show the hour of the people's movement has arrived, the hour of the democratic party has come. Good strength and good fight.

text: Friends, What does all the above prove?That the "tsunami" of auctions and losses of family property will continue, after the elections, whatever government is formed. That the people's homes can only be saved by the popular uprising and that is why a strong KKE is needed to organise the popular counter-attack. This state appears incapable of protecting the first home and securing our right to housing. All governments appear incapable of ensuring civil protection so that we stop burning in the summer and drowning in the winter!In fact, the state and its governments are too capable of ensuring the profits of the conglomerates and for the same reason they sacrifice our needs. The present state is hostile to us because it is the state of the dictatorship of capital. And this does not only concern the most obvious aspects, such as the undermining of strikes and the repression of demonstrations. It is about all aspects of our lives.
rewrite: Comrades, what does all this demonstrate? That the "wave" of foreclosures and loss of family assets will persist after the elections, regardless of which government takes power. That only through a popular uprising can people's homes be protected, which is why a strong KKE is essential to organize the people's resistance. This state seems unable to safeguard primary residences and guarantee our housing rights. All governments appear incapable of providing civil protection to prevent summer wildfires and winter floods! In reality, the state and its governments are quite capable of securing profits for big business, and for that very reason, they neglect our needs. The current state is antagonistic toward us because it serves the dictatorship of capital. This affects not just the most visible issues, like undermining strikes and suppressing protests, but every aspect of our lives.

text: And speaking of costing. How much do the parties of capital cost the life of the people here in Western Greece, who live in a region that is at the centre of the US-NATO plans, under the responsibility of all governments. With Aktion, Araxos, Andravida becoming daily potential targets of retaliation by the opposing imperialist camp. They have already been silenced. They do not make a sound about them. Because they know that everything they said about the country's security from NATO membership has long since collapsed.
rewrite: "And on the subject of expense. What price do the factions of capital exact from the lives of the people in Western Greece, an area central to US-NATO designs, with every government bearing responsibility. With Aktion, Araxos, Andravida turned into daily potential targets for retaliation by the rival imperialist bloc. They have already been muted. They utter no word about them. Because they understand that all their claims about national security through NATO have long since crumbled."

text: Something else very important: the regeneration of our shipyards and the Greek Defence Industry. Because for us, the non-negotiable condition of economic prosperity is the defence of national sovereignty. We do not take a single step back from our national rights.
rewrite: Another crucial point: revitalizing our shipyards and the Greek defense sector. For us, safeguarding national sovereignty is an indispensable prerequisite for economic prosperity. We will not retreat one inch from our sovereign rights.

text: But, friends, let's go to our programme that wants to give a new breath to the Greek economy. The programme, the social democratic programme, the programme of Democratic Socialism, the programme that reduces inequalities and creates opportunities and hopes for all Greek children, for all families. One promises things that cannot be done and the other hides what is going to happen with his budgetary choices. They boast about growth, about good statistics, when in reality our performance is unfortunately negative, as the OECD figures show. More than two and a half million Greeks are currently threatened with poverty and social exclusion, according to official figures. They praise that they reduced taxes, but the taxes paid by citizens in 2022 were 5 billion more than the targets. If this is not overtaxation, what is it? And even more so if we put on the table that most of these taxes are due to VAT consumption and special taxes that beat up the weakest, the workers, the unemployed and the middle class. They say they have increased the minimum wage by 20% and dispute the OECD figures of a 7.4% reduction in real wages. Unemployment, they say, is falling, but the new jobs are mostly €400 part-time jobs. This growth that has Mr Mitsotakis' name on it is creating real estate with internal loans. In a few years, with this policy, we will be foreigners in our country. Students will not be able to rent a house with dignity in the centre of Thessaloniki and the centre of Athens. Young couples will not be able to build their future with dignity and have children. And on the other hand, Mr Tsipras thinks that the economy is a cow that gives out milk without ever being fed.
rewrite: "Yet, comrades, let us turn to our plan that aims to breathe new life into Greece's economy. This social democratic agenda, the program of Democratic Socialism, seeks to lessen disparities and open doors of opportunity and hope for every Greek child and family. One side pledges the impossible, while the other conceals the consequences of its fiscal decisions. They tout growth and favorable statistics, yet in truth our outcomes remain regrettably poor, as OECD data confirms. Official numbers reveal over 2.5 million Greeks now face the risk of poverty and social marginalization. They boast of tax cuts, but citizens paid €5 billion more in taxes in 2022 than planned. If that isn't over-taxation, what is? Especially when most of this burden comes from VAT and excise duties that hit the most vulnerable—workers, the jobless, and the middle class—the hardest. They claim a 20% rise in the minimum wage, yet contest OECD findings of a 7.4% drop in real wages. Unemployment may be falling, they say, but many new positions are merely part-time roles paying €400. This growth stamped with Mr. Mitsotakis' name is fueling a property bubble with domestic credit. Under such policies, in a few years we may become strangers in our own land. Students won't afford decent rentals in central Thessaloniki or Athens; young couples will struggle to build a dignified future and raise children. Meanwhile, Mr. Tsipras seems to view the economy as a cow that yields milk without ever needing feed."

text: Compañeras and comrades, Friends and friends, With today's event and especially with the daily and tireless action of thousands of members of the KKE and the KNE, we are strengthening the thread that unites us with those who sacrificed for a world without exploitation of man by man, for socialism - communism. The dead workers of Chicago in 1876, the apology of Spice, the attitude and the shocking last notes of the 200 communists before their execution in Caesarian, the dead men and women workers at Fourmee in Northern France on May Day 1891 are among the many historical lessons that inspire us, mobilise us, to face with the same vigour, with the same pride, the onslaught of the authoritarian state, of the unaccountable employer. To hold high the flag of the interests of the working class against its exploiters, against the imperialists who are bloodying the planet. It is a guide of inspiration for the working people to bring to the fore the satisfaction of their modern needs, to fight for the wealth produced and stolen by a handful of parasites.
rewrite:
Comrades and friends,  
Through today's gathering and above all through the constant, dedicated efforts of thousands in the KKE and KNE, we are reinforcing the bond that links us to those who gave their lives for a world free from human exploitation, for socialism-communism. The Chicago workers slain in 1876, the defiance of Spice, the stance and the stirring final words of the 200 communists executed at Kaisariani, the laborers—men and women—killed in Fourmies, northern France on May Day 1891, stand among the many historical examples that motivate us, that drive us to confront with equal determination and dignity the assault of the authoritarian state and the unanswerable employer. To raise high the banner of working-class interests against its oppressors, against the imperialists who are drenching the planet in blood. It serves as an inspiring compass for working people to push forward the fulfillment of their contemporary needs, to struggle for the wealth created and seized by a handful of parasites.

text: So the Greece of 2023 is nothing like the Greece of 2015-2019. Then we had closed banks, zero growth. On the contrary, today, the country is growing at three times the rate of Europe. Our investments exceed 15 billion a year. The Greek economy came out of surveillance, it was upgraded 12 times.
rewrite: Thus, the Greece of 2023 bears no resemblance to the Greece of 2015-2019. Back then, banks were shuttered and growth was stagnant. In contrast, today the nation is expanding at triple Europe's pace. Our annual investments surpass 15 billion. The Greek economy has exited surveillance and been upgraded twelve times.

text: It is true that here in Fthiotida we have met again and again with the mass organizations of the people of the prefecture, of Fthiotida, with the unions of the workers of LARKO, the self-employed professionals, with the associations of farmers, with the health workers, with the committees of the flood victims. We listened and made their problems, their demands and their claims known throughout the country. We committed ourselves to fight with all our strength for them both in and out of Parliament and in the next Parliament. For example, we discussed with the representatives of the professionals of Lamia, of the very small businesses in the city, the problems they face, the effects of the price of energy and raw materials, and the debts that are piling up again. But also about the situation faced by a small business when its main provider, the people's family, is called upon day after day to cut back even on the basics in order to make ends meet.
rewrite: Indeed, here in Fthiotida, we have repeatedly gathered with the mass organizations of the prefecture's people, with the unions of LARKO workers, self-employed professionals, farmers' associations, healthcare workers, and committees of flood victims. We listened and broadcast their problems, demands, and claims nationwide. We pledged to fight vigorously for them, both inside and outside Parliament, and in the upcoming Parliament. For instance, we conferred with representatives of Lamia's professionals and small city businesses about their challenges: the impact of energy and raw material costs, and the mounting debts. We also addressed the plight of small businesses when their primary customers, ordinary families, are forced daily to cut back on essentials to survive.

text: But, listen. Nikos Kazantzakis wrote, "Lies are an anandry." That is why I am here not for promises, but for words, few and good, that are translated into actions. You will not hear lies from me.
rewrite: "Yet, consider this. As Nikos Kazantzakis observed, 'Lies are a form of impotence.' That is precisely why I stand before you not for pledges, but for words—sparse and true—that become deeds. You will hear no falsehoods from me."

text: And of course, the issue of refugee migration is also very important. Mr Mitsotakis went to Evros. And he took pictures at the fence. I remember that when PASOK started this project. Mr., then Mr. Samaras was saying that this is a meme-centric diversionary game to change the agenda and now they are running around taking pictures. So we have clear positions, there are borders at sea and everywhere and we have a duty to guard the country's borders. The country is not a closed vineyard, but... We understand. The farmer, the stockbreeder, the processor. Who sees today in the trees of Ilia, Crete, Messinia, the fruit rotting because there are no workers damaged by the policies of Mr. Mitsotakis. So I will say, for us there is no black or white, there is only. the foreground. We want. The country's commitments to be honoured regarding the refugee issue. When it comes to migration, there are borders. The country must not relive 2015. The only winner was Erdogan, who blackmailed the whole of Europe and we paid for it, as did other European nations. But we need a coherent immigration policy. What do our hotels need? Our economy, Our peasantry and get a coherent immigration policy, as all European countries have done without populism and cheap communication games. This is exactly what I represent. I represent the anxiety of every Greek woman and every Greek man for Greece to become a normal European country and not to be a hostage to the elitism of Mr Mitsotakis. And the populism of Mr Tsipras. This is what the Greek people deserve, nothing less.
rewrite: "Of course, the matter of refugee migration is also crucial. Mr. Mitsotakis visited Evros and had photos taken at the fence. I recall when PASOK initiated this project, Mr. Samaras at the time called it a meme-centric diversion to shift the agenda, and now they are the ones posing for pictures. Thus, our stance is clear: borders exist at sea and everywhere, and we have an obligation to protect the nation's boundaries. The country is not a closed vineyard, but... We comprehend. The farmer, the livestock breeder, the processor—who now sees fruit rotting in the orchards of Ilia, Crete, and Messinia due to labor shortages worsened by Mr. Mitsotakis's policies. So I will state, for us there is no black or white, only the immediate priority. We demand that the country's commitments on the refugee issue be upheld. Regarding migration, borders must be respected. Greece must not repeat 2015. The sole victor was Erdogan, who blackmailed all of Europe, and we bore the cost, as did other European nations. Yet we require a consistent immigration policy. What do our hotels need? Our economy, our agricultural sector—they need a coherent immigration policy, as all European nations have implemented, free from populism and shallow media tactics. This is precisely what I stand for. I voice the concern of every Greek woman and man for Greece to become a normal European country, not held captive by the elitism of Mr. Mitsotakis or the populism of Mr. Tsipras. This is what the Greek people merit, and nothing less."

text: Friends, neo-democrats from Chania and Crete, I always say that I prefer comparison to confrontation with our opponents. But there is an opposition to our own dense work and the clear objectives I have just mentioned.
rewrite: Friends, neo-democrats of Chania and Crete, I often remark that I favor comparison over confrontation with our rivals. Yet, there exists opposition to our intensive efforts and the precise goals I have just outlined.

text: Yes, the government of the Southwest all these four years, counting profits and losses for capital and business groups, that's why it passed one unpopular bill after another, implementing one by one the demands of the monopolies for greater profitability, what they themselves call "a friendly environment for investment"! SYRIZA and PASOK were also counting profits and losses, which is why the former supported 50% of the former and 70% of the latter, the bills of the New Democracy. If today Mitsotakis boasts about high growth rates and more investments, he hides the fact that they have stepped on the crushed labour rights and the squeezing of workers, while he does not say a word about the worrying signs that show that a new crisis is just around the corner.And all those promises he makes about wage increases and tax cuts will be measured with the same yardstick, that of profits!  So he adds: "If and when the fiscal, the strength of the economy allows it", i.e. the profits of the capitalists. May you live to eat clover, that is...
rewrite: Indeed, over these four years, the Southwest government has consistently prioritized the gains and losses of capital and business interests, leading to the enactment of numerous unpopular bills. These measures have systematically fulfilled the monopolies' calls for enhanced profitability, touted by them as "creating an investment-friendly climate"! Both SYRIZA and PASOK similarly weighed profits and losses, which explains why the former backed 50% and the latter 70% of New Democracy's legislative proposals. When Mitsotakis now touts high growth rates and increased investments, he conceals how they have trampled on eroded labor rights and intensified worker exploitation, while ignoring alarming indicators that a fresh crisis looms near. All his pledges regarding wage hikes and tax reductions will be judged by the same metric: profitability! Hence, he qualifies: "If and when fiscal conditions and economic strength permit," meaning the capitalists' profits. May you live to see better days, as the saying goes...

text: Even on the issue of professional contributions, ND and SYRIZA are practicing an unacceptable blackmail: either high contributions in order to get a relatively decent pension in old age, or lower contributions in order to finally get starvation pensions. However, the immediate demand of all employed professionals, of all pensioners, is that all anti-insurance laws be repealed here and now and that generous increases be given here and now, for decent pensions. This demand is supported by the KKE in all tones.
rewrite: On the matter of professional contributions, ND and SYRIZA are engaging in an unacceptable form of blackmail: either pay high contributions for a somewhat adequate pension later, or pay lower contributions and ultimately face meager pensions. Yet, the urgent demand from all working professionals and all pensioners is the immediate repeal of every anti-insurance law and the immediate provision of substantial increases to ensure decent pensions. The KKE firmly supports this demand in every possible way.

text: Thank you from the bottom of my heart. Fly the flags of the New Democracy and of our country. Let us send from here, from Crete, the message of the great victory.
rewrite: From the depths of my heart, I thank you. Raise high the banners of the New Democracy and of our nation. From this place, from Crete, let us proclaim the message of a momentous triumph.

text: A power in which the universal right to free public education is guaranteed, to pre-school education to support especially young parents of couples who are constantly living in insecurity and are being driven to depopulation, even the population of the country. Similarly, a power that guarantees the right to free health care by upgrading the existing hospital infrastructure, with an integrated primary health care system that does not depend on the pots and pans of donors and benefactors. As happened here in Thessaloniki, where the construction of the paediatric hospital, which the city so badly needs, has been frozen because the sponsor has withdrawn.
rewrite: A power that ensures the universal right to free public education, extending to pre-school education to particularly aid young parents in couples enduring persistent insecurity and facing depopulation pressures, even affecting the nation's population. Likewise, a power that secures the right to free health care by enhancing current hospital infrastructure, through an integrated primary health care system independent of the whims of donors and benefactors. As seen here in Thessaloniki, where the building of the paediatric hospital, urgently required by the city, has been halted due to the sponsor's withdrawal.

text: Friends, compañeras and compañerosWhat has been written on the pages of history in blood cannot be erased with dirty ink. No matter how many millions the EU spends, no matter what the parties of the system do, in our country the unhistorical theory of two extremes, unfortunately for them, remains a minority.And even if some candidates of the New Democracy (ND) are humiliated in the panels, saying that "the KKE is an anti-democratic party and should not participate in the elections"! Let them go with them to have some coffee...And even if Mr. Tsipras in Sibiu, Romania, signing, together with Merkel, Orban, Kurz and other "fiddlers" of the far right, anti-communist declarations with references to the "iron curtain", the terminology used by the extraordinary military courts in our country to send communists, fighters, to the detachment.
rewrite:
Comrades, friends and allies  
What history has inscribed in blood cannot be overwritten with tainted ink. No matter the millions spent by the EU, nor the maneuvers of establishment parties, the unhistorical notion of two extremes remains, to their dismay, a minority view in our land.  
Even when certain New Democracy candidates are disgraced in debates, claiming “the KKE is undemocratic and should be barred from elections”—let them go share a coffee together…  
And even as Mr. Tsipras in Sibiu, Romania, joins Merkel, Orbán, Kurz and other far‑right “fiddlers” in signing anti‑communist declarations that invoke the “iron curtain”—the very phrase used by the extraordinary military tribunals in our country to condemn communists and fighters to exile.

text: Why, what did I tell you here about our Crete, about the major projects that we are launching, four years ago? The motorway, ports, airports, safe transport and boosting tourism. Irrigation projects to support production and our villages. And thirdly, culture and greenery for a better life in our cities.
rewrite: "Why, what did I mention here regarding Crete, about the key initiatives we began four years ago? The highway, seaports, airports, secure transit, and enhancing tourism. Water management schemes to aid agriculture and rural communities. And third, cultural and environmental efforts for improved urban living."

text:

rewrite:
"And all this, while just a bit farther in the heavily impacted Castelli region, financing from major developers and the new airport's proprietors pours in freely and grows, alongside the devastation of the locale.
The scheme is clear. Disposing of the "bir para" people's assets and transforming the zone from farmland into a property market. text: Friends. The institutional changes. Many institutional changes are needed. The support of public education. Public school, public university, so that all Greek children have equal opportunities, the knowledge and skills necessary to meet modern challenges. By introducing remedial teaching to tackle inequalities, but also by upgrading special education structures for a real school of inclusion and not only, allowances which, unfortunately, are not enough for a decent everyday life for families with children who have learning disabilities or are on the autism spectrum. Emphasis on the vocational training school, extramural universities linked to the labour market and, of course, to the local economies and the specificities of local economies for those universities located in the periphery, with specific funding for research and innovation always. Around the level of the European Union average. We are much lower and this shows a huge weakness in research and technology development in the country. Also construction of new quality student residences so that young people can pursue their dreams, achieve their goals without doing computerised courses that prioritise their family's financial ability. Today you know all too well that in many universities it is very difficult to study because of the cost of living. So we have a vision to create modern dormitories where all children. Of weak families to make decisions based on their ambition and not on their financial ability. George said about social mobility. And I think someone George probably said about the issues. Of inherited power and someone else said about social mobility. We're living in the age. Of increased spatial mobility of geographic mobility, but at the same time it's the age of low social mobility and this is of course happening all over the western world. So that is why, because we have lived through the years of economic crisis have left many traumas behind, our priority is through public education at all levels. To enable every Greek child to build a dignified future in Greece.
rewrite: Friends. Institutional reforms. Numerous institutional changes are required. Strengthening public education. Public schools, public universities, to ensure all Greek children have equal opportunities, the knowledge and skills needed to confront contemporary challenges. Through implementing remedial teaching to address inequalities, and by enhancing special education frameworks for a truly inclusive school—not merely providing allowances, which sadly are insufficient for a decent daily life for families with children facing learning difficulties or autism spectrum conditions. Focus on vocational training schools, extramural universities connected to the job market and, naturally, to local economies and their unique characteristics for those universities in regional areas, with dedicated funding for research and innovation consistently. Aiming for the European Union average level. We are significantly below, revealing a major weakness in national research and technological advancement. Additionally, building new, high-quality student housing so young people can pursue their aspirations, achieve their objectives without relying on distance learning that favors their family's financial situation. Today, it is widely known that studying at many universities is very challenging due to living expenses. Thus, we envision establishing modern dormitories where all children from disadvantaged families can make choices based on ambition, not financial capacity. George spoke of social mobility. And I believe someone, likely George, addressed matters of inherited privilege, and another discussed social mobility. We live in an era of heightened geographic and spatial mobility, yet it is also a time of limited social mobility, a trend occurring across the Western world. Therefore, because we have endured years of economic crisis leaving many scars, our priority is to use public education at every level to empower each Greek child to construct a dignified future within Greece.

text: Friends, here in Thessaly, I cannot fail to mention the tragedy of Tempi. A tragedy that is engraved in the heart of the Greek people. 57 people lost their lives in a violent and sudden manner. Because our state is not a normal European state that protects the citizen, that has transport with security, transparency in institutions and meritocracy. It is a state that after the tragedy, instead of hearing an apology and justice doing its job, to find out how this disputed stationmaster came to be in this position and we were listening to Mr Georgiades and Mr Voridis telling us that the transfer of the disputed stationmaster was legal, and a week ago the committee appointed by Mitsotakis himself, the three-member committee, came out and said that the transfer of the stationmaster was illegal because he had exceeded the age limit. Have you heard any apologies from Georgiades and Voridis? Why has SYRIZA stopped talking about the tragedy of Tempi? Because quite simply, on 21 October 2021, in Mr Karamanlis' drawer there was a conclusion from the transparency authority that we submitted to Parliament during the controversial procedure. What did that report say? That since 2014, 9 years, certain persons in the Ministry and in the OSE did not allow telecommanding when the Contract said that it had to be completed in 2 years and even when all the 55 million euros of the project were all European money and not even 1 euro of tax of the Greek people. So what did justice do? It never got hold of the conclusion and when we asked Mr Karamanlis why the judiciary had not got hold of the conclusion, he replied boldly that even he did not know of the existence of the conclusion that the transparency authority had submitted to his Ministry. Well, this is the Greece we need to change, the Greece of the client state and of widespread corruption and contempt for the public interest.
rewrite: Friends, here in Thessaly, I must speak of the Tempi tragedy. A tragedy etched into the soul of the Greek people. 57 lives were violently and suddenly lost. This is because our state is not a normal European state that safeguards its citizens, ensures secure transport, transparency in institutions, and meritocracy. It is a state where, after the tragedy, instead of hearing an apology and seeing justice served—to uncover how this controversial stationmaster came to be appointed—we listened to Mr. Georgiades and Mr. Voridis claim the transfer was legal. Yet, just a week ago, the committee appointed by Mitsotakis himself, the three-member committee, stated the transfer was illegal due to an age limit violation. Have any apologies come from Georgiades or Voridis? Why has SYRIZA ceased discussing the Tempi tragedy? Quite simply, because on 21 October 2021, in Mr. Karamanlis' drawer, there was a finding from the transparency authority that we submitted to Parliament during the contentious process. What did that report reveal? That for 9 years, since 2014, certain individuals in the Ministry and OSE obstructed telecommanding, despite the Contract stipulating completion within 2 years—even though all 55 million euros for the project were European funds, not a single euro from Greek taxpayers. So what did justice do? It never obtained the finding, and when we asked Mr. Karamanlis why the judiciary hadn't accessed it, he brazenly replied that even he was unaware of its existence, though the transparency authority had submitted it to his Ministry. This is the Greece we must change: a Greece of clientelism, rampant corruption, and disregard for the public interest.

rewrite: Today the citizens of Chania are delivering their own resounding message of hope. A declaration of self-assurance, a proclamation of triumph, so that Constantine and Helen may rejoice in blue. Blue will not merely color Crete; it will spread across all of Greece. The entire nation.

rewrite: Whatever we recall, one truth stands out: Every smile, every shiver, every moment of hope and optimism, every gain during the four years of the anti-popular government in the South-West, the KKE played a part. text:
Friends and friends,
compañeras and comrades

rewrite:
Friends and allies,
compañeras and comrades

text: Just before the national elections, I can't stop talking about the National Health System that was born by PASOK, George Gennimata and Paraskevas Avgerinos. We created the National Health System, we have a duty to revive the National Health System. But how? Private health care spending is. rewrite: Just ahead of the national elections, I cannot help but speak about the National Health System established by PASOK, George Gennimata, and Paraskevas Avgerinos. We founded the NHS, and it is our responsibility to restore it. But how? Private healthcare expenditure is soaring. PASOK is here to repair the NHS, to mend public education, and to reconstruct the welfare state that will ensure the reduction of contemporary inequalities in our country. Only 2 to 4% of this fund is allocated by Mr. Mitsotakis for healthcare. rewrite: Friends. Comrades, we observed that on Monday Mr. Tsipras also came to our city. He even gave a speech here, near the statue of Ares in People's Square. rewrite: Friends, compañeras and compañeros. text: Friends, that is why I call on every Greek to choose between a state of opacity, patronage for the blue children, for the cronies of Mr.Tsipras, a state of meritocracy, transparency and respect for institutions, or a state of social injustice that implements policies that make the rich richer, or a state with justice and strong health and public education. Between a state that hands over the toil, the sacrifices of the Greek people through their red loans to the speculators of the funds, and a state that ensures the fair regulation of the private debt of households and businesses. Friends, Mr Mitsotakis. He touts himself as a champion of stability. He talks of paralysis when his track record includes the interception or capture of the rule of law, the blue children, the widening of social inequalities and he states clearly that he will hold elections as many times as necessary until he himself is elected Prime Minister. But he is probably not so sure of his strategy, because he said a moment ago that he will eventually use the first mandate. So let the Greek people see who has a firm position to govern the country? I have been talking for a year now about stability and progress since the first mandate, or Mr Mitsotakis, who has been talking about second and third elections, but in the face of deadlock, his staff say that he will use the first mandate. We will hear a lot because they understand quite simply that things are not that simple. For his part, Mr Tsipras voted for the simple proportional representation. What does simple proportional representation mean throughout Europe? It means that the parties that have 151 seats work together. But he is talking about a special simple proportional representation that in order to cooperate in the electoral system that he voted for he has to be the first party, do you know what that proves? That the real concern of the leader of Syriza is not to get rid of New Democracy and Mitsotakis, but to save his own political future.
rewrite:
Friends, this is precisely why I urge every Greek to decide: between a state of obscurity, of favors for the privileged few and the associates of Mr. Tsipras, or a state built on merit, transparency, and respect for our institutions. Between a state that perpetuates social injustice, enacting policies that enrich the wealthy, or a state grounded in fairness, with robust public health and education. Between a state that surrenders the hard work and sacrifices of the Greek people—through their red loans—to speculative funds, or a state that guarantees the fair settlement of private debt for households and businesses.

Friends, Mr. Mitsotakis presents himself as a pillar of stability. He speaks of paralysis, yet his record involves undermining the rule of law, favoring insiders, and deepening social divides. He openly states he will call elections repeatedly until he becomes Prime Minister. Yet he seems uncertain of his own plan, having just mentioned he might eventually accept the first mandate. So let the people see clearly: who offers a steadfast plan to lead the country? For a year, I have spoken of stability and progress from the very first mandate. In contrast, Mr. Mitsotakis talks of second and third elections, though his team now suggests he may use the first mandate. We will hear much more, as they are beginning to realize the situation is not so straightforward.

As for Mr. Tsipras, he supported simple proportional representation. Across Europe, this means parties with 151 seats collaborate. Yet he advocates a peculiar version where, to cooperate under the system he endorsed, his party must come first. Do you know what this reveals? That the true priority of the Syriza leader is not to defeat New Democracy and Mr. Mitsotakis, but to secure his own political survival.

text: A modern state must also effectively protect human rights. We did not imagine a few years ago that this issue would be so high on our priorities. We thought that the country after the years of post-independence had overcome these evils, these incredible and unbelievable distortions. In the end we were wrong, which is why we are proposing to upgrade the role of independent authorities to monitor and submit rules both to the state and to the markets. We created the independent authorities. We still support them today, and it is really outside the European framework the unethical attacks that are being made both by Mr Mitsotakis's system and against Mr Tsipras's system in the past on people who are fighting to keep Greece anchored in European values, and this shows that they are not politicians who really believe in these values, they are just ready to instrumentalise everything just for power, just for the chair. And that is one reason why this party will be the democratic party throughout time. I want to tell you that this is why I am committed to repealing the provisions of the New Democracy Act on the issues of the wiretapping cover-up. A substantive role in the DPA decisions on legal intercepts. Commission of Inquiry without the abuse of secrecy. And of course, a law that allows victims to be informed and not over a three-year period, so that the person who has committed the crime can be in civil protection for an extended period of time. Strengthening the independence of the judiciary, and it is sad that even today in the latest reports of the European Commission and the European institutions, this thing is put as a priority for Greece. We have a duty to strengthen the independence of the judiciary. That is why we say that the selection of its supreme leadership must be made by Parliament with an increased majority.
rewrite: A modern state must also effectively safeguard human rights. A few years ago, we did not anticipate this issue would rise so prominently on our agenda. We believed the nation, after the post-independence era, had moved beyond such grave and astonishing distortions. Ultimately, we were mistaken, which is why we advocate enhancing the role of independent bodies to oversee and propose regulations for both the state and the markets. We established these independent authorities. We continue to support them today, and it is truly outside European norms—the unethical assaults launched by Mr. Mitsotakis's system and previously against Mr. Tsipras's system on individuals striving to keep Greece aligned with European values. This reveals they are not politicians genuinely committed to these values; they are merely prepared to exploit anything for power, for the seat of authority. That is one reason this party will endure as the democratic party. I wish to emphasize that this commitment drives me to revoke the provisions of the New Democracy Act concerning the wiretapping cover-up. A meaningful role in the Data Protection Authority's decisions on lawful intercepts. An investigative commission free from secrecy abuses. And certainly, a law enabling victims to be informed promptly, not over three years, so that perpetrators cannot remain shielded under civil protection indefinitely. Strengthening judicial independence is crucial, and it is regrettable that even now, in the latest European Commission and institutional reports, this remains a priority for Greece. We have an obligation to fortify the judiciary's independence. Hence, we assert that the selection of its highest leadership must be conducted by Parliament with an enhanced majority.

text: We're talking about strengthening the special education structures to have the real school of inclusion.I go to many parts of Greece and I meet parents with children who have learning difficulties, who are on the autism spectrum and they say, you know, I have a fear and I'm talking about people 45, 50 years old. text: Friends, production. There cannot be a strong welfare state without strong production. rewrite: Comrades, production. A robust welfare state is impossible without robust production. Therefore, we social democrats prioritize sustainable development, a resilient Greece, a productive Greece. Our focus is ensuring 'Made in Greece' becomes a rallying cry to bolster domestic production across all sectors. Primary sector, agri-food, manufacturing, extroversion—'Made in Greece' everywhere. How will this be achieved? We cannot evaluate tourism solely by visitor numbers. We must establish other metrics. It is one matter to host 10 million visitors and another to generate 20 billion. It is another to welcome 20 million and still earn 20 billion. It is yet another to reach 30 million and double the country's GDP contribution. Are we assessing the added value of the current Greek tourism model? We do not aspire for Greece to become a vast hotel. We have different ambitions. And what are they? Quality tourism with tangible outcomes, where annually we track what share of travelers consumed domestic goods and how these products, in subsequent months, reach shelves in the European Union or third countries from Arabia to America. Why have the Portuguese succeeded, as the Spaniards did by emulating the Italians and the Portuguese by following the Spaniards? Thus, we cannot replicate something that is sound, that respects the environment and humanity. Must we live a decade hence as strangers on our own islands? No, we reject this distorted development model. So we intend all this to form a cohesive package of forward-looking policy that honors the Greek citizen, respects the environment, and values the nation.

text:

rewrite:
The sole genuine benefit these elections can bring our people is a significantly stronger KKE! text: Friends. I want to dwell a little on our national issues. It is for us, this patriotic movement party, PASOK, a very critical position of our political opponents on national issues. And I also want here from Ilia. To make the Greek people remember. To stimulate the intelligence of the Greek people and make them remember. Which party is the one that, on the big national issues with Turkey and the Balkans, has had stable and reliable positions for decades? And which parties are the ones that said other things before the elections, but then made compromises wishful thinking afterwards? With a specific strategy, we brought Cyprus into the European Union in 2004, making the island fully secure against Turkey's challenges with the Cyprus problem unresolved. What did our political opponents do?  Mr Tsipras. He went to Germany last. And he saw Mr. Solts. I did not hear him say the word arms embargo on Turkey's provocations, but we heard him say about the so-called new Aegean Prespa agreement he has not yet made sense of the previous Prespa agreement. So he needs to explain to the Greek people who his interlocutor will be, because he says that if the situation with Erdogan changes and the others come in, that is, Mr Kilindzaroglu, we can do the Prespes Aegean agreement. But Mr Kilidzaroglu, Mr Tsipras. He has made stronger challenges to our islands than Mr Erdogan. So what is the plan of this agreement? Shall we tell it during the election so that the Greek people know it? What are the positions of all parties on these important issues that concern not one generation but many generations to come?
rewrite: Friends. I wish to focus briefly on matters of national importance. For our patriotic movement, PASOK, the stance of our political rivals on these national issues is deeply concerning. And I also wish here, from Ilia, to remind the Greek people. To awaken the discernment of the Greek people and remind them. Which party has maintained steadfast and dependable positions for decades on major national matters concerning Turkey and the Balkans? And which parties spoke differently before elections, only to engage in wishful compromises afterward? Through a clear strategy, we secured Cyprus’s entry into the European Union in 2004, ensuring the island’s full protection against Turkey’s threats while the Cyprus issue remained unresolved. What did our political opponents do? Mr. Tsipras. He recently visited Germany. And he met with Mr. Scholz. I did not hear him mention an arms embargo regarding Turkey’s provocations, but we heard him speak of a so-called new Aegean Prespa agreement, though he has yet to fully grasp the previous Prespa agreement. Thus, he must explain to the Greek people who his counterpart would be, as he suggests that if the situation with Erdogan shifts and others, like Mr. Kılıçdaroğlu, come to power, we could reach a Prespes Aegean agreement. But Mr. Kılıçdaroğlu, Mr. Tsipras, has issued stronger challenges against our islands than Mr. Erdogan. So what is the plan for this agreement? Should we disclose it during the election so the Greek people are informed? What are all parties’ positions on these critical issues, which affect not just one generation but many to come?

text: The increase in rents, mortgage interest and taxes in recent years completes this nightmare scenario, which plunges popular households into uncertainty and despair. And these increases are not going to stop, they will continue. The ECB has already proceeded to raise the base rate by 4% in a year, in order to curb the galloping inflation in the Eurozone. To curb inflation, which the EU's own policy in the previous period increased by borrowing to provide large state packages to support its conglomerates and manage the crisis. It has been shown once again that any medicine for one symptom of the great patient, capitalism, becomes a poison for the other. There is no magic formula for the pro-popular transformation of a rotting system. The increase in the ECB interest rate, among other things, leads to a constant increase in mortgage rates. Thus, from 1.5% in 2021, the interest rate on a mortgage loan could exceed 4.5% this year.
rewrite: The recent surge in rents, mortgage interest, and taxes completes this nightmare, pushing ordinary households into uncertainty and despair. These increases show no sign of halting; they will persist. To combat soaring inflation in the Eurozone, the ECB has already raised the base rate by 4% within a year. This inflation was partly fueled by the EU’s own earlier policies, which borrowed heavily to fund large state support packages for its conglomerates and manage the crisis. Once again, it is clear that any remedy for one symptom of the ailing patient—capitalism—turns into poison for another. There is no miraculous solution for transforming a decaying system in favor of the people. Among other effects, the ECB’s rate hike drives mortgage rates steadily upward. Consequently, from 1.5% in 2021, mortgage loan interest could surpass 4.5% this year.

rewrite: Observe the developments unfolding around us in Chania. Projects surpassing 60 million in value. text: We are already seeing the results of this policy. 10.4 billion euros were in 2022 the net profits of only 150 business groups of those listed on the stock exchange, an increase of 303% compared to the previous year. rewrite: The outcomes of this policy are already evident. In 2022, merely 150 listed corporate groups reported net profits of 10.4 billion euros, a surge of 303% from the year before. Soon he may suggest we disregard it, as if families were waiting for the OECD to confirm what they already feel when entering the supermarket with heavy hearts.

text:
In particular, on the crime of auctions itself, we are witnessing a recital of hypocrisy and deception by ND, SYRIZA and PASOK. Together they all want to hide the fact that auctions will continue and increase after the elections, no matter which government is formed. Their phony confrontation tries to cover up the fact that they are all complicit in the crime, that they all together shaped and imposed the reactionary framework that puts the noose around the people's necks. So let's see what the truth is and how we got here.
The original law that was supposed to protect the first home during the era of the memoranda was the Katseli law of the PASOK government. The former PASOK minister herself has explained the benefits for the banks of this law. She has stated that it initially preserved the value of the properties in the domestic banks' portfolios, which would have collapsed if all the auctions had proceeded massively and abruptly, and that at the same time the banks secured a large part of the loan repayments.
rewrite:
Specifically regarding the crime of foreclosures, we are seeing a performance of hypocrisy and deception by ND, SYRIZA, and PASOK. Collectively, they aim to conceal that foreclosures will persist and intensify after the elections, regardless of which government takes shape. Their sham conflict attempts to mask their shared complicity in this crime, as they jointly crafted and enforced the regressive framework that tightens the noose around the people's necks. Therefore, let's examine the truth and how we arrived at this point.
The initial law intended to shield primary residences during the memorandum period was the Katseli law under the PASOK administration. The former PASOK minister herself has detailed this law's advantages for the banks. She noted that it initially maintained the property values in the portfolios of domestic banks, which would have plummeted if all foreclosures had occurred massively and suddenly, while simultaneously ensuring banks received a significant portion of loan repayments.

text: There will be a balanced development of construction to meet the needs of housing, infrastructure projects, support for industrial and agricultural production. Human-friendly cities will be formed, with sufficient green lungs and zones of popular sports and cultural activity. Integrated plans will be implemented for the management of water resources, waste and civil protection, with the development of modern standards and regulations. More generally, spatial planning will be based on scientific research to diagnose new social needs. All this can be done immediately, as soon as the people realise their power and decide to walk the path of subversion, hand in hand with other peoples. And the power of the people is proven in all cases: From the villages saved from the fires in Evia, in the Peloponnese, in Mytilene, to the great wave of solidarity with the peoples of Syria and Turkey after the recent earthquakes. This supremacy of the new society of socialism, to provide a radical solution to the question of housing and other popular problems, is illuminated by the contemporary subversive power programme of the KKE.
rewrite: Construction will advance in a balanced manner to address housing demands, infrastructure initiatives, and support for industrial and agricultural production. Cities designed for people will emerge, featuring ample green spaces and areas for widespread sports and cultural engagement. Comprehensive strategies will be applied to manage water resources, waste, and civil protection, alongside the advancement of modern standards and regulations. More broadly, spatial planning will rely on scientific study to identify emerging social requirements. All this can be achieved promptly, once the people recognize their strength and choose to pursue the path of transformation, alongside other nations. The people's power is evident in every instance: from communities rescued from wildfires in Evia, the Peloponnese, and Mytilene, to the massive solidarity shown for the peoples of Syria and Turkey following recent earthquakes. This dominance of the new socialist society, offering a fundamental resolution to housing and other common issues, is highlighted by the current transformative program of the KKE.

text: Another point of our programme. Tax system. As Social Democrats we serve the policy of progressive taxation, fair, progressive taxation. rewrite: Another key element of our platform is the tax system. As Social Democrats, we advocate for a fair and progressive taxation policy. Our current focus is on lowering labor taxes to foster quality employment, and reducing VAT on essential food items. Regarding the energy and economic crisis, we need strong market regulations to curb excess. Our market is not yet mature; speculation is too rampant, prices surge quickly and fall slowly due to ineffective market mechanisms. We must cap retail energy prices and slash by 50% the excessively high tax-free threshold for parental benefits. I emphasize this because a mere 5% reduction won't turn 4.8 million into 2,400. We propose lowering the limit from 800,000 to 400,000 to truly support the vulnerable and middle class, countering the New Democracy government's creative accounting that labels a 4.8 million euro tax-free parental benefit as social justice. This benefits not the common people but the elites that Mr. Mitsotakis's New Democracy dutifully represents. We must stop this disregard for the public good. Additionally, we advocate for a gradual, progressive rise in the tax rate on distributed dividends—currently among the lowest in the EU—and an extraordinary tax on excess profits of banks and large firms in monopolistic sectors. Other nations have taken similar steps when faced with widening gaps between deposit and mortgage rates. When we proposed this a year ago, we were called populists, yet when banks offered selective relief to a few borrowers as an election favor to Mr. Mitsotakis, it was deemed sound policy. Sadly, it appears powerful financial interests strongly desire this government's continuity solely because it poses no hindrance to their staggering accumulation of financial influence.

text: Friends, education. There is no other tool for social democrats, for a society of social mobility, for a society of low inequalities, if there is no strong public education. So what do we propose? A national baccalaureate. There is a huge talk about the base 10. Is that the only problem? Mr Tsipras is trying to fish in murky waters. Did any young people hear that no exams will get them into universities. But I must tell the restless youth that nowhere in the world do they get into universities without any exams at all. Let Mr Tsipras drop the mockery. No more mockery for young people too. It is a disgrace to not honour the young people of our country. So what is the national diploma? A national baccalaureate is not judging your future on an exam, with all that it means for the psychology of the student and the family. It is decided in the last 2 years by multiple exams and post-university options, where not only one exam but also the grade of the diploma plays an important role. What is the goal of this change? To take the focus off of tutoring and put the focus back on public school so that all students have adequate knowledge, adequate skills, and are competitive with a future perspective. Friends, and of course, with strong remedial teaching for all. And finally, strong special education structures everywhere. Only in this way will a socialist party create an inclusive school and all children of all Greeks will be able to participate equally with any learning difficulties in this strong public school. It is our commitment, as is the increase in teachers' salaries and real evaluation, not evaluation by second-raters, as imposed by the New Democracy party-state. Friends, outward-looking universities. What does an extroverted university mean? It is a university that is linked to innovation, to research, a university without family rule, a university that does not argue about the university police.
rewrite: Comrades, education. For social democrats, for a society with social mobility and reduced inequality, there is no alternative to robust public education. So what is our proposal? A national baccalaureate. Much is said about the base 10. Is that the sole issue? Mr. Tsipras is attempting to fish in troubled waters. Have young people heard that no exams are needed for university entry? Yet I must inform the anxious youth that nowhere in the world is university admission granted without any examinations. Let Mr. Tsipras end the mockery. No more mockery toward our youth either. It is shameful not to respect the young people of our nation. So what is this national diploma? A national baccalaureate does not determine your future through a single exam, with all the psychological strain that places on students and families. It is assessed over the final two years through multiple examinations and post-secondary pathways, where not just one test but also the diploma grade carries significant weight. What is the aim of this reform? To shift focus away from private tutoring and back onto public schooling, ensuring all students gain sufficient knowledge and skills, becoming competitive with future prospects. Comrades, and certainly, with robust remedial instruction for everyone. And lastly, strong special education frameworks in all areas. Only through such measures can a socialist party build an inclusive school where every child, regardless of learning challenges, can participate equally in this strengthened public education system. This is our pledge, alongside raising teachers' salaries and implementing genuine evaluation—not the inferior assessments enforced by the New Democracy party-state. Comrades, universities with an outward focus. What does an extroverted university entail? It is a university connected to innovation and research, free from dynastic control, a university that does not debate over campus security forces.

text: Why were the people's households burdened with so many debts to the state, to the tax authorities, to the social security funds, to the banks? Why so many red mortgages? This is why tax debtors alone exceeded 4 million under the SYRIZA government and are increasing under the ND government. This is also why the home ownership rate is steadily falling in Greece from 84% in 2005 to 73% today. rewrite:
Why are so many households weighed down by debts owed to the state, tax offices, social security funds, and banks? Why are there so many foreclosures? Why can’t people afford their rent and utility bills?  
The reason is the systematic assault on people’s incomes carried out by every government—past and present—which drains the public to serve the interests of capital and meet EU obligations. The cause lies in the memorandum and post-memorandum policies jointly advanced and enforced by ND, SYRIZA, and PASOK, working hand in hand.  
That is why tax debtors alone surpassed 4 million under SYRIZA and continue to rise under ND. It also explains why homeownership in Greece keeps declining—from 84% in 2005 to 73% today.  
Policies that slashed wages and pensions, eroded social security rights, raised unfair indirect taxes, and increased the overall tax burden have driven ordinary households into this plight. The ruthless pursuit of budget surpluses has brought the people to their knees.

text: What should we do; not to make the same mistake that we made with the energy and I want to be precise. Some people from Syriza and New Democracy cannot say. What should we do? Our generation from natural gas, which is not our own but an imported fuel. rewrite: How can we avoid repeating the error we made with energy—and I must be clear. Certain individuals from Syriza and New Democracy cannot speak to this. What should we do? And naturally, regarding natural resources for irrigation projects—building irrigation systems in Rhodope and Xanthi, supporting livestock farming, and establishing the pilot livestock park, all of which rank among our priorities.

rewrite:
Comrades, friends and allies,

rewrite:
Yes! We lived through the youth struggles. The students' fight for safety measures in schools. The students' efforts to bar university police from entering campuses. All the young people who turned away from petty squabbles over trivialities and took to the streets to ensure the premeditated crime in Tempe is never forgotten. So that human lives would no longer be weighed against profit.

We witnessed the students' major victory in last year's student elections, which shattered the ruling GOP and placed the KNE party in first after 36 years. Last year, a step was taken. Tomorrow, in the student elections, let the leap happen, despite the rigging frenzy by the GOP and other unfit groups. The youth must send an unmistakable message, 11 days before the parliamentary elections. It will resound once more: All-University Leading Force! And it will deliver the fitting reply to those who believe they can purchase the youth's conscience with a couple of ferry tickets to a Cycladic island, as Mitsotakis attempts during the campaign.

text: Just reading the headlines, one understands that despite their quarrels, despite their differences, they can form a government on May 22. So let one of them, Mitsotakis, with his self-reliance, and the other, Tsipras, with his allegedly progressive government, leave the blackmailing dilemmas about ungovernability. And he even has the audacity to call on the KKE "to take responsibility"! We could say a lot but we don't need to... Only what is well known to the workers, the breadwinning farmers and self-employed, the young children and women here in Larissa, in the whole of Thessaly. When SYRIZA, together with ND and PASOK, was counting profits and losses for capital during these four years, we, the KKE, were counting human lives. That is why we went to every workplace, in every town and village, in schools and colleges to organise the struggle of the workers, the people and the youth.We have taken on this great responsibility and we continue on this road with even greater determination, stubbornness and militancy. That is why today more and more people are thinking of supporting and voting for the KKE. Because they now see that a strong KKE means a strong people.
rewrite: Just from scanning the headlines, it's clear that despite their disputes and disagreements, they can establish a government by May 22. So let Mitsotakis, with his overconfidence, and Tsipras, with his so-called progressive administration, abandon their coercive scenarios about political paralysis. He even dares to urge the KKE "to assume responsibility"! Much could be said, yet it is unnecessary... Only what is already clear to the workers, the struggling farmers and independent professionals, the youth and women here in Larissa, across all of Thessaly. While SYRIZA, alongside ND and PASOK, was calculating profits and losses for big business over these four years, we, the KKE, were tallying human lives. This is why we reached every worksite, every city and hamlet, every school and university to mobilize the fight of the laborers, the populace, and the young. We have embraced this immense duty and we persist on this path with even stronger resolve, tenacity, and combativeness. This is why today, a growing number consider backing and casting their vote for the KKE. Because they now recognize that a powerful KKE signifies a powerful people.

text: This implies the investment grade. And keep my commitment from here, from Egaleo: if a strong government of the New Democracy emerges - which it will - the investment grade will be a reality before the end of the year. But, beware, with one condition that is in our hands: the stability and the prospects of the country, something that will only be guaranteed by a strong and experienced government on May 21.
rewrite: This suggests an investment grade rating. I reaffirm my pledge from Egaleo: if a robust New Democracy government is formed—and it will be—the investment grade will be achieved by year's end. However, note one condition within our control: the nation's stability and outlook, which only a strong, experienced government on May 21 can secure.

text: We have understood, of course, that Tsipras is not doing very well with history anyway. Now he has remembered again, as he does every time we have elections, to dig up the slogan "what a Plastira, what a Papagos", in order to mock the KKE. We inform him and his ilk that this slogan is historically justified.If he wants to know why, let him visit the school "Belogiannis", here in Kallithea, where the prison from which 71 years ago the Plastira government and its friends, the "devilishly good" of Mr. Tsipras, the Americans, took Nikos Belogiannis and his comrades and led them to the firing squad.And let them stop saying that Plastira and some of his ministers tried but failed to save Belogiannis! Even so, it makes their responsibility for the heinous crime more serious...Let alone that with some far-right associations that Mr. Tsipras has lately and there in Menidi or even before that in Kastoria, it is up for discussion whether he feels more like a political descendant of Plastira or Papagos...So let him stop scratching on the goo of the shepherd...
rewrite: We have long recognized that Tsipras struggles with historical accuracy. Now, as he does whenever elections approach, he has revived the slogan "what a Plastira, what a Papagos" to ridicule the KKE. We remind him and his supporters that this slogan is historically grounded. If he wishes to understand why, he should visit the "Belogiannis" school here in Kallithea, where the prison from which, 71 years ago, the Plastira government and its allies—the very "devilishly good" Americans admired by Mr. Tsipras—seized Nikos Belogiannis and his comrades, leading them to execution. They should cease claiming that Plastira and certain ministers attempted but failed to save Belogiannis! Even if true, it only deepens their culpability in this grave crime... Given Mr. Tsipras's recent affiliations with far-right groups in Menidi or earlier in Kastoria, it is debatable whether he aligns more with the political legacy of Plastira or Papagos... So let him refrain from stirring up old grievances.

text: To impose the reinstatement of the collective bargaining of the National General Collective Agreement as a starting point for raising the minimum wage by adopting the demands of the trade unions for increases above 850 euros and the simultaneous reinstatement of the three-year minimum wage. This practically means that a worker with a three-year contract will see his or her salary increase to 935 euros today and not in 2027 as promised by the ND. This proposal is linked to the other proposals of the KKE for a fixed daily working time, 7 hours, 5 days, 35 hours and no unpaid overtime, with the reintroduction of Sunday-working time. It is linked to the proposal for an inflation-based wage adjustment clause. With the restoration of the 13th and 14th salaries in the public sector, about which the Southwest and Syriza do not say a word, and the granting of all salary scales. With a strong KKE and mass workers' struggles we can impose the restoration of the sectoral Collective Labour Agreements and their compulsory nature without terms and conditions, which is a basic condition for increasing wages in all scales. This is the only pro-people's answer to the lies of the New Democracy, Syriza and PASOK that the average wage will supposedly be increased without repealing the laws that have undermined the Collective Labour Agreements.
rewrite: To reinstate the National General Collective Agreement's collective bargaining as the foundation for boosting the minimum wage, incorporating union demands for raises exceeding 850 euros and the immediate restoration of the three-year minimum wage. This ensures a worker on a three-year contract will receive a salary of 935 euros now, not by 2027 as pledged by the ND. This initiative aligns with KKE's additional proposals for a fixed workweek: 7 hours daily, 5 days, totaling 35 hours, eliminating unpaid overtime and reinstating Sunday work. It connects to the call for wage adjustments tied to inflation. It also involves reinstating the 13th and 14th salaries in the public sector—a topic ignored by Southwest and Syriza—and applying all salary scales. Through a robust KKE and widespread worker mobilizations, we can enforce the revival of sectoral Collective Labour Agreements, making them unconditionally mandatory, a key step for wage growth across all levels. This stands as the sole pro-people rebuttal to the falsehoods from New Democracy, Syriza, and PASOK, which claim average wages will rise without overturning the laws that have weakened Collective Labour Agreements.

text: I met some old friends on the way in. They may remember that I made my first political appearance here in Egaleo exactly 20 years ago, in April 2003. Since then you have surrounded me with your trust. I thank you from the bottom of my heart.
rewrite: "On my way in, I encountered a few old friends. They might recall that I first entered the political stage here in Egaleo precisely two decades ago, in April 2003. From that moment on, you have consistently placed your trust in me. For that, I am deeply and sincerely grateful."

text: No. The struggling people did it without expecting anything from above. It did it by looking where the struggle is organized, in the unions, in the associations, in the struggle committees. rewrite: "No. The struggling masses achieved this without anticipating any assistance from above. They accomplished it by focusing on where resistance is coordinated—within unions, associations, and struggle committees. They did so through daily combat against this brutal policy and the repression that follows it. Through defiance and noncompliance with unjust laws. By asserting their rights. text: So here it comes for all this and more the know how you know what you have to do so next Sunday to achieve much more together. All of you know that things. They are not stagnant.
