rewrite: So here it is: for all this and more, you know what must be done this coming Sunday to accomplish far greater things together. Everyone understands that circumstances are not fixed. That every individual’s input into our shared endeavor amplifies our power and can truly matter. You are aware that the vote in the C.C.E. has the potential to shift the tide, to create a Monday on May 22nd that stands apart from all previous days. Thus, we earnestly reach out to all who are considering, in these final voting days for the CEC, yet may still feel uncertain. To all who have Mr. C.E. among their options, but remain undecided. text: And I will not deal with the divisive "Polakism", which is the other face of Mr.Tsipras. I want to keep the image of my country high. I will not deal with the money trees he has rediscovered. 45 billion he is handing you, which can only lead to two possibilities: either a new tax raid, or bankruptcy and a new memorandum. But this is what Vincent Cornaros has long since replied to: 'He who speaks lies is spoken without a man'.
rewrite: "And I will not engage with the divisive 'Polakism', which represents the other side of Mr. Tsipras. I aim to uphold the dignity of my nation. I will not address the money trees he claims to have found. The 45 billion he is distributing can only result in two outcomes: either a fresh wave of taxation, or financial collapse and another memorandum. Yet, as Vincent Cornaros aptly responded long ago: 'He who tells lies is left without an audience'."

text: From the Western Sector, then, and from its seven municipalities, I start our struggle - municipalities which I know very well, I have walked them for 20 years, Agia Varvara, Agioi Anargyros, Kamatero, Egaleo, Ilion, Peristeri, Petroupoli, Haidari - so that this area becomes the starting point of our victorious journey.
rewrite: "Thus, from the Western Sector and its seven municipalities—which I know intimately, having walked them for two decades: Agia Varvara, Agioi Anargyros, Kamatero, Egaleo, Ilion, Peristeri, Petroupoli, Haidari—I launch our struggle, so this region may serve as the starting point for our victorious journey."

text: Because a vote for the KKE is a vote that is incompatible with submission, with the unpopular one-way system that this system cultivates. It is a vote of punishment to those who have brought us to this point and are preparing a similar continuation. It is a vote to expose the truth about everything that is happening against our people. It is a vote of honesty and confidence in the power that the people and the youth hold in their hands. Most of all, a vote for the KKE is a vote of hope and optimism to strengthen the struggle for an overall better life. It is the only vote that will cut the wind out of their sails, but will give a broader uplift to our people. It is the ballot with the hammer and sickle of hope, pride and honesty.
rewrite: A vote for the KKE stands against submission and the unpopular, one-way path fostered by this system. It serves as a rebuke to those who led us here and plan more of the same. This vote reveals the truth behind all that is being done against our people. It is a ballot of integrity and trust in the power held by the people and youth. Above all, a vote for the KKE is one of hope and optimism, strengthening the fight for a comprehensively better life. It is the sole vote that will deflate their ambitions while lifting our people higher. It is the ballot marked by the hammer and sickle—symbolizing hope, pride, and honesty.

text: So now, strong JCE. So that we can fight these battles from better positions. To prevent them from squeezing out victories, to finally pave the way for the radical changes we all long for. Because now we know better than ever. That only the people save the people when they take the road of conflict, the road of subversion. We proved it in the pandemic and in the great struggles. To save human lives, to support the hospitals and their staff. We proved it in the fires, in the floods, in earthquakes, in the great workers' struggles, such as in COSCO, in the e-food couriers, in the heroic Malamatina workers who did not bend with the support of all the people. And so many other struggles across the country. Now this slogan takes on a new meaning. The people should massively support their party, the KKE.
rewrite: Now, a robust JCE is essential. This enables us to confront these struggles from more advantageous positions, to block their attempts to secure victories, and ultimately to clear the path for the profound transformations we all desire. We understand now more clearly than ever: only the people can save the people when they choose the path of confrontation, the path of overturning the existing order. We demonstrated this during the pandemic and in major battles—to protect lives, to back hospitals and their personnel. We proved it in fires, floods, earthquakes, and in significant workers' fights, like at COSCO, among e-food couriers, and with the heroic Malamatina workers who stood firm with the people's solidarity. Countless other struggles nationwide echo this. Now, this call gains renewed significance: the people must rally en masse behind their party, the KKE.

text: See, for example, health. Maybe in the pandemic, the National Health System held up, had more ICUs, many more health workers, but our health has been the big patient for decades. That is why I am not satisfied with the steps we have taken forward. We need to make leaps, especially in our hospitals, especially in our emergency departments and in the prevention of serious diseases.
rewrite: Consider health, for instance. While the National Health System may have endured the pandemic with expanded ICUs and more medical staff, our overall health has been the true long-term patient. This is precisely why I find our progress insufficient. We must achieve significant advances, particularly within our hospitals, emergency rooms, and in preventing major illnesses.

text: The big construction groups are literally getting rich with the support of the state: Through concession contracts, PPPs, preferential terms for the tendering of large projects, even with bonuses of tens of millions of euros when they are not late in implementing their contractual obligations. But do all of us, the employed and self-employed, tenants and those who are struggling to repay their mortgages, really have any reason to continue on the path that has brought us to our current situation? We must and can think in terms of the experience we have accumulated over the years, in terms of what life itself has taught us. And life proves time and again that the class bias of government policy is always determined by the needs of capital and the steely laws of profit. Life proves that no matter how many governments change, the train of bourgeois governance is and will continue to move firmly on the tracks set by the ruling class and the EU's commitments. Let us consider that the current, dead-end road for us is not, after all, a one-way street as it is presented to us. To think outside the blinders, outside the walls of the current rotten system. We argue that there is a way out, socialism!
rewrite: Major construction firms are effectively amassing wealth with state backing: via concession deals, public-private partnerships, favorable bidding conditions for major projects, and even multi-million euro bonuses for meeting contractual deadlines. Yet do the rest of us—employees, freelancers, renters, and those straining under mortgage debt—truly have cause to stay on the course that has led us here? We should and can reflect based on the lessons gathered over time, on what lived experience teaches. And experience repeatedly shows that government policy’s class slant is always shaped by capital’s demands and the rigid logic of profit. It shows that regardless of how many administrations shift, the engine of bourgeois governance remains steadfast on rails laid by the ruling class and EU obligations. Let’s recognize that this current, hopeless path for us is not, in fact, a one-way street as portrayed. To see beyond the blinders, beyond the walls of this decayed system. We contend there is an alternative: socialism!

And all of us on the other hand who are fighting the daily struggle of dignity and survival, who fight every day every hour to keep our family standing, who have nothing but our minds and hands but who have in each other and all of us the power of the world to change this society. Can have a better future our people with their struggle with the KKE together can make it happen.
rewrite: Alone. On one side, they with their profits and losses, their bureaucrats and political agents, mired in corruption and scandal, undercutting each other and keeping watch. And on the other side, all of us, fighting the daily battle for dignity and survival, struggling every hour to keep our families afloat, possessing nothing but our minds and hands, yet holding within each other and together the power to transform this society. So, alone and yet all of us. And the many will prevail with a strong, formidable Mr. Epsilon. Why our country? It can have a better future; our people, through their struggle alongside the KKE, can make it happen.

text: Friends, in closing. I will say a word about Greek-Turkish relations, because next week we will know. Who will be the leader of the neighbouring country? We aspire and hope that above all, peace, stability, respect for good neighbourliness, respect for human rights, respect for international law, that a leadership will emerge that has all these characteristics. I do not see who that leadership is. On the one hand, Erdogan has spots that make Thrace blush. Western Thrace and the islands of the northeastern Aegean. On the other hand, Mr. Kilincaroglu is on a rally of threats and tensions with Greece, saying things about the Aegean islands. Mr. Tsipras goes to Germany and talks about the Aegean pressures to Chancellor Schulz with another leadership. Does Mr Tsipras have to explain to the Greek people before 21 May what he means by Aegean presses, why Andreas Papandreou, Andreas Papandreou and Aegean presses? And especially when we have these 2 options from the Turkish leadership, I cannot understand neither what he means nor how any convergence will take place. We obviously want a Turkey that respects its own people and its neighbours, which is why our priority when we are at this level of meetings with foreign heads of state is to talk about a unified European foreign policy that sends clear messages to Turkey and about another issue, the Euroarmy, so that the Greek people stop paying billions to the Europeans, while at the same time they are arming Turkey. The Eurostrike is an issue not only of Greek national sovereignty. It is an issue of security and social justice for all European peoples. So that Estonians, Finns and Greeks can feel secure. The Cypriots and all the European peoples of the periphery, and not for some to pay billions, for others to plunder and at the same time for Turkey to have the courage to challenge neighbouring countries. Let what happened in Ukraine be a lesson to them. We have a consistent attitude and now it is unthinkable. When in Ukraine SYRIZA played Pontius Pilate; now with Turkey thinking it has easy and magical solutions in its pocket and even going abroad without any such national understanding to invoke such scenarios.
rewrite:
Friends, in conclusion, I will address Greek-Turkish relations, as next week we will learn who will lead the neighboring country. We hope for a leadership that prioritizes peace, stability, good neighborliness, human rights, and international law—qualities I do not clearly see in the current options. On one side, Erdogan has actions that embarrass Thrace, both Western Thrace and the northeastern Aegean islands. On the other, Mr. Kilincaroglu engages in rhetoric of threats and tensions toward Greece, particularly regarding the Aegean islands. Meanwhile, Mr. Tsipras travels to Germany, discussing Aegean pressures with Chancellor Schulz under a different leadership. Shouldn’t Mr. Tsipras clarify to the Greek people before May 21 what he means by Aegean pressures, and why Andreas Papandreou is referenced in this context? Given these two Turkish leadership prospects, I find it hard to grasp his intentions or how any agreement might be reached.

We clearly desire a Turkey that respects both its citizens and its neighbors. That is why, in meetings with foreign leaders, our focus is on advocating for a unified European foreign policy that delivers clear messages to Turkey, and on advancing the Euroarmy initiative. This would prevent Greeks from paying billions to Europe while it simultaneously arms Turkey. The Eurostrike matter extends beyond Greek sovereignty; it is a question of security and social justice for all Europeans, ensuring that Estonians, Finns, Greeks, Cypriots, and other peripheral nations feel safe. It is unjust for some to fund billions while others exploit resources, emboldening Turkey to challenge its neighbors. Let Ukraine’s experience serve as a warning. We maintain a steadfast stance, and it is now inconceivable that, as in Ukraine where SYRIZA avoided responsibility, Turkey should believe it holds simple, miraculous solutions, or that anyone would propose such scenarios abroad without national consensus.

text: Friends. Justice. Justice is the great issue for our people. In every company, in every conversation there is desperation for justice. It has been ingrained in people from all corners of the country that justice does not exist and does not work. That no matter what the powerful do and while powerful and financially and politically powerful they will never pay and take their responsibilities while the people have no chance. So I want to say to you here from Larissa that we have a duty to build a new relationship of trust with the Greek people, and how is this relationship being built? When you respect justice, when you respect people, when you speak the language of truth and do not disregard their logic. So I want to tell you that there is no chance of me betraying any of you, because every day the relationship of honesty that I am building with the Greek people is getting stronger. I could not imagine my closest associate being convicted 13-0 by the Special Court, like Mr Pappas, Mr Tsipras' best friend, and instead of sending him home I would have him on the PASOK ballot papers. I could not imagine a close relative of mine being a protagonist in this corruption, like Mr Mitsotakis' nephew, and not being brought to justice. This is not a normal European country. I pledge to you that just as PASOK built the Greece of the 20th century, the Greece that demolished the post-civil war state, I pledge to you that together with all of you we will build the European country of the future, the strong Greece for all Greeks. In this party there will be no Patsy's in this party who will take the loans of the Greek people, disregarding their interests. In this party no corruption will ever again be tolerated. Together we will change the country, together we will change all the bad things and we have a duty to confront all the powerful interests that do not allow our country and the new generation to stand on its feet.
rewrite: Friends. Justice. Justice is the central concern for our citizens. In every workplace, in every discussion, there is a deep yearning for justice. People across the nation have come to believe that justice is absent and ineffective. They feel that the powerful, those with financial and political influence, evade accountability and avoid responsibility, while ordinary people are left without recourse. Therefore, I declare to you here in Larissa that we have an obligation to establish a new bond of trust with the Greek people. How is this bond formed? By honoring justice, by respecting the people, by speaking truthfully and acknowledging their reasoning. So I assure you, there is no possibility of me betraying any of you, because each day the sincere connection I am forging with the Greek people grows stronger. I could never conceive of my closest aide being unanimously convicted by the Special Court, as was Mr. Pappas, Mr. Tsipras' closest friend, and instead of dismissing him, placing him on PASOK's electoral lists. I could never imagine a close relative of mine being a central figure in such corruption, like Mr. Mitsotakis' nephew, and not facing legal consequences. This is not the standard of a normal European nation. I promise you that just as PASOK constructed the Greece of the 20th century, the Greece that dismantled the post-civil war establishment, I vow that together with all of you, we will build the European country of the future, a robust Greece for every Greek. In this party, there will be no scapegoats who burden the Greek people with debts, ignoring their welfare. In this party, corruption will never again be accepted. Together we will transform the country, together we will rectify all that is wrong, and we have a duty to challenge all entrenched interests that hinder our nation and the new generation from standing firm.

text: Seventeen SYRIZA cuts replaced increases - I see among us many friends I have known for many years, many of you are pensioners - 1.6 million of our fellow citizens saw the first pension increases in 12 years, almost 8%. And those who were wronged by the Katrougalos personal differential were boosted by EUR 200-300 and I pledge that they will continue to be supported until the Katrougalos personal differential is finally erased.
rewrite: Seventeen SYRIZA reductions were substituted with raises - I observe many longtime friends among us, numerous pensioners included - 1.6 million citizens experienced the initial pension boosts in 12 years, close to 8%. Those disadvantaged by the Katrougalos personal differential received an extra EUR 200-300, and I commit to sustaining their support until that differential is fully eliminated.

text: Do we want a government that will win in the rough and tumble or one that will shipwreck in the rough and tumble? Do we want a desperate homeland or an armored homeland? Do we ultimately want a leader with a voice abroad or a voiceless guest with a mind at home? In other words and very simply: Do we want New Democracy with Prime Minister Mitsotakis or do we want Syriza with Prime Minister Tsipras? This is the central question to which citizens will answer on May 21.
rewrite: Should we desire a government that triumphs in the fray, or one that founders in the tumult? Do we seek a homeland in distress or one that is fortified? Ultimately, do we want a leader who speaks with authority on the global stage, or a silent figure confined to domestic concerns? Put plainly: Do we choose New Democracy under Prime Minister Mitsotakis, or Syriza led by Prime Minister Tsipras? This is the pivotal question citizens will address on May 21.

text: Friends, four years ago some people told us that "the sea has no borders". And so, more than a million migrants were ploughing the land. However, that land of the "open vineyard" no longer exists. Illegal flows are being prevented, and in spite of those voices - I will say it again here, from the other side of Greece - the fence on Evros is being extended. And, indeed, under the seal of Europe, which rejected the wretched Papadimoulis amendment, which called for the defence of the external borders to be - look out - not financed by Community funds. It should be funded by all of us, all of you Greek taxpayers.
rewrite: Four years back, certain voices claimed "the sea knows no boundaries." Consequently, over a million migrants were tilling the soil. Yet, that terrain of the "open vineyard" is now gone. Unauthorized movements are being halted, and despite those opinions—I reiterate from across Greece—the barrier at Evros is growing. Moreover, under Europe's endorsement, which dismissed the misguided Papadimoulis amendment that sought to exclude Community funding for border protection—note well—it must be supported by all of us, every Greek taxpayer.

text: And a little further away, the regeneration of our shipyards, in neighbouring Elefsina. The workers have returned to work. And notice, they're back on what wages? From 1,500 to 3,000 euros. With investments of more than 100 million. We'll have a total of 2,000 workers, most of them working here, in West Athens.
rewrite: "And a bit farther off, our shipyards in nearby Elefsina are being revived. The workforce has resumed their duties. And take note, at what pay scale have they returned? From 1,500 to 3,000 euros. With investments exceeding 100 million. We'll employ a total of 2,000 workers, the majority based right here, in West Athens."

text: Friends and friends, the cause that led to the Tempi is what the people see before them every day. Thousands of students crammed into unsuitable buildings in the municipality of Larissa are finding it. In total, in the municipality of Larissa, 57 schools are housed in buildings that are characterised as ageing, having been built with little or no seismic specifications.Similarly, in the city of Larissa, the uneven crossings have turned into carmanioles, claiming the lives of many people, such as the crossing in Karla Street next to the 4th EPAL, the crossing at the ATA, the depot of the OSE in Mezourlo, where a few years ago a 15-year-old student was struck by lightning, in the "damaria" of N. Smyrna, where in 2017 a 10-year-old child was swept away and lost his life. The cause is found by hundreds of earthquake victims living in containers, two years after the earthquake of March 3, 2021. Thousands of people who are shaking their foliage in case they get sick find it, as public hospitals are straining with staff and infrastructure shortages. Hundreds of workers who lack essential health and safety conditions in their workplaces.
rewrite: Friends and comrades, the root of the Tempi tragedy is visible to all in daily life. In the municipality of Larissa, thousands of students are packed into inadequate school buildings. Overall, 57 schools in the area are located in aging structures, originally built with minimal or no seismic provisions. Likewise, in Larissa city, hazardous pedestrian crossings have become death traps, claiming numerous lives—such as those on Karla Street near the 4th EPAL, at the ATA, and at the OSE depot in Mezourlo, where a 15-year-old student was tragically struck by lightning years ago, or at the "damaria" in N. Smyrna, where a 10-year-old child was swept away and died in 2017. The cause is also evident for hundreds of earthquake survivors still living in containers two years after the March 3, 2021 quake. Thousands more, fearful of falling ill, find it as public hospitals buckle under staff and infrastructure shortages. Hundreds of workers, too, discover it through the absence of basic health and safety measures in their workplaces.

text: Well, I wouldn't change a word of those words. On the contrary, I am here to assure you that our motto is now a tangible reality: we said it and we did it.
rewrite: "Well, I wouldn't alter a single word of that statement. In fact, I'm here to confirm that our motto has become a concrete truth: we declared it, and we delivered."

text: Friends, compañeras and compañeros. We want from here, from Larissa, which became the epicentre of the unspeakable tragedy with the hundred of young victims in Tempi, from the city whose people and youth honoured the victims in the most shocking way, by flooding streets and squares for two weeks, to send again the message that this people, this youth, does not forget the crime in Tempi. After the slogan, 'SYRIZA, PASOK, ND, this crime has a history', shouted by thousands of workers and young people, today there are more and more people who realise that the policy responsible for this tragedy is the policy that treats critical sectors for people's lives, such as transport and public transport, as a field of profitability for big capital and business groups. Every time, but every time, it turns out that profit and social needs are not compatible. Either the former will be served or the latter.But are these not the obsessions of the KKE, which will say the same thing no matter what happens, as some parrots have written and are writing?But none of them can hide: The special report of the European Court of Auditors on the railways revealed by "Rizospastis" spoke of a delay in the introduction of modern electronic systems in all EU countries! It even said that this delay can be attributed mainly to the reluctance of railway companies to invest in equipment because of the costs involved.
rewrite: Comrades, friends, and allies. From Larissa—the epicenter of the unspeakable Tempi tragedy that claimed hundreds of young lives, a city whose people and youth honored the victims in a profoundly moving way, filling streets and squares for two weeks—we reiterate: this society, this youth, does not forget the crime at Tempi. Following the chant, “SYRIZA, PASOK, ND, this crime has a history,” echoed by thousands of workers and young people, a growing number now recognize that the policy behind this disaster is one that treats vital sectors like transport and public transit as mere profit fields for big capital and corporate interests. Time and again, it is proven that profit and social needs cannot coexist. One must be chosen over the other. Yet, are these not the persistent critiques of the KKE, accused by some of repeating the same message regardless of events, as certain commentators claim? But nothing can conceal the truth: The special report from the European Court of Auditors on railways, disclosed by “Rizospastis,” highlighted delays in deploying modern electronic systems across all EU nations! It even noted that this delay stems largely from railway companies’ reluctance to invest in necessary equipment due to the associated costs.

text: But it would be good for Mera25, when it says the word "rupture", to open a dictionary to see what it means, because rupture and oaths of loyalty to the Commission, to the EU, do not go together. Because a break with the system cannot, will not and will never be made by someone who refuses to call this system by its name and even runs to protect it now that many people, especially young people, seem to be starting to question it, with Mr Varoufakis telling them that in Greece we do not exactly have capitalism, but something else, which only he knows! Beware of the election mischief-makers, then! Because they, too, are on the same track as the others. So let's leave them alone to do their own thing. We're all against them, with a strong JCD. Alone, they all have only one concern, to fill the coffers of the monopolies and business groups with profits.
rewrite: However, it would benefit Mera25 to consult a dictionary regarding the term "rupture," as rupture and pledges of allegiance to the Commission and the EU are incompatible. A break with the system cannot, will not, and shall never be achieved by those who avoid naming this system and even rush to defend it just as many, particularly the youth, begin to question it—with Mr. Varoufakis claiming that Greece does not strictly have capitalism, but something only he understands! So, be wary of the electoral tricksters! They, too, follow the same path as the rest. Therefore, let them pursue their own agenda undisturbed. We stand united against them, with a robust JCD. On their own, their sole aim is to enrich the monopolies and corporate interests with profits.

text: In health you know very well here in Komotini, especially in Komotini, because of the situation in the hospital. Health. It is for the Greeks the third largest expenditure in the European Union. We are surpassed only by the Lithuanians and the Bulgarians. Why? Because quite simply. The great child of George Gennimata and Paraskevas Avgerinos is the National Health System. Some have left it to its mercy. And if there hadn't been a pandemic, I'd say they didn't know. But after the pandemic. The problem is tragically, it showed the lack of primary care. So we are committed to the regeneration of the NHS. We did it ourselves, we have a duty to regenerate it, First. Strong pay incentives for our health workers when thousands of health doctors are going abroad and their salaries are below the European average. Second. Permanent staff. Permanent staff to staff all hospitals and even incentives for specific specialties whose shortage leads to transfers of hundreds of surgeries across Greece. A new national health system means respect for the worker. That is why I pledge today that, just as we tabled an amendment a few months ago, which the new democracy did not vote for, to include health workers in the heavy and unhealthy category, we will also table an amendment as the next government to stop the mockery of our health workers and finally include them in the heavy and unhealthy category. And this is a clear commitment here in Komotini as well. Friends and friends. Strong primary care means going home. It means that the retired elderly person can have services, as in other European countries. You will tell me. But is there any money for all these things you are talking about? If there was no Recovery Fund, I would have to come up with a fiscal plan. But when the Portuguese, the Italians are using 8 to 10% of the Recovery Fund for their own public health systems, because in Greece we give 4, 2 of which actually go to services, the other 2% for the energy upgrade of buildings, which is essentially for the green transition, so Mitsotakis 2 %.
rewrite: Here in Komotini, you are acutely aware of the health situation, particularly due to the state of the hospital. Healthcare represents the third largest expense for Greeks within the European Union, trailing only Lithuania and Bulgaria. The reason is straightforward. The National Health System is the significant legacy of George Gennimata and Paraskevas Avgerinos. Some have abandoned it to fate. Had there not been a pandemic, one might think they were unaware. But after the pandemic, the tragic flaw revealed was the absence of robust primary care. Therefore, we are dedicated to revitalizing the NHS. We created it; we have the obligation to renew it. First, through substantial pay incentives for our healthcare workers, as thousands of doctors leave for abroad, their salaries falling below the European average. Second, through permanent staffing—filling all hospitals with permanent staff and offering incentives for critical specialties, shortages of which cause hundreds of surgeries to be transferred across Greece. A renewed national health system signifies respect for its workers. That is why I pledge today that, just as we proposed an amendment months ago—which New Democracy did not support—to classify health workers under heavy and unhealthy duties, we will propose it again as the next government to end the disregard for our health workers and finally grant them that classification. This is a firm commitment, right here in Komotini. Friends, robust primary care means care at home. It means elderly retirees can access services, as in other European nations. You might ask: is there funding for all these proposals? Without the Recovery Fund, a fiscal strategy would be necessary. But while Portugal and Italy allocate 8 to 10% of their Recovery Funds to their public health systems, in Greece we assign only 4%, with just 2% actually directed to services—the other 2% for building energy upgrades, which primarily supports the green transition. That’s Mitsotakis’s 2%.

text: Friends, compañeras and compañeros. And from here, from Egaleo, from the western districts of Athens, where the lives of tens of thousands of working-class families are squeezed, here where the hope for a better tomorrow passes every day through individual and collective toil and struggle, we want to address our hopeful call: Now is the time for decisive support and strengthening of the KKE! In the elections of May 21, we can terrorize those who terrorize us. We can neutralize their dilemmas and blackmail. To think and choose this time on the basis of our own interests, our own anxieties and our own needs.The thousands of workers, the unemployed who live in these neighbourhoods, the high school students who will be voting for the first time, the young people studying at the University of West Attica, the women who carry double and triple burdens at work and in the family, all of them know in their hearts that they have nothing substantial to expect from any government that is formed, among the parties that have ruled so far, ND, SYRIZA and PASOK and their various willing partners. They are not touched by the cockfights that take place for show, between those who have implemented and are alternately implementing the same and unchanging policy on the basic issues, for the benefit of the few.
rewrite: Comrades, friends and allies. Here in Egaleo, within Athens' western neighborhoods, where countless working-class households face daily pressures, where the dream of a brighter future is forged through personal and shared effort and resistance, we issue our urgent appeal: This is the moment to firmly back and reinforce the KKE! On May 21, through our votes, we can intimidate those who intimidate us. We can reject their false choices and coercion. To reflect and decide now according to our own concerns, our own worries, and our own demands. The many laborers, the jobless residents of these areas, the first-time voting high schoolers, the youth at the University of West Attica, the women bearing multiple burdens at work and at home—all sense deeply that they can expect little of real value from any administration formed by the parties that have governed until now, ND, SYRIZA, and PASOK, along with their ready collaborators. They remain unmoved by the staged clashes, the theatrical disputes among those who have enacted and continue to rotate the same unchanging core policies, serving the interests of the few.

text:
SYRIZA criticized at the time the basic provision of the Katseli law, that in order to support the first home, the borrower had to have and sell the rest of his assets. That is why SYRIZA stressed that of the 430,000 "red" loans, only 170,000 of the 430,000 "red" loans used the provisions of the law through appeals. Then, all parties of the system, SYRIZA, ND and PASOK, voted for the sale of "red" loans to funds, in order to ensure the competitiveness and profits of the banks and conglomerates and the interests of the lenders.
In the two years 2015 - 2017, the SYRIZA - ANEL government voted successively for the sale of "red" loans to funds, the implementation of electronic auctions and the "peculiar" for those who resist the auctions. The 'red' loans that have passed into the ownership of the funds amount to more than €85 billion. While 600,000 properties have been given as collateral as security for these loans. Of these, around 50% are mortgaged houses. On the online platform, since 2019, auctions have been posted on the online platform, averaging more than 25,000 per year. In fact, they soared to over 52,000 in 2022. Of course, not all auctions are completed immediately, the homes transferred are fewer. But the auction tsunami did not start now.
rewrite:
SYRIZA initially opposed the core clause of the Katseli law, which required borrowers to possess and liquidate other assets to protect their primary residence. Consequently, SYRIZA highlighted that out of 430,000 "red" loans, merely 170,000 utilized the law's provisions via appeals. Subsequently, all establishment parties—SYRIZA, ND, and PASOK—endorsed the sale of "red" loans to funds, aiming to safeguard bank and conglomerate competitiveness, profits, and lender interests.

During 2015–2017, the SYRIZA-ANEL administration successively approved transferring "red" loans to funds, enacting electronic auctions and "special measures" against auction resisters. Over €85 billion in "red" loans have shifted to fund ownership, with 600,000 properties pledged as collateral—approximately half being mortgaged homes. Since 2019, the online platform has listed an average exceeding 25,000 auctions annually, peaking at over 52,000 in 2022. While not all auctions conclude promptly, resulting in fewer home transfers, this auction surge did not originate recently.

text: Friends, we have a duty to talk about the cost of living, which also concerns education. The base 10, the university police, they were asking us on the channels saying, are you for or against the university police? But there is no university police. Mr Tsipras took your taxes. He made a body which does not exist today. Another buffoon. Why didn't we do what all European countries do? Private security companies, protection, cameras in the laboratories where there are expensive machines paid for by the Greek people. Is there a criminal act? The regular police go in and deal with crime, just like in every other place in our country. Why did we have to do something special that ultimately doesn't work? So let's get to the heart of the problem. What do we say? Strong higher education with extroversion and research to become the engine of agri-food development in Greece with serious research in universities. To give strength to our exports. There is no other way, we have to go to the average of research which is the European Union. We cannot have block researchers in universities with very little money. This does not honour the researcher, no one will come back. Primary, secondary what are we saying? The school is a parerguard nowadays. Children have given main burden and their families to tutorials. Our school, the public school, is not working. What should we do? National Baccalaureate. Only with a national baccalaureate will tutorials be a second priority and public school, public high school and public high school and of course exams will be a first priority. But what exams? Not in a minute, sorry, in a process of judging your dream, your future. But exams in the last 2 and 3 years, as it is in France and Germany. And of course, remedial teaching for all Greek children. To reduce the cost of tuition, to reduce inequalities among our people. And above all, the vision of real special education structures. We are a socialist party that is people-centred. I can't imagine in 2023 meeting 40 and 45 year old parents across Greece whose children are on the autism spectrum and having these young people say to me, I'm afraid of what my child will do when I'm gone from this life. This is not a normal European state and we have a duty to build serious special education structures for the school of inclusion, so that every citizen feels that the state is there for them and supports them.
rewrite: Friends, we must address the cost of living, which includes education. The so-called university police—some were asking on channels whether we support it or not. But there is no university police. Mr. Tsipras used your taxes to create a body that no longer exists. Another absurdity. Why didn't we follow what other European countries do? Hire private security, install cameras in labs with expensive equipment funded by the Greek people. If a crime occurs, the regular police handle it, as everywhere else in our country. Why create a special system that ultimately fails? Let's focus on the real issue. What is our stance? We need strong higher education, open to the world and research, to drive Greece's agri-food sector through serious university-led studies. This will boost our exports. There's no alternative; we must align with the EU's average research investment. We cannot trap researchers in universities with insufficient funding. That dishonors them, and no one will return. What about primary and secondary education? Today, schools are sidelined. Children and their families rely heavily on private tutoring. Our public schools are not functioning. What should we do? Implement a National Baccalaureate. Only then will tutoring become secondary, and public schools—along with exams—take priority. But what exams? Not hastily, but through a process that evaluates your aspirations and future. Exams in the final two to three years, as in France and Germany. And certainly, provide remedial teaching for all Greek children to lower tuition costs and reduce inequalities. Most importantly, we need a vision for genuine special education frameworks. As a socialist party focused on people, it's unacceptable in 2023 to meet parents aged 40 to 45 across Greece with children on the autism spectrum, hearing them say, "I fear for my child's future when I'm gone." This isn't typical for a European state. We have an obligation to establish robust special education structures for inclusive schooling, ensuring every citizen feels supported by the state.

text: But at the same time, along with the economic recovery, we have also strengthened our defence. To those who did not see borders at sea and wanted them open on land, we gave a double answer. We zeroed out refugee flows. We relieved our islands, we built modern structures instead of the shameful structures of Moria. We saved lives in the Aegean. And, yes, we extended the fence on Evros. The fence is being extended, let those who fought it and are still fighting it hear it well.
rewrite: Yet alongside economic recovery, we have also fortified our defenses. To those who disregarded maritime borders and demanded open land frontiers, we delivered a twofold response. We halted refugee arrivals. We freed our islands, replacing the disgrace of Moria with modern facilities. We preserved lives in the Aegean. And indeed, we expanded the barrier at Evros. The fence is being extended—let this be clearly heard by those who opposed it and continue to do so.

rewrite: "And the same occurred in education. I am certain that among us are some of the 25,000 newly appointed teachers in our educational system. The first such appointments in 12 years. 2,500 in Crete alone. From 62 Standard and Experimental Schools, we have expanded to 138. Our young children now learn a foreign language in kindergarten, and soon every Greek classroom, starting from the 5th grade, will be equipped with interactive whiteboards. 36,000 new interactive whiteboards for all our schools. text: But what does trust mean for PASOK? Trust means that every Greek citizen feels secure with his family, with his efforts, with his children. In Tempe, everyone said that this is what it was like to be so far, and they were right. 57 people lost their lives unjustly. At the same time, Mr Voridis and Mr Georgiades were saying that the transfer of the stationmaster in question was not illegal. The three-member committee appointed by Mitsotakis itself ruled that the transfer of the stationmaster was illegal. Did you see anyone apologize? Did you see anyone take political responsibility? And tell us whose New Democracy MP's party buffoonery was this illegal transfer? Or did SYRIZA and New Democracy apologize together, for signing in 2014 the contract to have telecoms €55 million, not even €1 from your taxes, all European funds, and after 9 years we had no telecoms? What happened because Mr Tsipras stopped talking about it? Because when we asked the Minister responsible, Mr Karamanlis, in Parliament. One simple thing. October 21, the independent transparency authority gave him a dossier that said exactly who was responsible for not implementing the telecommunications to avoid tragedy. And we asked him what did you do with that dossier? Did you take it to justice? The answer of Karamanlis, who today also adorns the ballot papers of New Democracy in Serres, despising the families, the pain, the tragedy that is collectively engraved in the memory of the Greek people was I did not know, he said, the existence of this report, that is what we deserve, not what we deserve a normal state that ensures security. Justice for all and not justice for all of us, but not for the cronies of Tsipras and Mitsotakis. We need another state and not the state that is a tool of bribery used by power systems to reproduce their power. We want to build this trust in the trust of the pure word of the concrete of the great reforms that finally make Greece a normal European state that respects every citizen, that honours the weak and supports the middle class.
rewrite: But what does trust signify for PASOK? Trust means each Greek citizen feels secure in their family, their endeavors, and their children's future. In Tempe, everyone acknowledged this was the situation until now, and they were correct. Fifty-seven individuals lost their lives unjustly. Meanwhile, Mr. Voridis and Mr. Georgiades claimed the transfer of the stationmaster was not unlawful. The three-member committee appointed by Mitsotakis itself determined that transfer was illegal. Did anyone offer an apology? Did anyone assume political accountability? And reveal which New Democracy MP's party folly authorized this illegal transfer? Or did SYRIZA and New Democracy jointly apologize for signing the 2014 contract for telecommunications worth €55 million—funded entirely by European money, not a single euro from taxpayers—yet after nine years, we still lack telecommunications? What occurred because Mr. Tsipras ceased discussing it? When we questioned the responsible Minister, Mr. Karamanlis, in Parliament about one simple matter: on October 21, the independent transparency authority provided him a dossier specifying who was accountable for failing to implement telecommunications to prevent tragedy. We asked what he did with that dossier. Did he refer it to justice? Karamanlis’s response—who now also appears on New Democracy's ballots in Serres, disregarding the families, the grief, the tragedy etched in the collective memory of the Greek people—was that he was unaware of the report's existence. This is what we receive, not what we merit: a normal state that guarantees security. Justice for everyone, not justice for all except the associates of Tsipras and Mitsotakis. We require a different state, not one that serves as a tool of corruption used by power structures to perpetuate their control. We aim to establish this trust through the integrity of our word, the substance of major reforms that will ultimately transform Greece into a normal European nation—one that respects every citizen, honors the vulnerable, and bolsters the middle class.

text: Let the people be strong, say the messages of optimism coming from workplaces, neighbourhoods, schools and colleges. Because more and more people now know that a new anti-people's government is about to be formed. They may delay it a little, but it will be built by parties that share the goals of capital that is why they have a common government program. This is now a done deal. They will form a government as they did in the past, when PASOK went with ND and all together first with LAOS and then with DIMAR, when SYRIZA went with the far-right ANEL and together with ND and PASOK they loaded us with a third barbaric memorandum. They will do their job, they will form a government. And we will do ours! We will strengthen the stable, confident, militant opposition, the KKE!
rewrite: "Let the people be strong," declare the hopeful voices from workplaces, neighborhoods, schools, and colleges. This is because many now realize that a new government opposed to the people is on the verge of taking shape. They might postpone it briefly, but it will be established by parties aligned with capital's interests, which explains their shared government agenda. This outcome is now certain. They will create a government as before—when PASOK joined ND, and all united first with LAOS and later with DIMAR, or when SYRIZA allied with the far-right ANEL and, alongside ND and PASOK, burdened us with a third brutal memorandum. They will carry out their role, they will form a government. And we will fulfill ours! We will fortify the steadfast, resolute, combative opposition, the KKE!

text: See what happened to the National Health System. Yes, it held up during the pandemic. Yes, it has more than double the number of ICUs, it has more than 15,000 health workers, more than 1,000 of them in total in Crete. It has salaries increased by 10%. But our health remains the big patient. That is why we will allocate 150 million euros just for the modernisation of health structures on our island.
rewrite: Look at the state of the National Health System. True, it endured the pandemic. True, it now has over twice the ICU capacity, employs more than 15,000 healthcare staff, with over 1,000 of them stationed in Crete. Salaries have risen by 10%. Yet, our health is still the primary concern. This is precisely why we are dedicating 150 million euros solely to upgrading the medical infrastructure on our island.

text: I ask you, does Greece in 2023 resemble Greece in 2019? The answer is: no, not at all. We have a fiscal surplus in 2022. This prudent management has succeeded in increasing our GDP by 26 billion; our debt, that very important indicator of our credibility, has been reduced by 40 full points, the largest reduction in public debt in the whole of Europe.
rewrite: "Let me ask you: does Greece in 2023 look anything like Greece in 2019? The answer is no, not in the slightest. In 2022, we achieved a fiscal surplus. This careful stewardship has boosted our GDP by 26 billion; our debt, that crucial measure of our trustworthiness, has dropped by a full 40 points—the most significant public debt reduction across all of Europe."

rewrite: "And let certain Mera25 MPs in parliament claim socialism was 'somewhat fascist,' as if that justifies capitalism being the ultimate system ever tested!!!! Leftists, progressives, and all democrats in this nation understand clearly that anti-Soviet and anti-communist sentiments have no link to progress, just as Mr. Tsipras’s recent remarks in Menidi regarding Pontians in the Soviet Union stray far from reality. text: But as simple as the above dilemmas are, the need for stability is equally obvious, friends, as well. The difficulties that lie ahead of us will not disappear. And in an uncertain global environment that will become increasingly complex, Greece needs a clear horizon on its path and a clear solution at the top. All the more so when our opponents are unprincipled.
rewrite: Yet, while these dilemmas appear straightforward, the necessity for stability is just as evident, my friends. The challenges awaiting us will not simply vanish. In a world growing ever more intricate and unpredictable, Greece requires a clear direction forward and decisive leadership. This is especially true when those opposing us lack any guiding principles.

text: Friends, compañeras and comrades, we believe that behind the pre-election cockfights of the parties that claim the first or even the second role in tomorrow's anti-people's government, what the KKE says has emerged more clearly in recent weeks is that the other parties share a common programme on the basic, major issues that will determine our lives after May 21 and for the years to come. This is increasingly being admitted by their own cadres who say that their differences are not as great as they are presented. We have now lost count of the relevant statements that leave open even the possibility of a New Democracy SYRIZA coalition government if that is required, have no doubt that these statements are not made in the absence of their leaders. Political massage and preparing the ground is called this for later and if these are said during the election, imagine what has to be done post-election. The foreign embassies, the various investment houses, the governor of the Bank of Greece himself admit it, all of them with one voice say that they are not worried about exactly what the composition of the next government will be, since whoever they say will do the job.
rewrite: Comrades, friends, and compañeras, it has become increasingly evident in recent weeks, amid the pre-election clashes of parties vying for a leading role in tomorrow's anti-popular government, that what the KKE asserts is true: these parties fundamentally agree on the major issues that will shape our lives after May 21 and in the coming years. Their own members increasingly acknowledge this, admitting their differences are not as significant as portrayed. We have lost count of statements even hinting at a potential New Democracy-SYRIZA coalition if needed; rest assured, such remarks are not made without their leaders' knowledge. This is political groundwork being laid for later, and if such things are said during the campaign, consider what will follow the election. Foreign embassies, various investment firms, and even the Bank of Greece governor concede this—all uniformly state they are unconcerned about the next government's exact makeup, as whoever assumes power will fulfill the task.

text:
Friends, compañeras and compañeros. Mr. Tsipras and the SYRIZA cadres constantly refer to the KKE and - with great self-confidence - declare that it is one thing what the parties say during the pre-election and another thing what they will do after the election. As far as this is concerned, they know something, we don't doubt it... So they say that after the elections "the KKE will have to take responsibility" for whether we prefer a Syriza government with PASOK, or whether we will open the way for Mitsotakis.You will have heard us say many times that we are not in 2012 or 2015. Let's think a little more carefully about what that means, what has changed since then... You know, today is the 11th anniversary of the elections of May 2012, which, in the midst of a deep capitalist crisis, brought about major rearrangements in the bourgeois political system, in the correlation between the bourgeois parties.The two parties - ND and PASOK - that had been in power since the post-war period were crushed, especially PASOK, which traditionally enclosed a large part of the working and popular classes, but also ND.

text: Ladies and friends, I cannot not speak here from the plain of Thessaly about agricultural issues, production, extroversion, the dignity of the farmer, because our goal is not only for you but also for your children and grandchildren to stay in the plain of Thessaly, to cultivate the land, to have exports, to increase our population when demography is one of the biggest national problems of the country. So that is why we say, as our founder, Andreas Papandreou, used to say, that the rural world is the backbone of the democratic party. For years now, the rural population has been declining. In the last decade, our farmers have decreased by some 260 000 and the area under cultivation by 6.5 million hectares. 1.3 billion in agricultural income has been lost. 70% of our farmers are in debt to public funds, the National Social Security Fund and banks. Tens of thousands of farmers and 727 cooperatives are carrying red loans from the time of the Agricultural Bank and many today are being extorted by the funds. The threat of foreclosures is stronger than ever, with the national risk of national danger of the deflation of the Greek economy. The cost of production has risen by 22.4% in this year and a half alone, with increases in electricity, oil, animal feed and fertilisers. What has the New Democracy government done to counter the undermining of the competitiveness of our productive base? Only ephemeral allowances. At the same time, the implementation of the new CAP and its programmes has been significantly delayed, with the result that thousands of farmers do not know what will happen with their applications, when their investments will be subsidised. Because of the delays, our farmers and livestock farmers risk losing 50% of their basic support and the country will be forced to pay new fines to the European Union. Finally, let the gentlemen of the New Democracy make up their minds and stop the mockery. Are the delays due to incompetence or is it an attempt to conceal the real reduction in subsidies for the Greek farmer? And of course, the other big issue is the land workers. text: Friends, compañeras and compañeros, Since we are here tonight in Larissa, in the Thessalian plain, we want to address the farmer and livestock farmer who is fighting for survival every day. We invite him to think that the policy implemented successively by all the last governments in our country is responsible for the continuous reduction of his income. Governments that had and still have as their common program the guidelines of the CAP, the interests of business groups.He should think that the New Democracy - Syriza - PASOK together support the one-sided orientation to the export of agricultural products, which benefits the commercial industrialists, while the massive imports add new difficulties to the life of farmers, degrading the quality of basic foodstuffs of the people. Together they voted for the 3rd memorandum, which cut the reimbursement of the special excise duty on agricultural diesel. It is no coincidence that all of them, in the face of the demand for guaranteed prices for products, are advocating the one-way CAP, which is going from bad to worse for the interests of the majority of farmers and, with its current revision (2023-2027), puts new obstacles to your survival. New Democracy - SYRIZA - PASOK together have formed an ELGA that wastes and hardly compensates. Together they have signed up to sanctions on Russia that are ultimately paid for by the farmers and all the people.
rewrite:
Friends, compañeras and compañeros,  
Tonight, here in Larissa on the Thessalian plain, we speak directly to the farmers and livestock breeders fighting daily for survival. We urge them to consider that the policies carried out by successive governments in our country are to blame for the steady decline in their income. These governments have shared a common agenda: following CAP directives and serving the interests of big business.  
They should realize that New Democracy, Syriza, and PASOK jointly promote an export‑focused model for agricultural products, which enriches agro‑industrial traders, while massive imports create further hardships for farmers and lower the quality of the people’s basic food. Together, they voted for the third memorandum, which slashed the refund on the special tax on agricultural diesel.  
It is no accident that all of them, when faced with demands for guaranteed prices, defend the one‑sided CAP—a policy that grows worse for most farmers and, with its current revision (2023‑2027), places new barriers to your survival. New Democracy, SYRIZA, and PASOK have jointly shaped an ELGA that squanders resources and offers inadequate compensation. Together, they have backed sanctions against Russia, the cost of which ultimately falls on farmers and all the people.

text: In 2020, the government of the New Democracy, with the new Bankruptcy Code, untied the hands of the creditors to seize and sell off a large part of the property of those who cannot afford to service their loans. In February 2023, a decision of the Supreme Court allowed the Management Companies, the servicers, who have taken over the affairs of the funds, to take legal actions themselves involving auctions. A decision that proved, among other things, what the representatives of the capital mean when they call for the judiciary to become a "source of confidence" for investments. The new programme of the Southwest for 'housing for the young' also has the same character: The support of banks and construction capital. What does the programme provide for? State-subsidized loans, which banks will give to young workers to buy property, much of which is owned by banks and construction capital. The new workers will turn into the new borrowers - with state-guaranteed loans - this time, and will wait for the next crisis and the collapse of their wages, only to then turn into the next period's over-indebted too. And yet, the limits and conditions imposed end up excluding the most vulnerable, while pushing young people into areas far from where they wish to live. The real beneficiary of the scheme is again the banks... The banks, who will make thousands of new and multi-secured loans from a thousand sides, while getting rid of properties that currently remain unsold.
rewrite: In 2020, the New Democracy government, through the new Bankruptcy Code, enabled creditors to seize and sell a significant portion of assets from those unable to repay their loans. By February 2023, a Supreme Court ruling permitted Management Companies—servicers handling fund operations—to independently initiate legal actions, including auctions. This decision highlighted what capital representatives imply when advocating for the judiciary to serve as a "source of confidence" for investments. Similarly, the Southwest's new 'housing for the young' program aligns with this pattern: it bolsters banks and construction capital. What does the program offer? State-subsidized loans from banks to young workers for purchasing properties, many of which are owned by these same financial and construction interests. These young workers will become new borrowers—with state-backed loans—awaiting the next crisis and wage declines, only to join the ranks of the over-indebted later. Moreover, the program's restrictions and criteria often exclude the most vulnerable, forcing youth into distant, undesirable areas. The true beneficiaries remain the banks, which will issue thousands of new, well-secured loans from various angles while offloading currently unsold properties.

rewrite: Today we mark this anniversary here, in Kallithea of the Resistance, in Kallithea of EAM and ELAS, of the EPON members and the “Eagle Boys,” who offered their finest youth to the struggle. rewrite: These and numerous other objectives form the core of the KKE's struggle. They constitute its political platform, its program for the people's own power. text: The well-known and unexceptional Varoufakis, who informed us that "anyone who feels rage and has no other way to express it is a fascist!" rewrite: The notorious and unremarkable Varoufakis declared that "anyone who feels rage and lacks alternative means to express it is a fascist!" Such statements are intolerable and perilous, deserving universal denunciation from all who uphold democracy. text: We have made it clear from the beginning that the dilemma of stability, of so-called ungovernability, which the government of the Southwest and - with variations - the other forces are putting to the people, is blackmail and false. rewrite: Friends. It is a great honor to be here today—both those present in person and those joining online. Some of you we have known for years; most we do not. That is the truth. I say this because I believe every person, particularly the young, deserves both prosperity and happiness. A socialist party, a social democratic party, must do all it can to ensure the possibilities of the welfare state and sustainable development, securing this right to happiness and prosperity.

text:
Revenues in the Greek market reached 2.2 billion euros this year, up from 1.4 billion euros in 2019. The abolition after 2012 of the OEK exacerbates the problem even more. More generally, the onslaught of tourism in city centres, not only in the form of airbnb, is also drastically changing land prices. Entire areas are being transformed into hotbeds of tourist interest. Tourist-oriented hotels and entertainment centres are springing up like mushrooms, driving up land prices. The redevelopment of city centres, the 'grand promenade', has precisely this aim. To turn cities into areas of tourist interest.Similarly, the changes in holiday construction are made to concentrate land in the hands of the tourism groups. Last November, tens of thousands of small landowners suddenly saw the abolition of building by derogation make them the pawns of big investors. Now, the way is opening up (with the de facto abolition of the 4-acre requirement for a large piece of land) for the massive concentration of land in large conglomerates.
We recall, that under the state policy promoted by ND and SYRIZA, large conglomerates are exempted from any zoning restrictions. They build hotels wherever they want with preferential conditions. In other words, the housing crisis in Greece is not only about the nightmare of foreclosures.
rewrite: Revenues in the Greek market climbed to 2.2 billion euros this year, rising from 1.4 billion euros in 2019. The post-2012 abolition of the OEK has further intensified the issue. More broadly, the surge of tourism in urban centers, extending beyond platforms like Airbnb, is radically altering property values. Whole neighborhoods are becoming focal points for tourist activity. Hotels and entertainment venues catering to tourists are proliferating rapidly, pushing land prices higher. The renovation of city centers, including projects like the 'grand promenade', is explicitly designed to transform cities into tourist destinations. Likewise, modifications to vacation construction regulations aim to consolidate land ownership within major tourism corporations. Last November, the elimination of building by derogation abruptly placed tens of thousands of small landowners at the mercy of large investors. Currently, the path is being cleared (through the effective removal of the 4-acre rule for sizable plots) for the extensive aggregation of land into large conglomerates. It should be noted that, under policies advanced by ND and SYRIZA, these major conglomerates face no zoning limitations. They can construct hotels in any location under favorable terms. Thus, the housing crisis in Greece encompasses more than just the distress of foreclosures.

text: On the issue of Golden Dawn. I cannot imagine that there are young people in our country who would consider voting for Mr Kasidiaris' party. The party that praises Hitler, the man who bloodied Greece, the party that painted its hands with the blood of Pavlos Fyssa and the immigrants. Their place is and will be in darkness and in prison. But here are some questions that all democrats must ask the Greek people every day until the next elections. Why did Mr Mitsotakis allow the murderers, the neo-Nazis, to campaign for three years from within the prisons? In what other European state would a gang - apart from ideology - campaign from inside the prison? In what other country would they wait 2 months before an election to legislate? We said from the beginning, and with the late Fofi Gennimata, that there had to be a law to prevent murderers from participating in our democracy. But Mr Mitsotakis had second thoughts; what are those second thoughts? As long as he was seeing Golden Dawn below 3%, he tells you a big remainder, low bar for self-reliance. As soon as he saw Golden Dawn going above 3%, I say to you, whoa, they're getting into parliament. Small remainder, self-reliance bar goes up. This is Mr Mitsotakis' code of opportunism even on these huge issues of democracy in our country. And of course Mr. Tsipras, who has the audacity to want to fish for votes in murky waters. And he doesn't vote, he didn't vote for the law that would have prevented the murderous neo-Nazis from participating in the political system. Mr Varoufakis, who had even more nerve. And I ask you, in which European country do parties of murderers, apart from ideologies, participate? So that's the left, that's the right. That is why we have a one-way street: the rebirth of PASOK and the democratic party with the principles and values of 3 September, the principles that made the Greek people live through the years of post-independence, the years of democracy, the rule of law and the separation of powers.
rewrite: Regarding the matter of Golden Dawn, it is inconceivable to me that any young person in our nation would contemplate supporting Mr. Kasidiaris' party. text: But how can you be in touch with the problems of the people when such a distance separates you from all this, no matter how much nonsense they say, it cannot be hidden that everywhere our people are constantly confronted with the same contradiction, that there are millions of workers who, with their work, their knowledge, with their knowledge, their skills, they produce all the wealth of this country, there are workers capable of producing, of creating with high qualification and ability, but not exploited in their industry, a new generation that comes with momentum and struggles for its education, with an appetite to create and grow, to exploit the new technologies and what humanity has produced, and on the other side there are a handful of people and their governments, who are trying to limit all this power, to put the brakes on it, to subjugate it within the framework of their own profit, who see the workers only as some necessary parts and tools to achieve their coveted capitalist profits, who see the rights of our people as an obstacle to their profits. rewrite: We universally shield farmland from seizure threats. Not one acre of Greek soil will be left to the vultures of the funds. text: In these election days, the other parties, the New Democracy, SYRIZA, PASOK/KINAL, remember the freelancers. The most dynamic businesses are the ones to which the programmes to support small and medium-sized enterprises announced by the EU and all governments are directed, and not, of course, every professional who relies on his own work, a few family members or at most 1-2 employees. text: Another point of our programme, of our priorities, is the major objective of tackling the national demographic issue. For us, demography is a huge issue. It is this issue that undermines society, the economy, the welfare state, every aspect of our country's life. So we have to put the younger generation at the forefront, without the younger generation at the centre of our policies, we cannot address the demographic. That's why we have announced, we were the first to put it in the public debate, the creation of a pool of 150,000 social housing units that will be either built from resources - new resources from the Recovery Fund, something that other countries have tried to do. Or by providing incentives, tax incentives or incentives, to reconstruct old houses to owners, so that they can put them into the social pool those houses are not given for purchase with low-interest loans, as Mr Mitsotakis is doing. We are not building a citizen-customer relationship with new ownership. We are practicing a time-resistant policy. What does that mean? They will be given at a very low rent, with social criteria, so that not only 150,000 families will benefit, but also thousands of families in the wider areas, and through competition we will help to de-escalate the already increased rents in homes that will not have been included in the programme, and this is what examples from other countries show. So with our policy, we will not only support 150,000 families, but also hundreds of thousands of other families. It is a solid policy that 150,000 is a stepping stone. We aspire to start from there to go to the models and levels of countries such as Portugal, Spain, Austria, Germany. And this is particularly important if we take a walk around the region where this event is taking place. Here, rents used to be very, very low. And today, all over the centre of Athens, rents because of short-term rentals, the lack of rules on the part of the state, compared to initiatives taken by other municipalities and other countries in Southern Europe, are prohibitive for a student who wants to study in Athens, for a person who wants to start his life by living in the city centre.
rewrite: A key element of our program and priorities is the major goal of addressing the national demographic challenge. For us, demography is a critical issue. These homes are not sold with low-interest loans, as Mr. Mitsotakis does. We are not fostering a citizen-customer relationship through new ownership. We are implementing a durable, long-term policy. What does this entail? They will be rented at very low rates, based on social criteria, so that not only 150,000 families will gain, but also thousands more in surrounding areas. Through competition, we will help reduce the already high rents in homes not included in the program, as examples from other nations demonstrate. Thus, our policy will support not just 150,000 families, but hundreds of thousands of others. It is a robust policy where 150,000 units are a starting point. We aim to begin there and advance toward the models and standards of countries like Portugal, Spain, Austria, and Germany. Now, throughout central Athens, due to short-term rentals and the state's lack of regulation—unlike measures taken by other municipalities and Southern European countries—rents are prohibitive for a student wishing to study in Athens or someone starting their life in the city center.

text: Friends, Compañeras and Compañeros, In Ioannina everyone can see the results of this common health policy, whether we look at the two public hospitals of the city or the Health Centres of the Epirus region. At the moment, the University General Hospital of Ioannina is receiving a huge number of cases, as a result of the conversion of the health system into a 'one disease' system during the pandemic period. All these cases are being treated with 600 vacant permanent staff positions! 450 employees are contract workers, in permanent hostage or permanent rotation! 150 contract workers in cleaning, catering and security, are under dismissal from December 2021 for a contractor to re-enter and with their struggle alone they have managed to stay on the job until September!  The staff are physically and mentally exhausted. Similarly, at the city's historic hospital, Hadjikosta, understaffing is combined with the highest average age of staff, who are constantly retiring without replacement. Every day, doctors are transferred from these hospitals and the prefectural hospitals to other hospitals in Epirus and Corfu, which are in a state of complete disintegration. On the other hand, private diagnostic centres are springing up every day. Whatever new infrastructure is being built, under the sponsorship of various merciful shipowners, does not mean new staff, but rather fillets to keep the health business going. And they are so unscrupulous that they are doing crazy business in childhood cancer and other areas, but at the same time they cannot secure a few nurses to reopen 6 of the 9 operating rooms at the University of Ioannina, or even build a pediatric ICU bed.
rewrite: Friends, Compañeras and Compañeros, In Ioannina the outcomes of this shared health policy are evident, whether examining the city's two public hospitals or the Health Centres across Epirus.
