And, naturally, through this new approach, to lessen the financial load of school costs on every family. Thus, via the national baccalaureate, we refocus secondary education as the core pathway, enabling youth to access university. Universities should be externally engaged, connected to industry and local growth, with research funding at EU average levels, innovation, and assured meritocracy in academic advancement. We are aware of the enduring issues in Greek universities regarding internal fairness, the need for better support and evaluation of educators at all levels, and recognition of educational contributions.

text: Our main priority, both historically and today, is the regeneration of the national health system. What does this mean? Increasing the funding of the NHS to the European average and strengthening its infrastructure with 8 to 10% of the resources of the Recovery Fund. Today New Democracy is essentially giving 2%. It reaches 4% because the energy upgrade of buildings is added up. You know it is unthinkable, when the Greek people, after many years of the economic adventure of new inequality, impoverishment, are third in private spending in the entire European Union, having also salaries - we are only surpassed by Bulgaria and Lithuania - Europe is making a fund specifically for the pandemic. And this fund is barely used. For this huge issue that concerns every Greek and especially the most vulnerable Greeks. So what are we saying about this? Repeal of Article 10 of the recent law of the New Democracy, which undermines the public character of the NHS, a strong and unified system of primary health care under public supervision with health centres in every municipality and integrated family medicine services everywhere. New modern hospitals which, as I said earlier, will have meritocratic selected administrations, utilisation of digital capabilities for full-day operation, especially in the interventional and surgical sectors. It is not possible in 2023 that we will not have followed these new scientific methods, which are improving health across Europe, and of course, we have a debt for a new health map. But this new health map will not be in political or politicised terms, it will be an objective new health map with hospital care for densely populated areas, the most important and pharaonic example being East Attica. But also in the rest of Greece based on population, based on the need of the summer which is still growing, the population due to tourism and the ageing of the population, we have to create this new objective health map. Create innovative care units outside hospitals for chronic diseases and day care, strengthen public rehabilitation centres and create new ones and fill all the real gaps in the NHS with permanent recruitment and transparent procedures, increase salaries at least at the level of the average of the European Union to attract highly qualified staff, but also to stop young health workers leaving abroad, which every day creates a huge issue for the future of the national system. Our commitment is to include all health workers in the heavy and unhealthy category. This was discussed, we had tabled an amendment in Parliament, but it was not passed by the government, a radical overhaul of the system for obtaining a specialty and an increase in the salaries of specialists. There must also be incentives for specialties that have been eliminated from the NHS, resulting in hundreds of surgeries being constantly postponed, fully staffed hospitals, health centres on our islands. It is a huge problem, as we have seen with a recent example in Serifos. Financial incentives. Covering housing costs, especially in areas with strong tourism, subsidies for attracting scientific potential to the region, support and increase of mental health structures, a huge deficit in our country compared to the European average and their integration into the primary care system, free medicines for vulnerable groups, low pensioners and the unemployed. No one alone, on the margins. This is a clear message from the democratic party. An increase in the social solidarity allowance, universal care services for children, the elderly, the homeless, single-parent families. Disability mainstreaming in all state policies and, of course, disability benefits should follow increases in the minimum wage.
rewrite: "Our foremost commitment, both in the past and now, is revitalizing the national health system. What does this entail? Raising NHS funding to match the European average and reinforcing its infrastructure using 8 to 10% of the Recovery Fund’s resources. Currently, New Democracy allocates merely 2%. It appears as 4% only by including building energy upgrades. Consider this: after years of economic turmoil leading to new inequalities and poverty, Greeks rank third in private health spending across the EU, with salaries among the lowest—only Bulgaria and Lithuania fare worse. Europe has established a pandemic-specific fund, yet it remains vastly underused for this critical issue affecting every Greek, particularly the most vulnerable. Our stance? Repeal Article 10 of New Democracy’s recent law, which erodes the public nature of the NHS. We advocate for a robust, unified primary healthcare system under public oversight, with health centers in every municipality and comprehensive family medicine services nationwide. Establish new modern hospitals with meritocratically chosen administrations, leveraging digital tools for round-the-clock operation, especially in surgical and interventional departments. It is unacceptable that by 2023 we haven’t adopted these advanced scientific methods already enhancing health outcomes Europe-wide. We also owe a new, objective health map—not politically motivated—prioritizing hospital care for populous regions, notably East Attica as a key example. Across Greece, accounting for population needs, seasonal tourism surges, and an ageing society, we must design this objective map. Develop innovative outpatient units for chronic conditions and day care, enhance public rehabilitation centers and establish new ones, and address all NHS shortages through permanent hires and transparent processes. Raise salaries to at least the EU average to retain and attract skilled professionals, halting the exodus of young health workers abroad—a daily threat to our system’s future. Offer financial inducements: housing support in tourist-heavy areas, grants to draw scientific talent locally, and bolstered mental health services, which lag far behind EU norms, integrating them into primary care. Provide free medicines to vulnerable groups, low-income pensioners, and the unemployed. No one left behind or marginalized—this is a firm pledge from our democratic party. Enhance the social solidarity allowance, extend universal care to children, the elderly, the homeless, and single-parent families. Mainstream disability across all state policies, and ensure disability benefits keep pace with minimum wage hikes."

We all rejoiced in October 2020, when we stood at that historic rally outside the Court of Appeals and heard the court ruling that characterized them for what they really are: a Nazi criminal organization that has no place in the jail except in prison!But we have never nurtured and cultivated any illusions that we are done with Nazism or that we can ever be done with it for good as long as the exploitative system of capitalism that breeds and feeds them remains. From the moment the magnificent mobilizations of the people and youth over the crime in Tempe broke out, and without there being any such indication in reality, articles and reports began to rain down on the possibility of strengthening such forces, as an alleged result of the youth's anger, even baptizing them as anti-systemic!Then they gave them plenty of free pre-election TV advertising time, on the occasion of the regulation brought by the government at the last minute before the Parliament closed, and while we could not even discuss this issue if the trial that has been dragging on for 8 years now, with huge responsibilities of both the previous SYRIZA government and the current ND government, had been finalized.And now we are watching an election game of who will fish better in the dirty waters of the far right and fascism.
Either with the ND trying to hit parties that are cutting off their votes, or with SYRIZA taking them under its wing. rewrite:
Comrades, friends and allies.  
For more than a decade, here in western Athens—in schools, neighborhoods, and workplaces—we have struggled to push back fascist and Nazi factions. We take pride that in these areas, they have faced strong resistance from communists, trade unions, and local residents.  
We all celebrated in October 2020, when we gathered at that historic demonstration outside the Court of Appeals and heard the verdict exposing them for what they truly are: a Nazi criminal organization that belongs behind bars, not in our communities!  
Yet we have never harbored the illusion that Nazism is finished, or that it can ever be fully eradicated while the capitalist system of exploitation—which breeds and sustains such forces—remains in place. We urged constant vigilance then, and we repeat that call today. Indeed, it was not long before the convicted Nazis began walking out of prison one after another, with barely a consequence.  
We tell the people and the working class, with full responsibility, that we are deeply alarmed by the dangerous political games being played recently. Ever since the powerful public and youth mobilizations erupted over the Tempe tragedy, articles and reports have proliferated—without any factual basis—suggesting that far‑right forces could gain strength from the youth’s anger, even labeling them as “anti‑systemic”!  
Then they were handed generous free airtime during the pre‑election period, under a last‑minute regulation pushed through by the government just before Parliament adjourned—all while the trial, which has been delayed for eight years with major accountability on both the previous SYRIZA government and the current ND administration, remains unresolved.  
Now we are witnessing an electoral contest over who can fish more effectively in the murky waters of the far right and fascism.  
Whether it is ND targeting parties that are siphoning off its votes, or SYRIZA embracing them under its wing. Whether it is Mitsotakis staging campaign theatrics at the Evros fence to appeal to that audience, or Tsipras rubbing shoulders with far‑right figures—as he recently did in Menidi—while adopting the anti‑communist rhetoric of bourgeois commentators and Nazi‑style propaganda about the Soviet Union!

text: But the reality is inexorable. Under ND, SYRIZA and PASOK, the private sector is growing day by day and is getting bigger and bigger, and it is getting more and more gluttonous from human suffering, at a time when it has been amply demonstrated that health care should be a social good and a right for all, not a commodity and a privilege for those who can afford it. Changing the way 18 hospitals are financed, based on the ability to attract patient-customers and achieve financial efficiency, is a law of the ND-PASOK government that SYRIZA put into effect. The recent law concerning the reform of EOPYY and Primary Health Care with the fiasco of the personal doctor is an extension of the unpopular reform enacted by SYRIZA in 2017.
